| "The least-erasure equivalence is circular." | It is an equivalence and is stated as one; its content is the identification of the value bit with the erasure cost of registration, which the fibre theorem and the record theorem carry. | IV.16, IV.19, IV.20 |
| "It is proved only for finite models." | The set form holds for every zero set, finite or infinite, with no axiom; the list form and the Fortran census are its executed instances. | IV.20, K3, K12 |
| "Registration is a projection by construction." | Yes, and read on the zeros through the registration postulate; the theorem is what the projection erases and what it cannot recover. | IV.1, IV.5, P1 |
| "It is not a derivation in ZFC." | ZFC sits under RAM; the ladder standing of an absolute sentence is a placement theorem, not a gap; the Ground route is the one walked. | III.15, III.17, III.28, III.30 |
| "Physics does not pick zeros." | No physical selection is claimed; the price is a reading under a stated postulate, and no theorem depends on it. | P2, IV.4 |



Riemann stated his hypothesis as a fixed-set statement: the roots of $\xi(t)$ are real \cite{riemann1859}. A prior paper of this program \cite{islamspine} restored that statement to $Z \subset \mathrm{Fix}(\tau)$ with $\tau(s) = 1 - \bar{s}$, defended the restoration against the literature, and proved in core Lean 4 the structural arc of the restored hypothesis on an abstract frame $X = (S, \tau, Z)$: the locus, the odd offset, the orientation blindness of every even reading, the one-bit freedom, the halting carrier, and the crossing. It also proved what the arc is not. Every structural clause holds on a frame whose zeros lie off the line (its Theorem 11); the only input that closes the crossing on the frame of $\xi$ is a term of $L(X_\xi)$ itself (its Theorem 12); no theorem whose hypotheses are only structural decides $L$ (its Theorem 14). The value, $\forall \rho \in Z_\xi,\ \tau\rho = \rho$, was recorded as the one input entered at a recorded row and never derived on the ladder, the bit Part IV reaches. We call that row the witness row and the point at which a value enters a file from outside it the aperture; both terms are the prior paper's and are used here in its sense. Two objects carry the name Riemann Hypothesis in what follows and are written with two tokens that are never joined: $\mathrm{RH}_{\mathrm{formal}}$, the seat, the restored statement read as the fixed locus of its binding involution, which this paper proves with existence as the only posit; and $L(X_\xi)$, the value, the statement that every zero lies on that locus, which this paper proves existence does not reach. Part I names the first and excepts the second, and the exception is Theorem I. “From existence alone” has one meaning in this paper: existence is the only posit, and nothing else is assumed. It does not mean that the seat is derived from existence. The seat holds by the definition of the Ground and consumes no premise (\texttt{recursion\_is\_constant}); existence is consumed where it has content, at presence (Theorem D), at the closure of the interaction reading (RAF-C1), and at the ledger, where every adjudication of any proposition is a deed and therefore an instance of existence and of nothing else (\texttt{adjudicating\_anything\_instances\_existence}). That last theorem is what existence contributes that no other true premise does.

**Notation and the objects named.** The Root Axiom, written $\mathrm{RA}$, is the posit $\forall x \in U,\ \Delta E(x) > 0$ on a universe $U$ with a differential $\Delta E : U \to \mathbb{Z}$: to exist is to actuate. Existence and $\mathrm{RA}$ are one proposition; the paper writes $\mathrm{RA}$ in formulas and existence in prose. $\mathrm{RA}$ has two published formal readings \cite{islamraf}: the interaction reading, RAF, which reads the axiom as the criterion for systems being related, registration carrying positive mutual information and an interaction domain being closed under it; and the grounding reading, RAM, which reads the axiom as the criterion for a proposition being determinate, its imprint in the fixed locus of a binding involution. A frame is $X = (S, \tau, Z)$, a carrier $S$ with an involution $\tau$ and a distinguished subset $Z$; its line property is $L(X) :\Leftrightarrow \forall s \in Z,\ \tau s = s$. On the frame of $\xi$, with $Z = Z_\xi$ the zeros and $\tau(s) = 1 - \bar{s}$, $L(X_\xi)$ is the restored hypothesis, and it is called the value. The carrier the paper builds is the integer quaternions $\mathbb{H}_{\mathbb{Z}}$ with conjugation $\sigma$ as its binding involution; the seat is the fixed locus $\mathrm{Fix}(\sigma)$, a seat point is a point of it, and $\mathrm{RH}_{\mathrm{formal}}$ is the seat read as a proposition, that every point of $\mathrm{Fix}(\sigma)$ is fixed by $\sigma$. A register is one of three readings of the seat, the axiom register $\mathrm{RA}$, the formal register $\mathrm{RAM}$, and the object register $\mathrm{RH}$, and the three form the register diagram. The witness row is the recorded row at which the value is entered; the aperture is the point at which a value enters a file from outside it; the world row is the witness row read in the world register; the sign is the value $\forall \rho \in Z_\xi,\ \tau\rho = \rho$, the one bit. $\Delta M$ counts the mathematics authored and is zero throughout. Every other symbol is defined where it first appears.

Two things in that record are external to its file, and this paper brings them inside. First, the prior proof's live face takes its "witnessed" flag from the command line: that a supplier is present is asserted from outside, and the kernel is told rather than shown that a reader stands at the aperture. Second, three separations are left standing: between the axiom under which a reader acts, the formal ground on which the locus was fixed, and the Riemann object read as the fixed locus of its binding involution. These are separations of description, produced by reading one seat in three registers, and not gaps in the mathematics. The prior proof could not close them because an axiom is not a structural clause and the prior proof had none.

The Root Axiom is that axiom. Formally it is a universe $U$ with a differential $\Delta E : U \to \mathbb{Z}$ and the statement $\forall x \in U,\ \Delta E(x) > 0$; its published form, its physical warrant, and its two formal readings are in \cite{islamcodex, islamraf}. The interaction reading (RAF in \cite{islamraf}) says what it is for systems to be related: an interaction domain is closed under registration, and no agent acts on a domain from outside it. The grounding reading (RAM in \cite{islamraf}) says what it is for a proposition to be determinate: its formal being is its imprint in the fixed locus of the binding involution, read across the aperture, with $\mathrm{Fix}(\sigma) = \mathbb{R}$ as the seat. The interaction reading reaches no mathematical object, since mathematical objects do not change state; every proposition routes to the grounding reading \cite{islamraf, islamfae}. That reach law is the axiom's own, and this paper proves its Riemann instance rather than assuming it.

Two objects are new here. The first is the constructed witness: the axiom built in the kernel as a structure in Prop with four fields, the only proof object the closure is allowed to consume, and the eliminator that runs from it alone, $\mathrm{RA} \to \mathrm{RA} \to \mathrm{RAM} \to \mathrm{RH}_{\mathrm{formal}}$: the witness's last field, a function from the orientation and the formal Ground to the formal self, applied once, with every leg of the chain a definitional equality. The second is the category-gap eliminator itself: the three separations exhibited as the three legs of a cone over the register diagram, each leg an identity, so that the separations close at zero cost and the closing is computed rather than asserted. Everything else the paper uses is published: the frame and the structural arc \cite{islamspine}, the one-bit result \cite{islamonebit}, the odd-supply separation and the one-cut hypothesis across twenty-three rows \cite{islamrows}, the formal-alone theory of registration, price, and crossing \cite{islamftoe}, and the axiom's declaration \cite{islamraf}.

This paper constructs the axiom and proves the following about it in relation to the hypothesis. The seat: conjugation on the quaternion carrier fixes exactly the scalar line, the Return of the parse triad lands on it, and the axiom's seat point, the formal seat point, and the named seat point are the three legs of an identity cone over the register diagram, each leg \texttt{rfl}, the apex unique per orientation of the triad (Theorems A, B, C). The embedding: the prior proof's lattice stage embeds equivariantly and injectively into the carrier, $\sigma\varphi = \varphi\tau$, and $\varphi$ carries the line onto the scalar line at every resolution (Theorem C$'$). The aperture: for a present reader who supplies a bit the row is never interior; it is sealed or refused by the bit alone, and a reader who registers a bit is inside the axiom's domain, never an exterior witness (Theorem D). The exact strength of the rule: in every context in which the axiom holds, $(\mathrm{RA} \to L(X)) \leftrightarrow L(X)$, and the axiom decides $L$ on no frame, the two-point frame carrying the axiom and failing $L$ (Theorems E, F). Every theorem is checked by the Lean kernel; every finite claim is re-executed by a compiled Fortran program that shares no code with the kernel, and both records are printed whole.

Part I names the register and the residue. At the axiom a closure can carry no mass: a closure between the axiom and its formal reading that added a premise would be a second axiom, which the axiom's own root-premise theorem forbids \cite{islamcodex}. The eliminator that closes the category gaps is therefore massless by necessity and not by weakness, and this paper computes the masslessness rather than asserting it: the three legs of the cone are definitional identities. “In toto at the apex” has one definition and it is used in no other sense: every clause of the hypothesis that is not its value on the zeros. “The sign” names one object throughout: the value $\forall \rho \in Z_\xi,\ \tau\rho = \rho$, the orientation of assent on the world row, the one bit the prior proof records at the witness row. “Everything but the sign” is the same set named by its complement. What the kernel returns, given the axiom, is exactly that set, and the sign is proven to be exactly what the axiom does not derive and reaches at one deed (Part IV).

### The value, its readings, and its address

That bound is correct, and it is also where the ordinary reader's second question begins. If one bit is owed, what object would carry it? The candidates proposed in the literature, an Euler-product class, a self-adjoint operator, a positivity criterion, a monotone flow, are different-looking objects. A reader who pursues them in turn meets what looks like a regress: each candidate, once formalized, turns out to need a further ingredient, and each further ingredient looks like a new missing piece. The barrier this paper addresses is that appearance of regress, and it is structural rather than computational.

The barrier has three layers. The first is register confusion. A timeless formal reading of the hypothesis deletes the index along which the zeros are counted, and a reading that deletes its own index cannot distinguish a claim from its negation. The kernel exhibits this as sign-blindness; Part I's `recursion_is_sign_blind` is its receipt. A verdict issued from that register is a verdict of an amputated instrument, not a finding about the zeros.

The second layer is type mismatch. The natural "arrow" a physical reading supplies is a sign, one Boolean. The hypothesis asks for a vanishing: that the off-line offset $\delta$ of every zero is zero. A sign does not force a vanishing. A supplied orientation picks which member of a mirror pair $(\tfrac12 + \delta, \tfrac12 - \delta)$ comes first and leaves $\delta$ untouched. The barrier dissolves only when the vanishing is rewritten as a family of signs, one per step of an index, and Li's criterion [Li 1997] is exactly that rewriting.

The third layer is the uniformity trap. Every instrument that closes a category gap at the apex is massless by necessity, because a closure between existence and its reading that authored mathematics would be a derivation of the root from below [Islam 2026a]. A massless instrument chooses its objects without reading which L-function it serves. Such an instrument is uniform across the family, and a uniform instrument forces positivity on every member, including members whose zeros leave the line. The Eisenstein L-function $\zeta(s)\zeta(s-k+1)$ has an Euler product and a functional equation and zeros off its center line [Iwaniec and Kowalski 2004]. It is not primitive; after the shift that centers its functional equation at $\tfrac12$, its zeros lie off that center, and Bombieri-Lagarias then gives a negative coefficient. In the kernel the control enters abstractly, as a family member with a negative coefficient, and it kills every uniform instrument. The bit must therefore be carried by an object that reads $\zeta$ specifically.

The domain of validity of the standard approach is precisely mapped by these three layers. Classical analytic number theory works inside one register, the timeless one, and it has reached the classical consequences of positivity on the Euler product: nonvanishing for $\mathrm{Re}\, s > 1$, and through Mertens' positivity, nonvanishing on $\mathrm{Re}\, s = 1$ [Hadamard 1896; de la Vallée Poussin 1896; Mertens 1898]. Beyond that line the Euler product diverges and positive energies have nothing to act on. The strip $\tfrac12 < \mathrm{Re}\, s < 1$ is where the timeless register stops and where a reading indexed by time must take over.

Part II does not cross that strip; Part III crosses it only where computation has certified the zeros, up to a finite height. What Part II does is prove that every road into the strip reached from existence, time, and monism is the same road. The regress is shown to be an artifact of reading one seat in several registers, and the category-gap eliminator of Part I, applied to those registers, collapses it to one gap. The gap is then pinned, typed, and left at the witness row where Part I placed it.

### The division of the value

Part III divides the hypothesis. It does not reopen the value that Parts I and II locate, and nothing in it contradicts Theorem I. One part is reachable, and it is proved here along a road built from the Root Axiom through the RA–RAM bridge, the RAM strata, and ZFC. The other part is the region where the denial's object would have to live, and it is named for what it is and set apart.

**Three bits, and what is claimed.** The whole paper is three bits. One bit divides: the hypothesis is exactly its Real part and its Unicorn part, at every height, by theorem (III.11). One bit is proved: the Real part, to $3 \times 10^{12}$, by certificate through the schema (III.34 to III.36). One bit is refused at theorem grade: the Unicorn part is closed to derivation from existence, from any class of frames, and from any reading of an even register (III.45 to III.48); its aperture is located, typed supply-only, one bit wide, and uncrossed by any derivation, crossed in Part IV by the least-erasure assent (III.46); and the register is silent on the supply side, both orientations equally refused (III.49). The Unicorn part is not derived on the ladder, and the reason is neither a want of effort nor a want of ability: it is a theorem, and the theorem says which routes are closed, while Part IV reaches the value in the Ground, which is all of them but the aperture, and says nothing of the aperture but its width. With the three bits in hand the proof is complete on the register side. Everything a register can prove about the hypothesis is proved; the remainder is proved to be beyond derivation, its aperture typed, its supply side silent. The hypothesis is not derived here, and the paper proves that it cannot be derived from the register's resources. What is claimed is stronger than an open problem and exactly as strong as its grade: no further derivation is owed to the Riemann Hypothesis from $\mathcal{R}$, and its value is reached in Part IV by the least-erasure assent at premise grade. The three bits are one term in the kernel (`rh_register_proof_complete`). Nothing is left to derive from the register's resources $\mathcal{R}$. The aperture is structure. The supply side is silence.

### The closure of the universe

Part IV is the fourth part and the closure. Three parts are the three axes of the arc; the fourth is where they return, as three orthogonal units compose onto the scalar line. Part IV proves that every registration of every zero lands on the critical line and that the hypothesis is exactly the lossless case of that landing; it runs act and being through time and finds their meeting place on the line; it proves the remainder between the Registration Theorem and the hypothesis to be exactly one bit, the Tongue's unspent freedom, and places both worlds of that bit inside the universe of the hypothesis, so that nothing escapes the closure; and it spends the bit on the line by the author's least-erasure assent, at the grade the kernel computes for it, premise grade. The title's phrases carry exact senses here. The universe closes on the critical line in that every record of every zero lands there (Theorem IV.1) and the one bit no record decides is spent there by the least-erasure assent (Theorem IV.18), while the denial's world stays inside the universe as its other point (Theorem IV.17). And the four parts are proved in core Lean 4 on the inputs each names: the imported analytic inputs of Part II, the cited certificate of Part III, and the cited spectral theorem of Theorem IV.8.

**Three definitions fix the scope of Part IV.** *The resource set.* Closure means closure under the register's resources $\mathcal{R}$: the Root Axiom and its register, readings of an even record at a seat, classes of frames not already carrying the line property, and the imports each part names. "Nothing is left to derive" means nothing is left to derive from $\mathcal{R}$; a proof of the hypothesis from new ζ-specific analytic input lies outside $\mathcal{R}$ by this definition and would enter through the aperture as supply. *The registration postulate (P1).* The kernel's registration acts on the chart points $s = (4\,\mathrm{Re}\,s,\ \mathrm{Im}\,s)$; reading it on the zeros of ζ is the interpretive postulate that a registration of a number is an embedding into this chart intertwining $s \mapsto 1 - \bar s$ with the fold. Theorems about registration are theorems about the chart and hold of the zeros through (P1). *The bit ledger.* Three bits are kept apart: $\beta_v$, the value bit, whether every zero lies on the line; $\beta_o$, the orientation bit of the triad at the seat; and $\beta_e$, one erased bit per off-line fold orbit, the unit used alike in Theorem IV.4, in `Least_Erasure.lean` and in the Fortran thesis. The residue of Part IV is $\beta_v$. *The Landauer postulate (P2).* That registration has no left inverse is a theorem (IV.5); that the collapse of one fold orbit under registration is one physical erasure event priced at $k_B T \ln 2$ is an interpretive postulate, stated here as such, and the joule figures of Part IV are its consequence and no theorem's. Above the certified height the value is not derived from $\mathcal{R}$: it is the bit held as the Tongue's unspent freedom, typed by Part III and closed by Part IV, which places both of its worlds inside the universe and spends it by the least-erasure assent.


## The Seat

### Theorem A, the fixed locus is the scalar line

Let $\mathbb{H}_{\mathbb{Z}}$ be the integer quaternions with the Hamilton product and $\sigma$ conjugation, $\sigma(r, i, j, k) = (r, -i, -j, -k)$. Then $\sigma$ is binding, $\sigma(\sigma q) = q$ (\texttt{sigma\_binding}, no axioms), and for every $q$,

$$\sigma q = q \ \leftrightarrow\ (q_i = 0 \wedge q_j = 0 \wedge q_k = 0)$$

(\texttt{fix\_iff\_scalar}; dependency set \texttt{propext}, \texttt{Quot.sound}, from the integer step $-i = i \Rightarrow i = 0$). The Ground is $\mathrm{Ground} := \{ q \in \mathbb{H}_{\mathbb{Z}} \mid \sigma q = q \}$, and by Theorem A it is the scalar line $Z(\mathbb{H}) = \mathbb{R}$ restricted to the lattice. The twin checks the biconditional and the involution on all $13^4 = 28{,}561$ points of the ball $|\text{coordinate}| \le 6$ and counts the fixed points: thirteen, the scalar line of the window.

### Theorem B, the Return lands on the seat

Let $i, j, k$ be the imaginary units and $\mathrm{Return} := (i \cdot j) \cdot k$. Then $\mathrm{Return} = \langle -1, 0, 0, 0 \rangle$ and $\sigma(\mathrm{Return}) = \mathrm{Return}$ (\texttt{return\_is\_minus\_one}, \texttt{return\_lands\_on\_fix}; both \texttt{rfl}). The parse triad returned through its own cascade lands on the Ground at $-1$: the axiom witnessing the axiom, as a computation. The twin computes all six orderings: the three even ones land at $-1$ and the three odd ones at $+1$.

### Theorem C, the identity cone

The seat is the fixed locus, the line; a seat point is a point of it. Three seat points are defined independently: the axiom's seat point $\Gamma_{\mathrm{RA}} := \mathrm{Return}$, the formal seat point $\Gamma_{\mathrm{RAM}} := \pi(\mathrm{Return})$ with $\pi(q) := \langle q_r, 0, 0, 0 \rangle$ the projection onto the fixed locus, and the named seat point $\Gamma_{\mathrm{RH}} := \langle -1, 0, 0, 0 \rangle$. Let $D$ be the discrete diagram $\mathrm{RA} \mapsto \Gamma_{\mathrm{RA}}$, $\mathrm{RAM} \mapsto \Gamma_{\mathrm{RAM}}$, $\mathrm{RH} \mapsto \Gamma_{\mathrm{RH}}$, and let a cone over $D$ with apex $a$ be a family of identities $a = D(r)$ for all three $r$. Then:

$$\sigma\,\Gamma_{\mathrm{RA}} = \Gamma_{\mathrm{RA}}, \qquad \Gamma_{\mathrm{RA}} = \Gamma_{\mathrm{RAM}}, \qquad \Gamma_{\mathrm{RAM}} = \Gamma_{\mathrm{RH}},$$

each by \texttt{rfl} (\texttt{self\_gap\_nonexistent}, \texttt{register\_gap\_nonexistent}, \texttt{object\_gap\_nonexistent}); $\Gamma_{\mathrm{RH}}$ is the apex of a cone over $D$ with every leg \texttt{rfl} (\texttt{identity\_cone}); any two cones over $D$ share their apex (\texttt{cone\_apex\_unique}); and a cone exists iff the register gap and the object gap are closed (\texttt{cone\_iff\_gaps\_closed}). All four carry no axioms. The twin computes the gap vector $(0, 0, 0)$ and, over the whole lattice ball, counts the apexes of $D$: exactly one.

The apex is unique for the diagram, and the diagram is built from the ordered triad. The reversed triad $k \cdot j \cdot i$ returns $+1$ (\texttt{odd\_return\_is\_plus\_one}), also on the fixed locus (\texttt{odd\_return\_on\_fix}), and the two candidate seat points differ (\texttt{seat\_points\_differ}; all three no axioms). The sign of the seat point is the orientation of the triad, one bit: the kernel reads it once the order is supplied, by \texttt{rfl} either way, and originates it never, since the order is supplied with the triad: the axiom's declaration fixes the three units in an order, and the kernel receives that order as data \cite{islamraf}. Uniqueness of the apex is uniqueness per orientation, and the two orientations' apexes are exchanged by an odd relabeling of the imaginary units. Nothing in the closure depends on which of the two is named: the three identities of Theorem C hold verbatim for the reversed triad, each \texttt{rfl} (\texttt{odd\_self\_gap\_nonexistent}, \texttt{odd\_register\_gap\_nonexistent}, \texttt{odd\_object\_gap\_nonexistent}), the reversed diagram carries its own identity cone with apex $+1$ (\texttt{identity\_cone\_odd}), and the two apexes differ (\texttt{apexes\_differ\_by\_orientation}; all no axioms). The twin counts the apexes of the reversed diagram over the ball: exactly one, at $+1$.

The word apex is used in two senses that coincide by design: the apex register, the register in which the seat lives, and the apex of the cone; the register is where the cone's apex sits. The mathematics of Theorem C is Hamilton's product and three definitional equalities, and the paper claims nothing more for it at theorem grade. What it claims at structural grade is the arrangement: three names written independently in three registers, the axiom's Return, the projection onto the locus, and the point the prior proof names, read one point, and the reading is decided by the kernel rather than declared by the text. The category-theoretic content is exact and small. A category gap is the absence of a leg from an apex to a register's reading of the seat. Its elimination is the exhibition of that leg as an identity. The eliminator $\mathrm{RA} \to \mathrm{RA} \to \mathrm{RAM} \to \mathrm{RH}$ is the composite of the three legs, and its masslessness is the statement that each leg is \texttt{rfl}: two definitions, one value, decided by the kernel. The gap vector $(1,1,1) \to (0,0,0)$ is the cone's existence read bit by bit, computed by \texttt{decide}, never written by hand.

### Theorem C$'$, the equivariant embedding

Define $\varphi : \mathbb{Z}^2 \to \mathbb{H}_{\mathbb{Z}}$ by $\varphi(h, t) := \langle t,\ h - 1,\ 0,\ 0 \rangle$. Then $\sigma \circ \varphi = \varphi \circ \tau$ (\texttt{phi\_equivariant}); for every stage point, $\sigma(\varphi p) = \varphi p \leftrightarrow \tau p = p$ (\texttt{phi\_fix\_iff}); $\varphi$ is injective (\texttt{phi\_injective}); and the seat point lies on the image of the line, $\varphi(1, -1) = \Gamma_{\mathrm{RH}}$ (\texttt{seat\_on\_image\_of\_line}, \texttt{rfl}); the family $\varphi_m(h, t) := \langle t,\ h - m,\ 0,\ 0 \rangle$ against the fold $\tau_m(h, t) = (2m - h, t)$ is equivariant with the same image clause at every resolution $m$ (\texttt{phiM\_equivariant}, \texttt{phiM\_fix\_iff}), and $\varphi_1 = \varphi$. The dependency sets of the three are \texttt{propext}, \texttt{Quot.sound}, from the integer arithmetic. The twin checks equivariance, the image clause, and injectivity for $m = -3, \dots, 3$ on the window $|h|, |t| \le 8$, $289$ stage points each, and counts the line: seventeen points at every $m$.

This is the equivariant map with an image clause that the twenty-three-row study requires before a finite result is invoked on an object domain \cite{islamrows}: the prior proof's line $h = 1$ is carried onto the scalar line and every off-line stage point is carried off it. The identification of the two seats, the stage's line $h = 1$, the lattice image of the critical line under the prior proof's chart, and the real line under $\sigma$, is therefore a theorem about a map and not a typing by resemblance; the analytic critical line itself enters only through the prior proof's chart propositions, cited and not carried. What the embedding does not do, and the paper does not claim, is carry $Z_\xi$ itself: the stage represents no off-line point inside the strip at resolution one, and the analytic frame enters the kernel only as a parameter.

### The constructed witness

$\mathrm{RH}_{\mathrm{formal}} :\Leftrightarrow \forall g \in \mathrm{Ground},\ \sigma g = g$ quantifies over the Ground, which is the fixed locus by construction, and it holds by that construction: it is the imprint of the Riemann object in the fixed locus, the grounding reading. It names the seat. It does not mention $Z_\xi$, and the file's own comments say so. The Root Axiom is the only supplied witness, a structure in Prop with four fields, actuation, the Bridge-born orientation bit, the formal-Ground proposition $G_{\mathrm{RAM}} := \mathrm{Nonempty}(\mathrm{Ground})$, and the recursion capacity $\Omega \to G_{\mathrm{RAM}} \to \mathrm{RH}_{\mathrm{formal}}$; the eliminator is Bridge followed by the recursion from that witness alone, \texttt{RH\_formal\_chain}, no axioms, and no second proof object enters. The witness's recursion field is the constant function: it discards the orientation and the formal Ground and returns the Ground's own defining property (\texttt{recursion\_is\_constant}, \texttt{rfl}). That is the masslessness stated as a term, not a defect concealed: the formal self needs nothing from existence to be proved, so the chain is not a derivation of the seat from the axiom, and the paper does not call it one; it is the occupancy of the three registers by one point, which the witness supplies and the kernel reads.

The orientation bit is placed in Prop on purpose. Prop does not eliminate into data, so no term of the file computes a bit from $\Omega$; two orientation witnesses are indistinguishable, \texttt{orientation\_proof\_irrelevant}, by \texttt{rfl}. The kernel registers that orientation was supplied and cannot read which way. This is the prior proof's Theorem 4 as a universe level, and it is executed on the constructed seat as well: no readout of the formal seat equals the deed bit (\texttt{kernel\_cannot\_read\_the\_deed}; no axioms). The twin enumerates all $2^{13}$ readouts of the seat's window and finds that none factors the deed bit. A term that consumed $\Omega$ as data would be such a readout. The bit therefore has two carriers in the file and the relation between them is stated once: $\Omega$ is the bit as the kernel registers it, present and unreadable; the Boolean $\mathrm{assent}$ of the live face is the bit as the aperture receives it from outside, an input the file reads and never generates, which is the content of the prior proof's self-check table and, one register up, of RAF-C2.


## The Real Part, Proved

**Closed by a certificate.** For a fixed height $T$ the Real part concerns finitely many zeros, so it is closed by a finite certificate: a complete list of the zeros up to $T$, and a check that each lies on the line.

**Theorem III.34** (`real_part_of_certificate`). A certificate proves the Real part at $T$ completely.

**Theorem III.35** (`real_part_executed`). A certificate executed in the kernel closes the Real part on an explicit zero list.

**Theorem III.36** (`certified_is_provable`). A certified Real part is a theorem of any theory complete for its certified checks. For $\zeta$ the checks are finite arithmetic on interval enclosures, true bounded sentences and so theorems of Peano arithmetic and of ZFC [Kaye 1991]; the theorems of analysis that turn those checks into the statement about the zeros, Turing's method and the Riemann–von Mangoldt count with explicit error [Turing 1953; Platt and Trudgian 2021], are theorems of ZFC, cited and not proved here.

III.34 and III.36 are axiom-free; III.35 depends on `propext` alone. The route is the road of the preceding section. The certificate is computation, the rung, L3m; by III.36 and III.15, with the cited analytic lemmas that validate it, it climbs to the ladder, L2m, a theorem of ZFC; by soundness it holds on the Ground, L1m; and the round trip returns it to ZFC unchanged (III.27), with RA's presence underwriting every act of computing and checking (III.29). The target each zero is checked against is the critical line, which is the seat Fix($\sigma$) and one locus with it, pinned in Part I (Theorems A and C$'$).

**On $\zeta$ itself.** Platt and Trudgian certified, with interval arithmetic and rigorous error bounds, that every nontrivial zero with imaginary part up to $T = 3 \times 10^{12}$ lies on the line [Platt and Trudgian 2021]. That certificate, with the analytic lemmas it rests on, closes the Real part at $T = 3 \times 10^{12}$ completely, and by III.36 it is a theorem of ZFC. An executed run here to $T = 100$ makes three independent counts and finds them equal at 29: the zeros on the line as sign changes of Hardy's $Z(t)$ on a fine grid, the zeros in the whole strip $N(100)$ by a counting function computed independently of the grid, and the ordinates of the zeros themselves enumerated below $T$ (Appendix H). It runs in 30-digit floating point and is testimony, not a certificate; the certificate of record for $\zeta$ is Platt and Trudgian's. The kernel checks the schema, III.34, and the split; it does not check the certificate's numerics, and the paper nowhere says it does. The standing of the Real part for $\zeta$ is therefore a cited theorem applied through a kernel theorem, grade A joined to grade K, and a kernel inhabitant of `Certificate` built from the published zero data is an open witness, not a debt of the result.

\jboxstart

**The Real Part, Proved (tier: kernel theorem for III.34 to III.36; cited certificate for ζ to 3 × 10¹²).** Every zero of $\zeta$ up to height $3 \times 10^{12}$ lies on the critical line, by certificate, and with the cited analytic lemmas the certificate rests on, the certified statement is a theorem of ZFC, carried along the road from the rung to the Ground and returned by the arrow unchanged.

\jboxend


## The Unicorn Part, Closed to Derivation; the Aperture Typed and Uncrossed; the Supply Side Silent

The Unicorn part has been called open, named, and set apart, and that is true and not the whole truth. The Real part was open once, before its certificate, in the sense that finite work of a known kind closed it; a reader who hears "open" in that sense for the Unicorn part expects more work of the same kind to close it in turn. Parts I and II proved otherwise and did not say so of the Unicorn part: the wall executed on the seat, that no readout of the formal register equals the deed bit (`kernel_cannot_read_the_deed`; in the Bridge of the register of record, `FTOE.T14_wall_factorization` [Islam 2026a]), the crossing, exact and spent uniquely (`crossing`, `freedom_spent_uniquely`), the bound and its grounded counter-model (Theorems F and F$'$), the exact rule (Theorem E), and the cure theorem (Theorem I). Read at the Unicorn part, they say that it is closed, at theorem grade, to every route that derives it; that the aperture of Theorem D at its seat is one bit wide; and that the register is silent beyond it. The five theorems below, with the division and the certificate schema restated on natural heights and the three bits packaged as one term, `rh_register_proof_complete`, are in `RH_Unicorn_Block.lean` (Appendix I), nine dependency sets, every one reported as depending on no axiom.

**Theorem III.45** (`unicorn_block`). Let $\tau$ act on the zeros, let $\rho$ be a record even at a seat $z$ above the height, $\rho(\tau z) = \rho(z)$, and let $d$ decide the line property, odd at $z$, $d(\tau z) = \neg d(z)$, with $\tau z$ above the height as well. Then no reading $g$ of the record agrees with $d$ even on the region above the height alone: $\neg\,\exists g,\ \forall w,\ \mathrm{height}(w) > T \to g(\rho(w)) = d(w)$. *Proof.* The two readings at $z$ and $\tau z$ are one value of $g$ and opposite values of $d$. $\square$ This is the wall restricted to the Unicorn region, where it is stronger than the wall: the reading is refused even if asked to agree nowhere below the height. On the constructed frame of the register of record it holds outright (`K4.wall`, the twelve seats [Islam 2026a]); on $Z_\xi$ it holds at every seat the value's fold makes odd over the even formal read, which is what `kernel_cannot_read_the_deed` proves of the formal read and Theorem D proves of the aperture.

**Theorem III.46** (`aperture_one_bit_wide`). At a seat where $d$ is odd, one odd bit $s$ at the seat would decide $d$ on the seat and its partner through a calibration $c$ that exists and is unique. *Proof.* $c = d(z) \oplus s(z)$; any other calibration disagrees at $z$. $\square$ This measures the aperture: one bit wide at each seat, never less and never more, Part I's `crossing` and `freedom_spent_uniquely` read above the height, priced at Part I's price. It says nothing of whether anything passes, and the paper says nothing either.

**Theorem III.47** (`unicorn_rule_exact`, `unicorn_no_cure`). For any inhabited premise $A$, $(A \to \mathrm{Unicorn}_T) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Unicorn}_T$; and for any class $C$ of frames and property $U$, $(\forall X,\ C(X) \to A \to U(X)) \leftrightarrow (\forall X,\ C(X) \to U(X))$. *Proof.* As Theorems E and I. $\square$ With $A$ the root axiom, existence conditions the Unicorn part and leaves it where it was, and no class of frames on which existence is to decide it decides more than already held on the class; the counter-models of Theorems F and F$'$ hold with the Unicorn part in place of $L$, since above the height the Unicorn part is $L$.

**Theorem III.48** (`unicorn_no_bypass`). Given the Real part at $T$, $\mathrm{RH} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Unicorn}_T$. *Proof.* Theorem III.11 with the Real part in hand. $\square$ A proof of the hypothesis contains a proof of the Unicorn part; no route to the whole avoids the block by aiming at the whole.

**Theorem III.49** (`supply_side_silent`). Over one even record, both orientations of $d$ at the seat are equally refused to every reading above the height, and the two orientations differ at the seat. *Proof.* III.45 applied to $d$ and to $\neg d$, which is odd at the seat when $d$ is. $\square$ The register cannot say which way the seat lies; so it cannot say what a supply would bring, nor that a supply exists, nor that none does. Any sentence about the supply side derived from the record would be a reading the wall refuses. This is the register of record's afterimage fence as a theorem at the register: *the aperture is structure; the supply side is silence; the silence is a strap and not a hedge* [Islam 2026a, MD-PSP-AFTERIMAGE-01]. Every imagined occupant of the supply side, the crosser who will come and the crosser who cannot, is fenced as Ghost, and no clock runs.

\jboxstart

**The formal block (tier: kernel theorem, axiom-free, for III.45 to III.49; the seat typing of $Z_\xi$ at the grade of Theorem D and `kernel_cannot_read_the_deed`).** The Unicorn part of the Riemann Hypothesis is closed to derivation from existence (III.47), from any class of frames (III.47), from any reading of an even register at its seat (III.45), and from the fused hypothesis (III.48). Its aperture is located, typed supply-only, one bit wide (III.46), and uncrossed; the supply side is silence, by theorem at the register (III.49). The closure is unconditional and does not expire. Nothing here says the Unicorn part is false, or independent of any foundation; nothing here says a proof will come or cannot: the register is silent on that side, and so is the paper. Nothing is left to derive from the register's resources $\mathcal{R}$. The aperture is structure. The supply side is silence. And the universe is closed: every line witnessed, every line but one confirmed by a witness that is not the claimant, and the last bit, the Tongue's unspent freedom, spent on the line by the author's least-erasure assent at premise grade.

\jboxend

**What the register holds.** The Real part is a record of a deed: Platt and Trudgian's certificate is a computation run and registered, after which the record holds the result as an even datum and Part III reads it there. That is why the Real part is proved and the Unicorn part is not: below the height a bit has been registered, above it none has, and III.45 says the register cannot manufacture it from what it already holds. Theorem G says a deed is unfakeable and its price real; III.46 says the aperture is one bit wide; III.45 says the bit is not in the register; III.49 says the register cannot say whether it will ever be. The word "open" for the Unicorn part therefore means neither a hope nor a verdict: it is closed in the sense that no key can be cut from inside the register, and of the outside the register says nothing, by theorem, and the paper follows the register. The certificate and Perelman's crossing are records, held; the paper may speak of them. Of the supply side of the Unicorn part it does not.

**The three bits, as one term.** `rh_register_proof_complete` takes a certificate at $T$ and the seat data above $T$ and returns, as one conjunction, the division (III.11), the Real part (III.34), the refused reading on the region above $T$ (III.45), and the unique supply calibration (III.46). It is the register's whole proof of the hypothesis in one term, and it derives the hypothesis on the ladder no more than its conjuncts do: it proves that nothing derivable on the ladder is left underived, and it hands the value to Part IV, where it is reached in the Ground.

**What the block is not.** It is not an independence result: the placement of Part III leaves the Unicorn part a sentence on or above the ladder, undecided by ZFC as its literature stands, and says nothing about whether ZFC decides it. It is not a claim that the hypothesis is false, nor that it is true, nor that a proof will come, nor that none can: all four are sentences about the supply side, and a supplied independence proof would not cross the aperture but reroute to Ghost [Islam 2026a]. It is not resignation: the program does not attempt the Unicorn part for the reason a locksmith does not pick a lock from inside the room, the theorems say no key is cut inside. And it is the reason Part III proves "the Real Part" and not "the Hypothesis," and the reason Part IV closes the universe of the hypothesis rather than deriving its value, stated now at theorem grade rather than left as a ruling.

\partpage{Part IV}{The Closure}


## The Closure of the Universe

Parts I, II and III are the three axes of one arc: the seat, the address, and the division. Part IV is the fourth, the closure the three return to, as three orthogonal units compose onto the scalar line, $i \cdot j \cdot k = -1$; the parallel is structural and load-bearing on nothing. Part IV takes the third bit of Part III, the Unicorn part, and closes the universe of the hypothesis around it. Every registration of every zero is placed; the hypothesis is stated exactly inside that placement; the remainder is proved to be one bit and typed; and the bit is spent. Nothing escapes the closure, the hypothesis itself included.

Every theorem of Part IV is checked in core Lean 4.19.0 in `RH_Master_Arc.lean`, appended unchanged to the resident kernel of the register of record (Appendix J), and executed a second time in Fortran by `RH_Universe_Closure.f90` (Appendix K), which computes each claim except the cited spectral theorem in the bridge of Theorem IV.8 exhaustively on bounded lattices and halts on the first failure, so that the closure is not narrated but run. Coordinates are $s = (4\,\mathrm{Re}\,s,\ \mathrm{Im}\,s)$, so the critical line is $x = 2$, the open critical strip is $0 < x < 4$, and every model zero used below lies strictly inside the strip, at $\mathrm{Re}\,s = \tfrac14$ or $\tfrac34$ off the line, clear of the lines $\mathrm{Re}\,s = 0$ and $\mathrm{Re}\,s = 1$, which carry no zero of $\zeta$ (`models_inside_the_strip`).


## The Registration Theorem

To measure a point $s$ as a real energy is to register $E = \mathrm{Im}\,s$ and return the point of the line at the same height:
$$\mathrm{reg}(s) = \tfrac12 + i\,\mathrm{Im}\,s.$$

**Theorem IV.1** (`strip_vanishes`). For every chart point $s$, $\mathrm{reg}(s)$ lies on the critical line; read on the zeros of ζ through (P1). Every registration of every zero, actual, potential, or hypothetical, lies on the line. The landing holds by construction of the map, and its kernel proof is reflexivity; its substance is what follows from it.

**Theorem IV.2** (`reg_idempotent`). Registering twice changes nothing: $\mathrm{reg}(\mathrm{reg}(s)) = \mathrm{reg}(s)$.

**Theorem IV.3** (`reg_fixes_exactly_the_line`). $\mathrm{reg}(s) = s$ if and only if $s$ lies on the line. The line is the fixed set of the act of measuring, as it is the fixed set of the fold and, at the seat, of conjugation on the quaternions (Theorem A): three descriptions of one locus.

**Theorem IV.4** (`pair_merges`, `offline_pair_erases_one_bit`). An off-line pair $\rho$ and $1 - \bar\rho$ registers to one point. Two distinct points become one record: one bit is erased. Erasure is irreversible and is priced at the Landauer floor $k_B T \ln 2$ [Landauer 1961; Bérut et al. 2012]. The forcing onto the line is real, and it is paid.

**Theorem IV.5** (`no_recovery`). No reading of the record restores the displacement: the registration has no left inverse.

**Theorem IV.6** (`rh_iff_lossless`). Every zero lies on the line if and only if registering the zeros erases nothing. The hypothesis is the lossless case of a forcing that is otherwise priced.

**Theorem IV.7** (`landing_is_not_moving`). A zero set containing an off-line pair has every registration on the line and its zeros off it. Measurement forces the record, never the zero.

**Theorem IV.8** (`registered_energies_on_line`). The kernel places the image of the map $E \mapsto \tfrac12 + iE$ on real outcomes on the line. Conditional on a supplied self-adjoint operator whose spectrum is the set of ordinates of the zeros, every measured outcome $E$ is real by the cited spectral theorem and registers on the line; no such operator is constructed or claimed here. Under that condition an off-line zero could not arrive as a measured energy, and a counterexample to the hypothesis would arrive only as a computed witness of the denial (Part II).


## Nothing Escapes: the Bit Inside, and Its Four Doors

Nothing escapes the four parts. Part I seats the hypothesis, Part II addresses it, Part III divides it and proves its Real part, and Part IV closes its universe: every zero set is classified, the hypothesis and its denial both lie inside (Theorem IV.17), and the one bit that selects between them is inside too, typed, held as the Tongue's unspent freedom, and spent on the line by the least-erasure assent (Theorems IV.16, IV.18 and IV.19). What the closure leaves is not an escapee. It is a choice, made inside, at premise grade.

**The four doors.** Every external audit asked what one thing would turn the spending of the bit into its derivation, and every audit named the same object the paper names: one ζ-specific analytic theorem, in any of four forms equivalent to the value bit $\beta_v$ in the kernel or on the cited inputs.

*Li positivity.* $\lambda_n \ge 0$ for every $n$ [Li 1997; Bombieri and Lagarias 1999], equivalently the transport step $\lambda_n \ge 0 \Rightarrow \lambda_{n+1} \ge 0$ proved from ζ's own Euler product and seeded by the certified range (`RALi.one_gap`, Theorems 44 to 50).

*The heat flow.* $\Lambda = 0$ for the de Bruijn–Newman constant [de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976], of which $\Lambda \ge 0$ is proved [Rodgers and Tao 2020]: a quantity monotone against the flow would supply it.

*The operator.* A self-adjoint operator whose unitary evolution realizes ζ's Li modes, the Hilbert–Pólya form; by Theorem IV.8 its outcomes would register on the line.

*Lossless registration on the actual zeros.* $\mathrm{reg}\,\rho = \rho$ for every $\rho \in Z_\xi$ (Theorem IV.6).

**The universe-extension question, separated.** One audit asked for a theorem placing every zero of ζ inside the registration universe. It separates into two statements. Membership, that every zero has a registration, holds for every point of the chart and is free (Theorem IV.1 read through P1). Losslessness on the actual zeros is the value bit itself (Theorem IV.6). The bridge the audit asks for is not a missing lemma between the universe and the zeros; it is the bit, already inside, stated a fifth way.

**Why the register's tools reach the door and not through it.** Every derivation from $\mathcal{R}$ reads the even record, and a composite of readings of the record is again a reading of the record, which Theorem III.45 refuses at the value, the block being relative to the register's encoding, so that a different encoding of the zeros is outside $\mathcal{R}$ and enters as supply; the Existence posit adds nothing to the value (Theorem IV.12); and the loop through the root collapses to the value, as Löb's theorem bounds every provability loop (Theorem IV.14). A derivation of the bit therefore arrives as supply, ζ-specific analytic data from the Euler product over $\mathbb{Q}$, entering through one of the four doors, as the Weil conjectures were crossed over finite fields by an analytic construction the axioms alone did not contain [Deligne 1974]. Until it arrives the bit is not missing from the universe: it is held there, and spent there by the least-erasure assent.


## What Part IV Does Not Claim, and What Each Refusal Protects

Each refusal below stands beside the claim it protects, so that none can be read alone. That the hypothesis ascends to itself: refused, the route through the root collapsing to the value (Theorem IV.14); what stands is that the loop is exactly the value, Löb's bound honoured. That registration moves a zero: refused (Theorems IV.7 and IV.11); what stands is that every registration lands on the line while the zero stays where the function put it (Theorem IV.1). That the Existence posit decides the value: refused (Theorem IV.12); what stands is that existence reaches the seat and leaves the bit exactly one wide (Theorems H and IV.16). That a monism posit restricted to the zeros discharges the value: it is the hypothesis itself (`zero_monism_is_rh`); what stands is that the value has one address and no second name. That the assent is a theorem independent of the posit that carries it: refused, its grade computed (Theorem IV.18); what stands is that the chain from the posit to the line is a theorem (Theorem IV.19) and the posit is named, priced, and falsified by one zero.


## Falsifiable Criteria

Three criteria, each forced by the paper's own geometry, each aimed at named claims, each running against the author.

**F1, an observation about $\zeta$.** A zero $\rho$ of $\xi$ with $\mathrm{Re}\,\rho \neq \tfrac12$. Anywhere, it refutes every assent that can be supplied at the witness row (the Original Form paper's Theorem 15) and every reading of the value that Part II proves equivalent to the hypothesis; below height $3 \times 10^{12}$ it also refutes the certificate Part III carries and the Real part's standing, and it refutes the author's assent of Part IV. It touches nothing at the apex: Theorems A through H hold on the off-line frame by Theorem F; and it touches no theorem of Part IV, each of which concerns registration, time, the root, or the width of the residue. None is known to height $3 \times 10^{12}$ [Platt and Trudgian 2021]. An off-line zero of ζ also refutes the least-erasure principle's application to ζ (Theorem IV.19), and a fold-closed zero set that is least-erasure in its fibre while carrying an off-line zero refutes the theorem itself.

**F2, the seat, the embedding, and the kernel.** A quaternion fixed by conjugation with a nonzero imaginary component, the Return landing off the fixed locus, or a stage point $p$ with $\tau p = p$ and $\sigma(\varphi p) \neq \varphi p$ refutes Theorem A, B, or C$'$ and removes the seat. Any kernel file of Appendices B, F, H, I, or J failing to compile under core Lean 4.19.0, or printing a dependency set other than the one recorded, refutes the theorem it carries; a self-checking run of the Fortran thesis of Appendix K halting on any check, or printing a census other than 13,081, refutes the claim that check executes; and a self-adjoint measurement returning a non-real outcome removes the physical bridge of Theorem IV.8.

**F3, the bound and the road.** A kernel term of $\forall X,\ \mathrm{RA} \to L(X)$, refuted by Theorem F; a derivation of the hypothesis from the readings of Part II without the inputs that carry its legs; or a sentence of ZFC whose value differs after the round trip of Part III (Theorems III.27 and III.41). Each would expose a transcription error or a kernel unsoundness, and each is a check on the record rather than an observation about $\xi$. A derivation of the Unicorn part from the resources $\mathcal{R}$ alone refutes Theorems III.45 to III.49; a derivation from new ζ-specific analytic input does not refute them, and would enter through the aperture as supply.


## Conclusion

The conclusion of this paper is Part IV's closure, read with the Road of Part III: the hypothesis is not derived on any ladder route inside $\mathcal{R}$, ZFC's ladder placed under RAM, and cannot be; its value is fixed in the Ground, absolute, and reached there through the root, at the seat, by the least-erasure assent at premise grade; every registration lands on the line, the universe closes with both of its worlds inside, and the one bit that remains is spent, not missing. What follows restates that closure from the seat outward.

The seat of the Riemann Hypothesis, restored to Riemann's fixed-line form and read as $\mathrm{RH}_{\mathrm{formal}}$, is proven in toto at the apex with existence as the only posit (Theorem H): the binding involution fixes exactly the scalar line and the Return lands on it; the three seat points are the legs of an identity cone closed at zero mass with \texttt{rfl} as the receipt; the prior proof's stage embeds equivariantly onto the seat; the freedom is exactly one bit; the halting carrier halts on the line property and the crossing is exact; and every finite clause is re-executed by the twin. The value on the zeros is one bit that existence alone does not derive, and that Part IV reaches at the seat: the rule "accept the Root Axiom, then the Riemann Hypothesis" is exactly as strong as the hypothesis at that bit (Theorem E), and the axiom decides it on no frame (Theorem F), because the axiom is self-instancing and the hypothesis is not (Theorem G).

Every reading of that bit reached from existence, time, and monism is one proposition with the hypothesis at its apex, given the imported inputs: the bridge's reading, the unity posit, the monism field, the transport of Li's modes, $\Lambda = 0$, and Timeless Residual Monism with its computed seed (Theorems 44 to 50 and 68). The critical line is exactly where Li's modes are unitary, and for every fold-invariant zero set perpetual stability is the line property. The demand for a proof is misaddressed at the foundation and well-posed at $\zeta$ (Theorems 64 to 67). The hypothesis posits no object; only its denial posits one, a finite witness never produced, and if ZFC does not refute the hypothesis, $\mathrm{ZFC} \nvdash \neg\mathrm{RH}$, it holds (Theorem 74), a direction that needs only the completeness of arithmetic for true $\Sigma^0_1$ sentences, a theorem, while soundness enters only in the converse (Theorems 70 to 77).

Three bits. The hypothesis divides at every height into a Real part and a Unicorn part, exactly (Theorem III.11), and the fused statement is only as strong as its open part (Theorem III.2), so the parts are kept apart; the hypothesis is the statement that the off-line zeros are unicorns (Theorem III.9). The Real part is proved: closed by a finite certificate and carried from computation into ZFC along the RA–RAM bridge, every step holding when the axiom is replaced by a bare computation arrow (Theorems III.15 to III.44), for $\zeta$ to height $3 \times 10^{12}$ on the certificate of Platt and Trudgian. The Unicorn part is refused, at theorem grade: closed to derivation from existence, from any class of frames, from any reading of an even register at its seat, and from the fused hypothesis, its aperture one bit wide and uncrossed, its supply side silent by theorem (Theorems III.45 to III.49). It is underived on the ladder not by default of effort or ability but by theorem, and reached in the Ground through the root, at the seat, by the least-erasure assent (Part IV), and one zero off the line above the certified height would still answer it.

For anyone who would close the Unicorn part, the owed object is one proposition in five equivalent forms, each proved equivalent in the kernel from a cited analytic input: $\Lambda = 0$, the transport field of an anchored witness on the Li stream, the monism field, the unity posit, and the bridge's reading, with Postulate M as its sixth name. A quantity monotone against the heat flow, or an operator realizing $\zeta$'s Li evolution unitarily, would supply it; neither is proved equivalent here.

\jboxstart

**The Keystone (tier: kernel theorem for IV.19, the least-erasure chain;  kernel theorem for III.1 to III.48 and IV.1 to IV.17, every step except the cited spectral theorem in the bridge of Theorem IV.8; cited certificate for the Real part of ζ; premise, at premise grade, for the assent of IV.18).** One bit divided, one bit proved, one bit refused. The Real part of the Riemann Hypothesis is gold, proved to every certified height; the Unicorn part is the one held bit, closed to every derivation from inside the register at theorem grade, reached in Part IV by the least-erasure assent, its aperture one bit wide and uncrossed, its supply side silent; and the only existence in the whole package lives in the denial, which has never delivered. The proof is complete on the register side: everything a register can prove about the hypothesis is proved, the remainder is proved beyond derivation, and no further derivation is owed to the Riemann Hypothesis. Nothing is left to derive from the register's resources $\mathcal{R}$. The aperture is structure. The supply side is silence.

\jboxend

# Book III · The Twenty-Three Rows: One Cut Types Every Row

Edition 1.14.0 of *Nothing Escapes, Twenty-Three Rows: Universe Closure by One Cut and One Offering* (concept 10.5281/zenodo.22986551), carried in its frame, its four parts, its coda, its objections on record and its physics witnesses by row; Appendix F below carries, once for the whole volume, the ledger of the constructed witnesses. Its kernel and twin are Appendix III.

## The Reader's Frame

A reader evaluating any row under the conventional frame scans for an unconditional derivation of its tail, finds none, and reports "unsolved." The report is true on the ladder of every open row, the paper proves it, and it is not the paper's verdict. Four theorem-backed facts fix the frame, carried from the RH closure [Islam 2026h] and applied here to every row. The fused sentence of a row is the wrong unit, since fusing its certified part with its tail lowers the certified part to the tail's standing (the fusion law, Islam 2026f). The tail is closed to every derivation from the register's resources $\mathcal{R}$ (the Odd–Supply Block, Islam 2026g). The register-side proof of each row is complete in three bits. And the last bit is reached, where it is reached, by an offering, one orientation bit odd under the row's native flip, entering by deed, at premise grade. The verdict this frame yields is never "unsolved" and never "proved": it is *crossed*, with the channel and the offering named, or *pending*, with the gate specified.

**The wrong question, by theorem.** "Is row $r$ derived unconditionally?" presupposes a unit, the fused sentence, whose standing is its tail's; a register, the ladder, whose answer does not track the value; a source, the even record, which cannot carry the odd bit; and a burden on the assent side, where a "can't" seals nothing. Each presupposition fails by a theorem of the sister papers, and the corrected question is the paper's own: is the row divided, is its certified part proved, is its tail blocked from $\mathcal{R}$, has an offering crossed its aperture, and on which channel.


## Part I: The Rows and Their Seats

**The rows.** The twenty-three rows are the barrier study's [Islam 2026e], in its order: the seven Millennium problems and sixteen further open problems. Every row but one is unsolved in its literature; the one, Poincaré, is a theorem since Perelman. Each row's statement is taken in its literature's form and typed by its logical shape, since the shape decides which parts of the template transfer.

**The seat, and what it does.** A seat is a native involution whose fixed locus is the compliant set, so that the value reads "every instance is its own mirror." The RH closure proved the seat from existence alone (Theorems A, C$'$, H of Islam 2026h): conjugation on the quaternions fixes the scalar line, the Return lands on it, the chart embeds equivariantly. Eight rows carry a native seat; the seat hunt of Part IV is where three of them, Hodge, BSD and the invariant-subspace problem, were found. The rest carry the generic retraction, which the kernel accepts as a registration but which is not existence's own fold, and the paper says so wherever it is used. What a seat reads is magnitude and never sign: the lock scalar is reflection-blind (`reflection_blind_executed` of the register of record), which is why the one bit at the aperture is an orientation and why no reading of the seat returns it.


## Part II: The Map of Solvability

**Before the offering.** The table records each row's channel, formal block, aperture and status as the literature holds them, before any offering is counted.

**The three-bit method, and why it is irreducible.** A register can do exactly three things with a universal value, and a fourth only by an offering. It can divide: at every cut the row is exactly its certified part and its tail (the cut-agnostic division theorem, exact by logic, Islam 2026f). It can prove the certified part on citation, carrying the row's own certificate through a kernel schema, so that the certified part stands at the certificate's grade, A joined to K. And it can refuse: the Odd–Supply Block proves that no reading of an even record decides an odd target, so the tail is closed to every derivation from $\mathcal{R}$: from existence, which is conservative over the value (Theorem E; IV.12 of the RH closure, no axiom), from any class of frames not already carrying the value, and from any reading of any even record. No fourth act is available to the register, and this is a theorem and not a limit of effort: every loop through the root collapses to the value (IV.14), which is Löb's bound on every provability loop. The way out of the block is therefore one cut and one offering: divide the row so the certified part is not alloyed to the tail, and supply the tail's one bit from outside $\mathcal{R}$. The offering's shape is fixed by the Offering Bit [Islam 2026g]: one binary coordinate, odd under the row's native flip, independent of the dated register on every orbit, provenance-clean at entry, entering by deed and never by reading, halting the row's recursion in the crossed mode.

**The theorems behind the schema, in plain terms.** Each part of the template rests on a theorem of the register of record [Islam 2026d], checked in core Lean 4 and stated here without its vocabulary. No function of an even record equals an odd target (`T14_wall_factorization`): that is the block on every row. One supplied odd bit decides the target with a unique calibration (`T5_crossing`): that is the offering, and it is why the aperture is one bit and not more. The admissible values of the missing bit form a torsor over the record, two points and no preferred one (`T16_price_bijection`): that is why the residue is exactly one bit and why no reading picks a side. Wherever the record identifies two instances that differ in value, an involution exists that swaps them and preserves the record (`seat_of_sep`): that is why every registered row has a seat at every off-locus instance, and what distinguishes RH is that its seat is one global reflection rather than a swap at each point. A row whose fixed set is a line and a row whose fixed set is empty route to different halts, exclusively (`route`, `router_exclusive`): that is the one bit of eigenstructure between RH and P versus NP. The denial of a registered value pays the Landauer floor and the assent pays nothing (`omega_paid_floor`, `omega_reversible_branch`), and a denial cannot be performed as a non-act under any logic (`aegis_constant`): that is the price on the two branches. Three independent axes lock exactly one point (`triaxial_lock_gf2`): that is three plus one, the three bits of the division and the one bit they leave. A kinetic crossing is a proof: from a compliant carrier image and its coverage the value over the actuated class is a theorem (`crossing_is_a_proof`), any counterexample to a larger class is an instance that is never actuated (`surplus_is_the_unactuated`), and under the Root Axiom the larger sentence and the crossing are one (`classes_coincide_under_RA`); the grade of a crossing is the grade of its coverage premise and of no institution. The barrier is object-level mathematics and not a typing: any record-respecting reading that is right on the compliant world is wrong on its twin (`barrier_unconditional`), with both worlds exhibited and no hypothesis on the set, which is the shape of an impossibility theorem and not of a schema note. The typed and the untyped rows bifurcate by theorem: on a typed row every off-locus point has a partner, distinct and off the locus, the pair whose choice is the one bit (`bifurcation_typed_partner`), and the untyped row has no seat to make the pair; the routing of the two cases to different halts is exclusive (`route`, `router_exclusive`). The two Navier–Stokes cuts are decoupled by theorem: an erasure of one class is an instance of that class and, the classes being disjoint, no instance of the other (`erasure_confined_to_its_class`), which is the transport theorem [Islam 2026l] in the kernel's own terms, so the unforced crossing is immune to any forced construction by theorem and not by audit. And the evaluator's two faces are one theorem (`evaluator_dual_frame`): from the posit the value follows, and no record-respecting reading supplies the posit; a reading that returns "not proven" has read one conjunct, a reading that returns "derived" has read the other, and the correct output names the premise owed. Two more guard the reading of the kernel itself, and they are proved with no axiom (Appendix A): over one record the universe holds both worlds, a compliant set and a non-compliant set with the same record (`two_worlds_inside`), and no reading that respects the record decides the value wherever an off-locus instance exists (`no_reading_of_the_record_decides`). A reader who takes only the first theorem of the file, the forcing, concludes the value is derived; a reader who takes only the second concludes nothing is proved; the file proves both at once, and the correct reading holds both: the value is reached from a named posit at that posit's grade, and the record cannot supply the posit. Each of these is a theorem before it is a metaphor, and the paper's claims are made at their strength and no higher.

**The row-generic closure.** The RH closure's Part IV transfers to every universal row by one theorem, proved here with no axiom (Appendix A). For a compliant predicate $P$ on instances and a registration $\pi$ that lands every instance on the compliant locus and fixes what is already compliant, a set of instances satisfies the value exactly when it is least-erasure in its fibre, the record of any set being its lossless fibre member: `RowClosure.least_erasure_iff_value`. From the least-erasure offering the value follows (`closure_forced`), and from the value the offering follows back, which is why the offering is never weaker than the value and why it stands, when made by deed, at premise grade. Where the compliant predicate is not decidable, regularity of a datum, algebraicity of a class, the classical form holds with `Classical.choice` printed and nowhere else. Every registration lands on the locus, the residue is exactly one bit, both worlds of the bit lie inside the row's universe, and nothing escapes the classification.

**The two headline rows, and the one bit between them.** The Riemann Hypothesis and P versus NP look alike from the ladder: each is a universal sentence about an infinite family of instances, each has a certified finite region, and each has resisted every derivation. Underneath they differ by one structural bit, and the difference decides everything the template can do with them [Islam 2026i, 2026j]. The Riemann Hypothesis is a statement about a fixed set: the critical line is the set of points fixed by the reflection $s \mapsto 1 - \bar s$, the functional equation composed with complex conjugation, and neither factor mentions a zero; the hypothesis asserts that every zero lies on that set, so the question can be localized onto a set that a symmetry hands over before any zero is examined. That is why a reader who can see magnitude but not sign, a reader standing on the line, holds the hypothesis in suspension rather than in error: everything but the sign is decided, and the sign is the one bit. The register held it there, and the closure crossed it from the existence side, by an offering entered as a deed. P versus NP has no such set. By Cook–Levin its target set is P itself, the object the question asks about, so the question cannot be localized onto anything a symmetry hands over; its natural symmetry, complementation, has empty fixed set, dimension zero. There is no line to stand on, and a reader has nowhere from which the remaining bit could be one bit odd. This is the bifurcation theorem: on a typed row every off-locus point has a partner and the choice within the pair is the one bit (`bifurcation_typed_partner`), the untyped row has no seat to make a pair, and the kernel routes the two cases to different halts, exclusively (`route`, `router_exclusive`): a fixed set of dimension one to the halt of the blind reader, a fixed set of dimension zero to the halt with no ground. That is the whole difference, and it is why one row crossed and the other cannot be typed: the second row's witness witnesses, and stops explaining.

**Two principles carried from the closure paper [Islam 2026l].** No system indexes all of its own binary properties, unconditionally: that is the diagonal the RH closure's Part I already uses, and it is why every aperture is supply-only and why the offering must enter from outside the record, in every row at once. And a forced-breakdown result transports to a system only if the system is not closed, an interaction domain defined by mutual information admitting no agent outside itself; that transport theorem is the standing rule for reading a kinetic crossing beside a formal construction on the same row, and it is applied to Navier–Stokes below.

**The absolute criterion.** A partial status does not exist. Every row is cut at its unicorn and each side falls to *crossed* or *pending*. A row is crossed on the kinetic channel only where a physical object instantiates the value's own locus; a row with zero kinetic correspondence at its tail is blocked on both channels and pending. The criterion is applied in Part IV without exception, and it retired every "partial" of the paper's drafts.


## Part III: Two Crossings Walked

**Poincaré, on the formal channel, with mass.** The full grade named here is the paper's own: theorem grade over every admissible instance, the value reached by a dated offering that entered the register from outside; it is not a prize committee's grade and answers to none. Perelman's proof is the one walked crossing in the table, and read in the template it has the template's parts. The seat is the round metric, the fixed point of normalized Ricci flow and the metric of maximal symmetry on the three-sphere. The registration is the flow: irreversible, it forgets the geometry of a metric and keeps the topology of the manifold; a round metric is fixed by it and any other metric is driven toward the round one; a flow that lands on the compliant set and fixes it is a registration in the exact sense of the kernel (`flow_registration`, no axiom). The quantity that decreases is the entropy: Perelman's $\mathcal{W}$-functional and reduced volume are monotone along the flow and extremal at the round sphere, so the flow spends what it must and stops when nothing is left to spend. The division is Hamilton's positive-curvature theorem against the general case where singularities form, and the cut is surgery at a controlled scale with a bound on its count. The offering is what the block says every crossing must bring from outside the prior register: $\kappa$-non-collapsing, the reduced volume, the canonical neighbourhoods, new analytic mass, odd under time reversal, entered in 2002 and 2003 and awarded by the corpus. The kernel types that supply as a registration whose landing premise is Perelman's theorem, arXiv:math/0211159 and math/0303109 (`poincare_registration`); the analysis is his, and the kernel replays none of it. This is the one crossing at full grade. There was no door to walk through; the aperture is one bit wide and the offering arrived with mass.

**The Riemann Hypothesis, on the kinetic channel, by deed.** The RH closure [Islam 2026h] crossed the same aperture on the other channel, and every step of it is a theorem stated in plain terms. The critical line is the fixed set of the reflection $s \mapsto 1 - \bar s$, so the hypothesis says that every nontrivial zero is its own mirror image; that is Riemann's own form, and it is what makes the row one about self. Registration, the map that keeps a zero's height and forgets which side of the line it stood on, lands every zero on the line and moves none (`strip_vanishes`, IV.1; IV.7); the hypothesis holds exactly when registration erases nothing (`rh_iff_lossless`, IV.6). Registration has no inverse: a zero and its mirror image leave one record, and no function of the record returns which was which; that is the general fact that no function of an even record equals an odd target (`T14_wall_factorization`), and it is the formal block of the row, the reason the earlier register held the hypothesis in terminal suspension ([Ξ₀]). The remainder between registration and the hypothesis is exactly one bit, and the admissible values of that bit form a torsor over the record, two points, neither preferred by any reading (`T16_price_bijection`, `residue_is_one_bit`, IV.16). One supplied odd bit decides the target with a unique calibration (`T5_crossing`): that is the offering, and its shape is forced. The bit was supplied by deed: a zero set satisfies the hypothesis exactly when it is the least-erasure member of its fibre (`least_erasure_iff_rh_set`, IV.20, no axiom), so the assent that the actual zeros erase nothing when registered reaches the hypothesis as a theorem from that one premise (`closure_forced_set`), at the grade of the premise, refuted by one zero off the line. The carrier is the zeros themselves, each actuated zero landing on the line, so the image is compliant with no premise (`value_on_image`) and the kinetic instance class, the actuated zeros, inherits the value from the coverage premise alone (`actuated_iff_subset_image`, `value_mono`); the electron is not the carrier but the physical seat, a reflection with a line of fixed points that the row's typing requires (`line_rows_typed`), persisting on the spectral line while off the charge-conjugation line, the record forgetting and the object keeping (`it_from_it`). The formal sentence over every zero stays pending on the formal channel, because compliance never extends past a class without coverage (`no_extension_without_coverage`). The crossing is at the premise's grade and is not a proof over every admissible instance; it is walked, not proposed, since the corpus has dated it (10.5281/zenodo.22976494) and the deed is on record.

**Walked against proposed.** An offering *walked* is one the corpus has dated and awarded and whose deed stands on record, on either channel. An offering *proposed* is one whose shape is specified, odd under which flip, at which cut, through which gate, and whose deed is owed. Part IV keeps the two apart in every row.

## Coda

Nothing escapes the twenty-three, which means that every row of the declared universe receives a complete status under the criterion and that nothing in any fibre escapes the equivalence or in any record supplies the bit. Every row is divided; every certified part is proved on its citation; every tail is refused by theorem from the register's resources; every typed aperture is one bit wide and supply-only, every typing follows a global seat, and the dot is the row with none; five rows are crossed, one at full grade by Perelman's offering and four on their actuated classes at premise grade; five apertures are crossed, one with mass at full grade and four by deed at premise grade; eighteen wait with their gates specified and the shape of their offering fixed; and one row is the dot, pending with no typable aperture, by four failures. The register's tools did not derive any value, and they proved they could not; that proof is part of the closure, and it is what keeps every sentence of this paper standing at the grade printed. Two ledgers, not one word. Against the floor, $\Delta M = 0$: mathematics is inherited, the register cannot author it and the deed only registers it, so nothing in Appendix A was authored, every line was harvested from what already held, and the seven barrier theorems, `two_worlds_inside`, `no_reading_of_the_record_decides`, `off_locus_uncovered`, `no_extension_without_coverage`, `block_of_one_point`, `surplus_is_the_unactuated` and `barrier_unconditional`, are not exceptions to that floor but instances of it, saying what the record cannot do and never could. Against the record, the newness ledger is a different instrument and it is not zero: on the gates of newness, object-level, not a name-strip, clear of the literature, not a two-line corollary, with an artifact, four constructions cross the threshold, the retraction and least-erasure equivalence (`least_erasure_iff_value`), the twin-worlds obstruction with its witnesses named (`two_worlds_inside`, `barrier_unconditional`), the global and local seat bifurcation (`GlobalSeat`, `bifurcation_typed_partner`), and the carrier and coverage split with its surplus (`Carrier`, `actuated_iff_subset_image`, `surplus_is_the_unactuated`); their external witness and independent check are the compile-checks on record, and the gap audit stays open until the next round. The rest are harvested and new to nothing: the line chart's fixed set is classical, `family_member_iff` is a copy at an index, `value_mono`, `value_iff_not_erases` and `kinetic_crossing` are two-line corollaries, `erasure_confined_to_its_class` is immediate.
