## Appendix E: Physics Witnesses by Row

Every witness here enters at corroboration grade and promotes nothing: a corroboration joined to a claim takes the weaker grade (`citation_cannot_promote`), so no verdict of Part IV moves. What the census shows is where the template touches the world. Two witnesses run across every row. Gravity is the registration: sources of one sign, no source off the locus, no two worlds over its record and hence no bit for a record to miss, the retraction itself, the reversible branch that keeps no record and pays no floor. Magnetism is the barrier: charges in pairs under conjugation, no monopole, remanence as two states over one record, the kept bit, the priced branch whose loop's area is the price of erasure, where Landauer's floor was measured in the laboratory. Under time reversal the electric record is even and the magnetic target odd, and no function of the even record returns the odd target. Both are typed in the program's physics register (PSP-SPHYS-ARROWS-01, `SPHYS_Two_Arrows.lean`), and both are readings, not a field theory.

The reading the two arrows license, at structural grade and no higher: quantization is the priced registration of a bit, and a row with no off-locus point has no bit to register. Gravity, the one-signed field, is the reversible branch with nothing to quantize, and its resistance to quantization is a fact of type and not of difficulty; magnetism, the two-signed field, carries the bit and is quantized in flux. The two are one registration read on its two branches. This paper claims the typing and refuses the field theory.

# Book IV · The Fourth as Cosmic Closure

Edition 1.3.0 of *Nothing Escapes: The Fourth as Cosmic Closure*, carried in its body; its kernels and twin are Appendix IV.

## Two Things That Cannot Be Reached

Proof and measurement each have a blind spot, and the two blind spots face each other.

**The ghost.** A physical object, an electron, a neutrino, a spectrum in a magnetic cavity, supplies what a formal ladder cannot derive, and it supplies it by a deed on the kinetic channel. Read as a formal proof it is a ghost: it stands where the formal register cannot see it, and it reaches nothing on the far side of the cut.

**The unicorn.** A zero of $\zeta$ off the critical line is a well-posed object of arithmetic. Read as a measured energy it is a unicorn: a measurement returns a real number, the height, and registration puts every measured zero on the line. No measurement ever shows one.

This paper proves that the ghost and the unicorn are closed by one cut, the critical line itself, and that nothing escapes it.


## The Frame: Three Axes and the Fourth

The closure of the Riemann Hypothesis (Islam, 2026a) runs in four parts. **The seat**: the fold $s \mapsto 1 - \bar s$, whose fixed set is the critical line, handed over before any zero is examined. **The address**: every reading reached from existence points to one proposition, with the hypothesis at its apex. **The division**: the cut at the certified height $T = 3 \times 10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian, 2021) separates the proved part from the tail, and the tail is closed to derivation from inside the register, by theorem. **The closure**: the three return onto the scalar line, as $i \cdot j \cdot k = -1$ returns three orthogonal units to $-1$, and the universe of the hypothesis closes with both worlds inside.

This paper reads the fourth part as a cosmic closure. The two registers, the formal one that proves and the physical one that measures, each leave one thing out of reach. The fourth part closes both with one cut.


## The Unicorn: What Measurement Never Shows

Take the critical strip in a chart that keeps everything exact: a point is its doubled real part $x$ and its height $t$, the critical line is $x = 1$, and the fold sends $x$ to $2 - x$ and keeps $t$ (`fold_involution`); its fixed set is exactly the line (`fold_fixed_iff`). Registration is the measurement of a zero as an energy, $s \mapsto \tfrac12 + i\,\mathrm{Im}\,s$: it keeps the height, which is what a measurement returns, and lands on the line.

Three theorems carry the physical face. Registration lands every point on the line (`reg_lands_on_line`). It fixes every point already there (`reg_fixes_line`). And a point off the line is never the image of a registration (`unicorn_never_registered`). A zero off the critical line is therefore a unicorn in the physical register: whatever is measured, it is not that.

**At every resolution.** The chart is exact at any grain. With the line at $x = n$ and the fold $x \mapsto 2n - x$, every theorem of the cut holds for every $n$ (Appendix D), and $n = 1$ is the chart above (`resolution_one_is_the_chart`). At that coarsest grain the open strip holds no point off the line (`coarse_strip_is_the_line`), so its off-line pair sits on the edges, at real parts 0 and 1, where the prime number theorem already forbids zeros (Hadamard, 1896; de la Vallée Poussin, 1896). From $n = 2$ on the open strip carries points off the line (`interior_off_line_exists`), and at $n = 10$, the grid of the executed twin, the pair at real parts 0.4 and 0.6 is off the line, strictly inside the strip, and registers to one record (`interior_pair_at_resolution_ten`). The unicorn is shown where a counterexample would have to stand.

**The classical face.** A measurement returns a real number, and a self-adjoint operator has a real spectrum. The Hilbert–Pólya program rests on that fact: were the heights of the zeros the eigenvalues of a self-adjoint operator, every zero would lie on the line (Conrey, 2003). The unicorn is the same fact on the chart: whatever registration returns lies on the line.


## The Ghost: What the Record Never Reads

Registration keeps the height and forgets the side. The two points of an off-line orbit, $s$ and $1 - \bar s$, are distinct (`off_line_pair_distinct`) and register to one record (`reg_forgets_side`), so no reading of the record recovers which side a point stood on (`ghost_side_unread`). The formal register works from the record; the side is exactly what it cannot read.

That bit is supplied in the physical register by a deed, never read in the formal one. The same fact, run the other way, is the ghost: a carrier whose image lies on the locus reaches no instance off it (`ghost_generic`). A physical object offered as a proof about the far side of the cut touches nothing there.

**The classical face.** Sieve methods work from data that cannot tell a number with an odd count of prime factors from one with an even count, and so cannot reach parity: Selberg's parity barrier (Friedlander and Iwaniec, 2010). The record here is symmetric under the fold in the same way, and it cannot reach the side at any resolution (`ghost_side_unread`).


## One Cut, One Bit

The two unreachables are one point's two faces. Off the line, a point has a partner, its side vanishes from the record, and no registration shows it, all three at once (`ghost_and_unicorn_one_bit`). On the line, the point is its own partner and registration keeps it whole.

**Nothing escapes.** Every point of the strip is in exactly one of these two cases (`nothing_escapes_one_cut`): on the line, fixed and registered without loss; or off it, paired, side forgotten, never measured. The ghost's bit and the unicorn are not two mysteries. They are the two faces of one point on the far side of one cut.


## The Hypothesis Is Lossless Registration

On any list of zeros, registration erases nothing exactly when every zero is on the line (`lossless_iff_on_line`). The Riemann Hypothesis is lossless registration.

**Both worlds inside.** One chart holds a lossless world and a world with one priced orbit: a zero on the line registers to itself, while the pair at $x = 0$ and $x = 2$ at one height registers to one record (`both_worlds_inside`). Two points into one record is one bit forgotten, and forgetting a bit costs at least $k_B T \ln 2$ (Landauer, 1961; Bérut and colleagues, 2012). The twin computes it at 300 K: $2.87098 \times 10^{-21}$ J per off-line orbit.

**Executed.** The twin registers the first ten zeros, heights from Odlyzko's tables, and every one comes back bit for bit: nothing erased. It sweeps the whole grid, 19 real parts by 20 heights: every registration lands on the line, the fold is an involution, no off-line point is ever a registered point, and every off-line pair shares one record. Placed in a list with the ten zeros, one off-line pair is where the loss appears, two points and one bit. Eight checks, zero failures (Appendix B). The same sweep of the grid is decided in the Lean kernel (`twin_grid_decided`), so the executed twin and the proved chart agree point for point.


## The Same Cut on Every Row

Nothing in the chart is special to the Riemann row. On any locus $P$ with a registration onto it, the value is lossless registration (`lossless_iff_value`), an off-locus instance is never a registered point (`unicorn_generic`), and no carrier landing on the locus reaches it (`ghost_generic`). Every instance of every row is on the locus or off it, where no registration shows it and no carrier reaches it (`one_cut_generic`). This is the cut the twenty-three-row volume runs row by row (Islam, 2026b), and the six constructed witnesses land on it (Islam, 2026c–h).


## The Ledger: Where the Cut Has Been Witnessed, Crossed and Confirmed

The cut has been met in the world, row by row. Each constructed witness is a carrier landing on its row's locus; where it covers the row's actuated class, the row is crossed on its channel; where its image is compliant as built or measured, it is confirmed. The ledger below is the twenty-three-row volume's own (Islam, 2026b, Appendix F); its theorem names are those of that volume's kernel, carried in the Master Codex's Code Block. Every status in it is computed from recorded facts, and every entry in the last column is nothing or one object of a computed kind.

\endgroup



Read against the one cut, the ledger says one thing. Every crossed row is a row where a carrier stands on the near side and nothing on the far side is measured; every pending row owes the one object that would put a carrier there; and the dot owes nothing, because its row has no seat and so no cut to stand on either side of.


## The Cosmic Closure

The fourth part closes the universe of the hypothesis. Every point stands on one side of one cut, and the two things neither register can reach both stand on the far side: the formal register cannot read the side, and the physical register cannot show the point. Nothing escapes the cut.

What remains is one bit: the side of the cut on which the actual zeros stand. The formal register cannot read it; the physical register cannot show its alternative. The closure spends it by the least-erasure assent, at premise grade, beside the Root Axiom: the actual universe occupies the zero-cost member of its record's fibre. No physical fact here proves a mathematical sentence, and no derivation of the hypothesis from the axioms of set theory is claimed; the bit is supplied, never read.

And the mirror fixes the form any counterexample must take. What the formal register cannot read is supplied in the physical register by a deed; what the physical register cannot register, a zero off the line, could be exhibited only by computation. **A counterexample would arrive as a computed witness, never as a measured energy.**

Arithmetic says the same. The hypothesis is equivalent to an arithmetical sentence that a single failing instance would refute by a finite computation: to the unsolvability of one Diophantine equation (Davis, Matiyasevich and Robinson, 1976), and to an inequality between the divisor sum of $n$ and the harmonic number $H_n$ holding for every $n$ (Lagarias, 2002). A counterexample, if one exists, is a computation that ends; the mirror and arithmetic agree on its form.


## Falsifiers

**F-Measure.** A measured energy identified with a zero off the line. On the chart no registration returns one, at any resolution (`unicorn_never_registered`). **F-Record.** A reading of registered records that recovers the side of an off-line orbit. No function of the record does (`ghost_side_unread`). **F-Computed.** A zero of $\zeta$ computed off the critical line, at a real part strictly between 0 and 1, as the grid's interior pair is (`interior_pair_at_resolution_ten`). It would falsify the hypothesis in exactly the form the mirror predicts, and it is the one channel the theorems leave open.


# Book V · The Six Witnesses, Edition 1.5.0

The six constructed witnesses of the twenty-three rows, in their synchronized edition 1.5.0, each carried in its body with its own spine; their shared ledger is carried once, in Book III, and the series' typed ledger of their falsifiers is in Book VII.

## The Electron Is the Seat

*Charge Conjugation as the Reflection, the Positron as the Partner, Annihilation as the Registration That Keeps the Energy and Forgets the Side, and Spin as the Return to Minus One.* Edition 1.5.0.

**Abstract.** Charge conjugation, pair annihilation and the sign a spinor takes under a full turn are three of the oldest facts of quantum physics, and they have never been read as one shape. This paper reads them on the closure template by which the Riemann Hypothesis was closed in the author's sealed volume, and finds that the electron carries the template's seat and its registration. Charge conjugation is a reflection whose fixed set is the neutral sector, as the critical line is the fixed set of the reflection s to 1 minus s-bar; the electron stands off that set with an exact partner, the positron, differing from it in one sign; gravity's record of the pair is the same for both, two worlds over one record, and antihydrogen falls as matter does; annihilation lands the pair on the neutral locus as light, keeping its energy and forgetting which constituent was which, the registration that keeps the height and forgets the side, and the clinic records it as a line of response; positronium's photon count reads the bit of the whole and never the identity of its parts; a bound electron never rests and a free one never decays; a full turn returns the spinor to minus one, the Return of the quaternion units; and the electron is round, its only orientations the charge sign and the spin. Twenty correspondences are proved on finite models in core Lean 4 and seventeen checks are executed on the measured constants in Fortran: the Rydberg energy reproduced to a part in a billion, the virial theorem from independent constants, both positronium lifetimes within a tenth of a percent, the anomalous moment from the five-loop series. Every claim is at corroboration grade and promotes nothing; the Riemann closure stands on its own receipts. The companion paper, The Neutrino Is the Witness, reads the crossing on the neutral lepton; this one reads the seat and the registration on the charged one.

### 1. The Reader's Frame

This paper is one of six constructed witnesses for the closure template of the Riemann Hypothesis and the twenty-three rows. Each builds, for the rows it serves, the carrier the two volumes named and did not build: an explicit construction from the world into the row, whose image is compliant by the row kernel's own theorem (`value_on_image`), with coverage of the row's full class kept as the premise the volumes print. Physicists have used charge conjugation since Dirac, annihilation since Anderson, and the spinor's sign since the first neutron interferometers, each as a tool in its own chapter. This paper asks what shape the three share, and answers from the laboratory: they are the seat, the registration and the Return of the closure template by which the author's sealed volume closed the Riemann Hypothesis. Each section begins with the physics, its measurement and its citation, and only then names the part of the template it instantiates.

Two refusals frame everything that follows. The paper does not claim that any physical fact proves any mathematical sentence: a corroboration joined to a claim takes the weaker grade, the Riemann closure stands on its own receipts, and the sealed volume mentions neither the electron nor the neutrino and needs neither. And the paper does not claim that the electron carries the whole template. The one part it does not exhibit is the posit itself: the assent that the actual zeros erase nothing under registration is a number-theoretic assent with no electron analogue, and it needs none. The companion papers show the offering's mechanism, a bit supplied by deed from outside the record, in the neutrino's mass, and the posit's shape, a registration that erases nothing because nothing stands off its locus, in gravity's fold; spending the posit on the zeros is the author's assent. What the electron shows is that the template's seat and registration are shapes the world already uses.


**Negative warrants.** Three, stated so that no reader supplies them. No physical fact here is read as a proof of a mathematical sentence: a corroboration joined to a claim takes the weaker grade (`citation_cannot_promote`). No derivation of any row's sentence from the axioms of set theory is claimed: a crossing holds on its channel's own class at its printed grade, and what a sentence over every admissible instance adds is exactly the unactuated (`surplus_is_the_unactuated`). No field theory and no unification of couplings is written or implied.


### 2. The Template, Read from the Laboratory

The Riemann closure has four parts, the seat, the address, the division and the closure, and the electron reads three of them: the seat in Sections 3 to 5, the closure's registration and residue in Sections 6 and 7, and the address in Section 10; the division, a certified region joined to an open tail, has no reading specific to the electron. The **seat**: the critical line is the fixed set of the reflection $s \mapsto 1 - \bar s$, and the hypothesis says every zero is its own mirror image. In the laboratory the reflection is charge conjugation and its fixed set is the neutral sector, the particles that are their own antiparticles. The **registration**: the map that keeps a zero's height and forgets which side of the line it stood on, landing every zero on the line and moving none already there; the hypothesis holds exactly when it erases nothing. In the laboratory it is annihilation, which keeps a pair's energy and forgets which constituent was which, landing the pair on the neutral sector as light. The **residue**: exactly one bit, a two-point torsor over the record that no reading of the record decides. In the laboratory it is the sign of the charge, the only thing that separates an electron from a positron.

Three theorems of the author's row-generic kernel carry these parts. Over one record both worlds exist, and no reading that respects the record decides the value (`two_worlds_inside`, `no_reading_of_the_record_decides`). Under a global seat, every point off the fixed set has a partner, distinct and also off it (`off_locus_pair`). And the fold onto the locus is a registration in the exact sense of the kernel (`Registration`). The sections that follow find each of these in a measurement.

### 3. Charge Conjugation Is a Reflection

Dirac's equation of 1928 required a partner for the electron, and Anderson found it in cosmic-ray tracks in 1932: a particle of the electron's mass bending the other way. The operation that exchanges them, charge conjugation, is an involution: applied twice it returns every state to itself (`conj_involution`). Its fixed set is exactly the neutral sector: a state is its own conjugate if and only if it carries no charge (`self_conjugate_iff_neutral`). The photon and the neutral pion sit on it as particles, each its own antiparticle, and each carries under the operation a sign, its charge-conjugation parity, which is the bit Section 7 reads; the electron does not sit on it.

This is the template's seat, found in physics before the template was written. The critical line is the fixed set of a reflection that mentions no zero; the neutral sector is the fixed set of a reflection that mentions no particle's history. In both cases the question of where an object lies is posed on a set that a symmetry hands over before the object is examined.


### 4. The Positron Is the Exact Partner

The electron stands off the fixed set, and its partner under the reflection is the positron: distinct from it, and also off the neutral sector (`positron_is_the_partner`, `the_pair`). This is the kernel's pair theorem exhibited: under a global seat, every point off the locus has a partner, distinct and off the locus. The partner is exact. The CPT theorem of relativistic quantum field theory requires particle and antiparticle to share mass and lifetime, and the measurements agree: the masses of the electron and the positron are equal to eight parts in a billion, and their charges equal and opposite to four parts in a hundred million (Particle Data Group). Conjugation keeps the mass and the spin and flips only the sign of the charge (`pair_differs_in_one_sign`): the two points of the pair differ by exactly one sign, and that sign is the residue of the template, one bit.


### 5. Gravity Cannot Tell Them Apart

Gravity reads mass, and the pair has one mass. The mass record of the electron and of the positron is the same while the states are different (`two_worlds_one_record`), and no function of the mass record returns the charge (`no_reading_of_mass_returns_charge`). This is the two-worlds theorem in its plainest physical form: two states, one record, the bit invisible to every reading of the record.

It is also measured. In 2023 the ALPHA-g collaboration released antihydrogen, a positron bound to an antiproton, in a vertical trap and found it falls with $(0.75 \pm 0.13 \pm 0.16)\,g$, consistent with the fall of ordinary matter at 1.2 standard deviations (computed in Appendix B). Gravity does not read the sign. The author's companion analysis types gravity as the reversible branch of registration, the fold onto the locus that keeps no record of the sign, and magnetism as the priced branch that keeps it (Nothing Escapes, Twenty-Three Rows, Appendix E); the antihydrogen result is that typing observed in a trap.


### 6. Annihilation Is Registration

An electron and a positron at rest annihilate into two photons of 511 keV each, back to back, carrying the pair's whole rest energy of 1021.998 keV (computed in Appendix B). The pair lands on the neutral sector: the light carries no charge (`annihilation_lands_neutral`). The energy is kept (`annihilation_keeps_energy`). And which constituent was which is forgotten: annihilating the electron with the positron and the positron with the electron leave the same record (`annihilation_forgets_side`), the two photons being identical bosons from which no measurement returns the identity of the parts.

This is the template's registration with its two clauses intact. The Riemann registration keeps a zero's height and forgets its side; annihilation keeps the pair's energy and forgets its sign. And the record takes the shape of a line. Back to back, the two photons carry the pair's whole rest energy; at any other opening angle they carry less (computed in Appendix B), so momentum conservation forces the record onto a line through the point of annihilation, and the line is symmetric under exchange of its ends (`line_of_response_symmetric`). Positron emission tomography is built on exactly this: every annihilation in the patient is recorded as a line of response between two detectors, and the image is reconstructed from lines that keep where and when and forget which particle was which. The registration of the Riemann closure is performed millions of times a day in hospitals.


### 7. What the Record Keeps: Positronium

Before it annihilates, an electron and a positron can bind into positronium, and here the record keeps one bit: not the identity of the parts, but the symmetry of the whole. The charge-conjugation parity of the bound state is $(-1)^{L+S}$, and $n$ photons carry $(-1)^n$; the electromagnetic interaction conserves it. So parapositronium, with spins opposed, must decay into an even number of photons, two, and orthopositronium, with spins aligned, into an odd number, three (`para_two_photons`, `ortho_three_photons`, `ortho_not_two`). The extra photon costs a power of the coupling, and the lifetimes differ a thousandfold: computed from the lowest-order rates with their one-loop corrections, 125.231 ps for para and 142.068 ns for ortho, against measured 125.14 ps and 142.05 ns, within a tenth of a percent, a ratio of 1134.5 (Appendix B).

The template's reading is exact. A registration can keep a bit of the whole while forgetting everything about the parts: the photon count reads the whole's parity and never which constituent was the electron. The two-worlds theorem is about the parts; the whole's bit is a different bit, and the record keeps it.


### 8. The Floor: The Electron Never Rests and Never Decays

The program's one declared premise is that to exist is to actuate: no existent carries zero kinetic content. The bound electron is its cleanest instance. In the hydrogen ground state the kinetic energy is 13.605693 eV and the potential energy $-27.211386$ eV, computed independently from the Bohr radius and $\hbar c$; twice the first plus the second vanishes to a part in a billion, the virial theorem, and the total reproduces the Rydberg energy to the same precision (Appendix B). By the virial theorem a bound electron's kinetic energy is minus its total energy, so a bound electron never rests (`bound_never_rests`). Confinement forbids rest, and the atom is the proof.

The free electron never decays. It is the lightest charged particle, every lighter state is neutral, and so no final state of its decay can carry its charge (`decay_forbidden`). The Borexino experiment bounds its lifetime above $6.6 \times 10^{28}$ years. The floor of the charged sector is kept by the electron alone: it cannot stop moving and it cannot stop existing.


### 9. Spin: The Return Lands on Minus One

A rotation by $2\pi$ returns every vector to itself and every spin-one-half state to its negative; only a rotation by $4\pi$ returns the spinor. This was demonstrated for neutrons by interferometry in 1975 (Rauch; Werner) and holds for every spin-one-half particle, the electron first among them; the twin computes it on the rotation matrices to a few parts in $10^{16}$ (Appendix B). The unit quaternions are the spinor rotations: the unit $i$ is a half-turn about one axis, $i^2 = -1$ is the full turn (`spin_two_pi`), and $i^4 = 1$ the double turn (`spin_four_pi`). Three half-turns about three perpendicular axes return every vector to itself and give $i j k = -1$ (`the_return`).

That product is the template's Return, the product of the three axes landing on the scalar line with a sign that no reading of the three axes' magnitudes decides. The electron carries it at every full turn. Dirac's equation assigns it the magnetic moment of $g = 2$; how far the electron departs from two is the next section's number.


### 10. One Number and One Bit: The Anomalous Moment and the Round Electron

The electron's anomalous magnetic moment, $a_e = (g-2)/2$, is the most precisely measured property of any elementary particle: $a_e = 0.001\,159\,652\,180\,59(13)$ (Fan and collaborators, 2023). Schwinger's first term, $\alpha/2\pi$, fixes it to three figures; the universal series of quantum electrodynamics in $\alpha/\pi$, computed through five loops (Laporta; Aoyama, Kinoshita and Nio), with $\alpha$ from rubidium recoil (Morel and collaborators), gives 0.001159652175783, short of experiment by $4.8 \times 10^{-12}$, the order of the mass-dependent, hadronic and electroweak terms the universal series omits (Appendix B). Every reading of the electron, its spectrum, its moment and its recoil, converges on one number, the fine-structure constant: one address. One tension is disclosed and left open: the caesium and rubidium recoil values of $\alpha$ differ by 5.5 standard deviations (Appendix B). An address with a disputed digit is still one address.

The electron is also round. An electric dipole moment would be odd under time reversal, and the fixed set of time reversal is the zero dipole (`round_iff_T_fixed`). The JILA measurement of 2023 bounds the electron's dipole below $4.1 \times 10^{-30}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$, about $1.1 \times 10^{-19}$ of its own reduced Compton wavelength (Appendix B). Nothing in the electron's shape carries an orientation: its only orientations are the sign of its charge and the direction of its spin. The residue the template assigns is one bit per pair, and the electron carries no second one.


### 11. Falsifiers and Owed Deeds

Four falsifiers, each ordinary. **F-Pair:** a difference in mass or charge magnitude between the electron and the positron, breaking the exact partner of Section 4 and CPT with it. **F-Round:** a detected electric dipole moment at any accessible level, an internal orientation beyond the charge sign and the spin, which would require a second bit where Section 10 finds one; the Standard Model's own prediction lies far below present reach. **F-Gravity:** antimatter falling differently from matter, which would mean gravity's record reads the sign and would break the two-worlds reading of Section 5. **F-Decay:** an observed decay of the electron, breaking the floor of Section 8.

Nothing is owed on the row's channel. Three measurements would sharpen the readings without moving the paper's standing: the disputed digit of the fine-structure constant, the electron's size at the tens-of-TeV scale, and the precision of antimatter's fall.

## The Neutrino Is the Witness

*How the Closure Template of the Riemann Hypothesis Is Instantiated by the Particle That Never Leaves the Ground.* Edition 1.5.0.

**Abstract.** The Riemann Hypothesis was closed in a sealed volume by one template: the seat found by symmetry, the value located at one address, the hypothesis divided at its cut, and the universe closed so that the value holds exactly when a named posit holds, the last bit spent by assent. This paper shows that the template is not a construction of number theory: the neutrino instantiates it part by part. Its mass is the floor supplied by deed where the register wrote zero; its single registered chirality is the aperture bit spent by the world; its sterile partner is the physics of a pending row, a formal object no carrier lands on; its Majorana question is membership in the fixed set of conjugation, the locus inhabited or not, with the deciding deed named; its oscillation is registration in a second basis, unitarity being losslessness and a sterile admixture an erasure; and its mass ordering is a one-bit address. The electron complements it as the witness of the seat, the off-locus point with its partner. Eleven correspondences are proved on a finite model in core Lean 4 and executed on the measured mixing parameters in Fortran, unitarity checked to better than a part in 10^16, the flavour sum to ten decimals, the sterile shortfall measured. Every claim is at corroboration grade and promotes nothing; the Riemann closure stands on its own receipts and this paper does not touch them. Two bits stay owed, the Majorana bit to neutrinoless double beta decay and the ordering bit to JUNO, and three ordinary falsifiers are named.

### 1. The Reader's Frame

This paper is one of six constructed witnesses for the closure template of the Riemann Hypothesis and the twenty-three rows. Each builds, for the rows it serves, the carrier the two volumes named and did not build: an explicit construction from the world into the row, whose image is compliant by the row kernel's own theorem (`value_on_image`), with coverage of the row's full class kept as the premise the volumes print. Every correspondence is stated as a theorem on a finite model in core Lean 4 and executed on measured parameters in Fortran. It refuses to claim that any physical fact proves any mathematical sentence. A corroboration joined to a claim takes the weaker grade, and the Riemann closure's verdicts stand on their own receipts; the sealed volume does not mention the neutrino or the electron, and it does not need to. What this paper adds is the other direction: it shows that the template is not an artefact of number theory. The world runs it.

A reader who arrives from the conventional frame will scan this paper for a derivation of the Riemann Hypothesis from physics, find none, and be tempted to report the absence. There is no such derivation here and none was attempted. The unit evaluated is the template, not the hypothesis, and the question answered is whether the world instantiates its parts. The Riemann closure has four parts. ### 3. Two Roles, Two Particles

The electron witnesses the seat. Under charge conjugation it is an off-locus point with a partner, the positron, distinct and off the locus; the pair shows where the reflection is and that the bit exists (`electron_pair`). The electron leaves the ground constantly. It binds, excites, radiates, and actuates nearly everything the register knows; it is the actuator par excellence and, for that reason, a poor witness of the crossing, because it is never the thing on the locus. It does witness the registration in its exact form: an electron and a positron annihilate onto the neutral sector as light, keeping their energy and forgetting which was which, the registration that keeps the height and forgets the side; the companion paper, The Electron Is the Seat, reads that from the laboratory.

The neutrino witnesses the crossing. It sits on the seat's fixed set (`neutrino_on_the_locus`). It is registered in one chirality and never the other. Its sterile partner is a formal object no carrier lands on. Its oscillation is a registration in a second basis whose losslessness is a named hypothesis. Its mass ordering is a one-bit address. And its mass is the floor supplied by deed where the register wrote zero. One particle, every part. The two roles are complementary and never interchangeable: the seat needs a pair, and the crossing needs an occupant of the fixed set.


### 4. The Floor: Mass Supplied by Deed

The formal register of the neutrino, the Standard Model in its minimal form, wrote its mass as zero: no right-handed field, no mass term. The world returned mass greater than zero by oscillation, at Super-Kamiokande in 1998 and at the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory in 2001, and an observed difference of squared masses forces at least one nonzero mass (`oscillation_forces_floor`). The twin executes the fact on the measured values, $\Delta m^2_{21} = 7.53 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{eV}^2$ and $\Delta m^2_{32} = 2.453 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{eV}^2$ for the normal ordering, whence $\Delta m^2_{31} = 2.528 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{eV}^2$, all positive.

This is the program's floor confirmed against the register that denied it. The Root Axiom says that to exist is to actuate: no existent carries zero kinetic content. The neutrino is the boundary case, minimal actuation and nonzero, an existent that passes through the Earth almost without registering and still registers. It is also the archetype of an offering: a bit entered from outside the record, by deed, that the record could not have supplied, and it entered physics two decades before the template was written down.


### 5. The Bit, Spent

Under a global seat every off-locus point has a partner, and the residue of a typed row is the choice within the pair. The neutrino shows that choice made. It is registered left-handed and never right-handed (`active_registered`, `sterile_uncovered`); the registered state and its mirror differ by exactly one bit at the same charge (`one_bit_apart`). Parity violation, observed by Wu in 1957 and built into the weak interaction as it stands, is the world assigning one sign to the pair the seat makes. No other particle exhibits the assent so nakedly: the aperture bit of the template, one bit wide, spent by the world and read from no record.

The right-handed neutrino is allowed by the Lagrangian and uncovered by every weak registration. It is a formal object with zero kinetic correspondence, exactly the status the rows paper calls pending: the row exists in the formal register, no carrier lands on it, both channels blocked by the absolute criterion. The neutrino carries both tables in one particle, the active state crossed and the sterile state pending, one bit between them. Where the rows paper had to say what a pending row is, the neutrino shows one.


### 7. The Locus, Inhabited: Majorana as the Fixed Set

Charge conjugation is an involution whose fixed set is exactly the neutral line (`conj_involution`, `majorana_iff_neutral`); the neutrino sits on it. Whether the neutrino is its own antiparticle, Majorana or Dirac, is precisely the question whether an existent is its own mirror image under the seat, the Riemann row's own form asked of one particle. It is undecided, and the deed that decides it is named: neutrinoless double beta decay, sought by the LEGEND, KamLAND-Zen, CUORE and nEXO programs. One observation, one bit, the value's locus inhabited or not. This paper holds the bit open and does not guess it. What it fixes is the shape of the question and its gate, which is what the template does for every row.

Oscillation is registration forgetting a basis, the second of the registration's two physical faces; the first, keeping the height and forgetting the side exactly as the Riemann registration does, is annihilation, read in the companion paper. The neutrino propagates in the mass basis and is detected in the flavour basis: the record reads flavour and the object keeps mass, the record forgetting and the object keeping. ### 3. One Arrow, Named at Last

To exist is to actuate, and actuation is directed: an existent registers in a record, and registration runs one way. Physics met this arrow twice and gave it two names, the magnetic and the gravitational, without asking whether they were one thing. They differ in exactly one respect, and the respect is the template's: whether the registration keeps a record of what it cannot read. Magnetism keeps it and pays for it. Gravity keeps nothing and pays nothing. Read on the template, they are the priced and the reversible branch of one registration, the Omega guard's two branches, floor-priced and floor-free.


### 4. Magnetism: The Arrow That Keeps a Record

A single-domain nanomagnet with uniaxial anisotropy is described by the Stoner–Wohlfarth energy $e(\theta) = \tfrac12 \sin^2\theta - h \cos(\theta - \psi)$, with $h$ the applied field in units of the anisotropy field and $\psi$ its angle to the easy axis. Swept down from $h = 2$ and back up, it traces a hysteresis loop. At $h = 0$ the descending branch holds $m = +0.996$ and the ascending branch $m = -0.996$ (Appendix B): two states, one applied field, the record $h$ identical and the state different. That is the two-worlds theorem in a material (`two_worlds_at_zero_field`): over one record both worlds exist, and no reading of the record decides which. The magnet keeps the bit the record cannot read; remanence is the kept bit. The constructed switching field is 0.767 against the astroid's 0.766, within one part in a thousand, so the construction is the textbook magnet and not a caricature of one.


### 5. The Price of the Record

The loop encloses area, 3.036 in units of $\mu_0 M_s H_K$ (Appendix B), and the area is energy dissipated per cycle. For a bit thermally stable at room temperature, with anisotropy energy $KV = 40\,kT$, one switch costs $5.0 \times 10^{-19}$ J, against Landauer's floor $kT \ln 2 = 2.87 \times 10^{-21}$ J at 300 K. The priced branch pays, and it never pays less than the floor: Landauer's bound on the erasure of one bit has been approached in the laboratory with a colloidal particle (Bérut and collaborators, 2012) and with nanomagnetic memory bits themselves (Hong and collaborators, 2016). The price is not an accident of materials. It is what keeping a bit costs, and magnetism is the field that keeps one.


### 6. The Pair That Never Separates

Magnetic charges come as north and south, and no one has ever isolated one: there is no monopole. In the template's terms, an off-locus point never appears without its partner (`magnetism_pair`, `off_locus_pair`). And magnetism is the odd face of the field. Under time reversal the electric field is even and the magnetic field odd (`electric_even`, `magnetic_odd`), and no function of the even record returns the odd target (`no_reading_of_E_returns_B`). The barrier of every open row, that the bit is not in the record, is the magnetic field's relation to the electric one.


### 7. Gravity: The Arrow That Keeps None

Gravitational sources have one sign: every mass is positive, every source is its own conjugate, and none stands off the locus (`gravity_no_off_locus`). A row whose every instance is compliant admits no erasure and no two worlds, so there is no bit for a record to miss (`no_bit_without_off_locus`). The constructed witness is an orbit: a body in a Kepler potential, integrated by velocity Verlet for ten revolutions, returns its energy to within $2.8 \times 10^{-7}$ throughout; the path integral of the gravitational force equals the change of kinetic energy; and with every velocity reversed the orbit retraces to its starting point within $1.5 \times 10^{-12}$ (Appendix B). No loop, no remanence, no price: the reversible branch, floor zero and never cost zero (`reversible_free`). The typing forecasts what will not be seen: a field whose every instance is compliant can show no hysteresis whatever its record (`one_sign_no_remanence`), so a gravitational loop is forbidden by theorem before any experiment looks for one.


### 8. The Fold onto the Locus

Gravity is the registration itself: the fold that lands every configuration on its locus with nothing left over, a monic image of the configuration and not a stored copy (`Registration`, `value_iff_fixed`). That is why gravity reads as geometry: a row with no off-locus point is a row already on its locus. On the formal channel the fold is Ricci flow, which Perelman carried through the Poincaré row, and which arises in physics as the renormalization flow of the two-dimensional sigma model (Friedan, 1980): the one crossed row with mass is crossed by a gravitational fold. And gravity cannot read the one sign the pair carries: antihydrogen falls as matter does (ALPHA-g, 2023), as the companion paper The Electron Is the Seat reads from the laboratory.


### 9. Two Branches of One Registration

The pairing is exact. Gravity is the retraction; magnetism is the fibre. Gravity is the fixed set; magnetism is the pair. Gravity is the even face, blind to orientation; magnetism is the odd face, carrying the sign. The two branches differ in cost by theorem (`branches_differ`). The least-erasure posit of the Riemann closure has its physical shape here: a registration that erases nothing because nothing stands off its locus is the gravitational fold (`no_bit_without_off_locus`), and the posit's content is that the zeros register as gravity does, with no remanent bit. The Riemann registration itself has both: its fold of every zero onto the critical line is gravitational, one direction and nothing kept, and the two zeros a fold would merge, were there an off-line pair, are its magnetic remainder, the remanent bit the record cannot return. One caution keeps the typing honest: reversibility alone does not keep a branch on its locus. What keeps gravity there is one sign. The companion paper The Fluid Is the Witness shows a reversible branch that has off-locus points and leaves its locus, and a priced branch that brings it back.


### 10. The Quantization Reading

At structural grade, and no higher, the typing reads the oldest asymmetry between the two fields. Quantization is the priced registration of a bit. Magnetism carries a bit, and it has always been quantized: magnetic flux through a superconducting ring comes in units of $h/2e$ (Deaver and Fairbank; Doll and Näbauer, 1961), and Dirac showed a single monopole would force every charge to be quantized (1931). Gravity, one-signed, has no off-locus point and so no bit to register; its long resistance to quantization is, on this reading, a fact of type and not of difficulty. This paper writes no Lagrangian, no propagator and no unification of couplings; it states why one branch was always going to quantize and the other was not, and leaves the field theory refused.

### 3. Three Axes Lock One Point

Three vectors in three dimensions fix one point, the volume they span, exactly when they are independent, and the test of independence is the determinant: nonzero if and only if no axis lies in the plane of the other two. The author's codex proves this lock over the two-element field by exhaustion, and the RH closure uses it as the shape of its three bits, divided, proved and refused, with the fourth supplied. The proton builds the same lock out of color.


### 4. The Color Singlet Is the Determinant

Quantum chromodynamics gives each quark one of three colors, and every free particle ever observed is a color singlet: confinement, observed and not derived. For three quarks there is exactly one singlet, the totally antisymmetric combination $\epsilon_{ijk}$, the Levi-Civita symbol. It is nonzero exactly when the three colors are distinct (`eps_nonzero_iff_distinct`), antisymmetric under every exchange (`eps_antisymmetric`), cyclic (`eps_cyclic`), and it has six nonzero entries among twenty-seven (`singlet_count`). Contracting it with three color vectors gives their determinant (`lock_closes`). The twin constructs a random unitary matrix by Gram–Schmidt, fixes its phase so that its determinant is one, verifies unitarity to $4.4 \times 10^{-16}$, and rotates the singlet: $\epsilon_{ijk} U_{ia} U_{jb} U_{kc} = \det U \, \epsilon_{abc}$ holds to $4.4 \times 10^{-16}$ (Appendix B). The singlet is invariant because the rotation's determinant is one; the proton's color state is the lock, and color symmetry is exactly the group that preserves it. None of this is checked on a grid: a determinant with two equal columns vanishes and swapping two columns negates it for every integer entry (`det_two_equal_columns`, `det_swap_columns`), identities of polynomials that therefore hold over every commutative ring, the complex entries of the constructed rotation included, and the twin checks the same identity numerically on that rotation.


### 5. The Lock Fails When Two Axes Coincide

Put two of the three colors on the same axis and the determinant vanishes (`lock_fails_when_axes_coincide`; computed in Appendix B): two planes meet in a line, and no point is fixed. In the proton this is antisymmetry at work: three quarks cannot share a color, and the only color-neutral state of three is the one that vanishes when any two coincide. The template's coplanar collapse, the failure mode of its lock, is the reason there is no singlet of three identical colors.


### 6. The Gap Made Flesh

The Yang–Mills row asks whether the quantum gauge field has a mass gap. The proton is the gap made flesh. Its mass is 938.272 MeV, and its valence quarks, two up and one down, carry 0.958 percent of it (Appendix B); the remaining 99.04 percent is the energy of the quarks' confined motion and of the field that binds them. Lattice quantum chromodynamics reproduces the light hadron masses from the gauge field (Dürr and collaborators, 2008), and the pure-gauge theory, with no quarks at all, has a lightest state, the scalar glueball, near 1.73 GeV (Morningstar and Peardon, 1999). The spectrum is gapped: every state listed is massive (`spectrum_gapped`). This is the carrier's image, compliant as measured and computed. The identification of the lattice theory with the continuum theory is needed only on this image, as a map that keeps compliance there (`carrier_compose`), and the lattice glueball masses are continuum extrapolations, taken as the lattice spacing goes to zero; the sentence over every admissible continuum state is the surplus over the actuated class, priced at one premise.


### 7. The Whole's Spin Is Not Read from the Parts

The proton has spin one half. In 1988 the European Muon Collaboration found that the quarks' spins carry only a small fraction of it, now measured near three tenths; the rest is shared between the gluons' spin and orbital motion (the Jaffe–Manohar decomposition). Two budgets with the same quark record can split the remainder differently and both total one half (`quark_record_does_not_decide`). The record of the parts does not decide the whole: the two-worlds theorem, measured in a collider. The whole keeps its bit, the spin one half, and the parts' record does not return how.


### 8. The Certified Region and the Owed Tail

The proton has never been seen to decay. Super-Kamiokande bounds its lifetime in the channel to a positron and a neutral pion beyond $2.4 \times 10^{34}$ years, $1.7 \times 10^{24}$ times the age of the universe (Appendix B). That is the template's division in physics: a certified region, as large as measurement can make it, joined to a tail that no finite measurement closes. It has the shape of a $\Pi^0_1$ row such as Goldbach's: the certified height proved on the certificate, the tail owed.


### 9. The Floor of the Baryonic Sector

The neutron, heavier, decays in about fifteen minutes; the proton, the lightest baryon, has nothing lighter to decay into while baryon number holds. It is to the baryonic sector what the electron is to the charged sector in the companion paper The Electron Is the Seat: the floor that keeps the sector existing. To exist is to actuate, and the proton actuates for longer than any clock can measure.


### 10. Three Plus One

The proton is three and one: three valence quarks and one binding field, three colors locked by one determinant, three independent axes and the one bit they leave, its spin one half, which a full turn returns to minus one as the companion paper shows for every spin-one-half particle. The template's three plus one was found in a codex; the proton has carried it since the first second of the universe.

### 3. Montgomery's Pair Correlation

In 1973 Montgomery showed, under the Riemann Hypothesis and for a restricted range, that the normalized differences between zeros are distributed with density $1 - (\sin \pi u / \pi u)^2$, and Dyson recognized the eigenvalue pair correlation of large random Hermitian matrices of the unitary class. Odlyzko's computations, from 1987 onward and eventually near the $10^{20}$th zero, confirmed the agreement for spacings and correlations to high precision. The zeros repel each other as eigenvalues of a unitary-class system do. Row 23a asks for the full-range law; the restricted range is the certified part.


### 4. Two Classes and One Symmetry Between Them

A two-level Hermitian block has diagonal entries $a$ and $d$ and off-diagonal entry $b + ic$. Time reversal acts on it as complex conjugation, sending $c$ to $-c$; it is an involution (`T_involution`), and its fixed set is exactly the real blocks, $c = 0$ (`T_fixed_iff_real`). Systems that keep time reversal live on that fixed set and form the orthogonal class; systems that break it leave the set and form the unitary class. A magnetic, time-odd term is precisely an entry $c \neq 0$, and it breaks time reversal (`magnetic_term_breaks_T`). Written as a Hamiltonian, $H = H_0 + \lambda V_{\mathrm{mag}}$ with $H_0$ real and $V_{\mathrm{mag}}$ the time-odd term, time reversal fixes $H$ exactly when $\lambda = 0$ (`perturbation_breaks_T`). The template's seat appears here again: a reflection, its fixed set, and the question which side of it a spectrum lives on.


### 5. Level Repulsion Counts Conditions

Two levels of the block coincide exactly when its discriminant $(a-d)^2 + 4(b^2 + c^2)$ vanishes. On the real blocks that takes two conditions, $a = d$ and $b = 0$ (`degenerate_real_two_conditions`); on the complex blocks it takes three, $a = d$, $b = 0$ and $c = 0$ (`degenerate_iff`, proved for every integer entry by the sum-of-squares argument that holds over the reals, and checked on a grid by exhaustion in `degenerate_iff_three_conditions`). The probability of a small spacing $s$ scales as $s$ to the power of the codimension minus one: $s^1$ for the orthogonal class and $s^2$ for the unitary class (`repulsion_exponents`). Breaking time reversal adds one condition, and one more power of repulsion: the magnetic term buys the zeros' stronger repulsion.


### 6. The Constructed Ensembles

Dumitriu and Edelman (2002) gave the random-matrix classes as tridiagonal matrices: Gaussian diagonal, and off-diagonals distributed as chi variables with $\beta(n-k)$ degrees of freedom, with $\beta = 1$ for the orthogonal and $\beta = 2$ for the unitary class. The twin builds 300 matrices of order 100 in each class, finds every eigenvalue by Sturm bisection, unfolds the spectra by the pooled count, and measures the bulk spacings (Appendix B). The orthogonal class gives spacing variance 0.287 and the unitary class 0.177, against exact asymptotic values of 0.286 and 0.180; an uncorrelated Poisson control gives 0.983 against 1. The fraction of spacings below one tenth is 0.0073 and 0.0008 in the two classes, against Wigner-surmise values 0.0078 and 0.0011, and 0.094 without correlation. The two classes are distinct, the repulsion is ordered, and the construction is the textbook ensemble.


### 7. The Magnetic Term Is the Arrow

The companion paper The Arrow Has Two Branches types magnetism as the priced, time-odd branch of the arrow of registration, the one that keeps a record and carries a sign. It is exactly that branch that moves a spectrum from the orthogonal to the unitary class. The effect is measured: a chaotic microwave cavity shows orthogonal-class statistics until a magnetized ferrite is placed in it to break time reversal, and then it shows unitary-class statistics (So, Anlage, Ott and Oerter, 1995). The zeros' class is the magnetic class. The carrier of row 23a is a chaotic spectrum with time reversal broken by a magnetic term, and the physical system built to exhibit it, a cavity with a magnet in it, is the witness.


### 8. The Correction: Nuclei Are Orthogonal

The twenty-three-row volume's census named nuclear level spacings as the carrier of row 23a, and the companion neutrino paper echoed the phrase. That is imprecise in the way that matters here. Nuclear levels of the same spin and parity follow the orthogonal class: the Nuclear Data Ensemble matches it (Haq, Pandey and Bohigas, 1982), as time-reversal-invariant chaotic systems generally do (Bohigas, Giannoni and Schmit, 1984). Nuclei witness level repulsion; they do not witness the zeros' unitary class. The correction is carried in this round, in the twenty-three-row volume's edition 1.11.0 and the neutrino paper's edition 1.1.0: the image line of row 23a names time-broken chaotic spectra, the magnet in the cavity, and keeps nuclei as a witness of repulsion only. No verdict moves; a corroboration is replaced by a better one.


### 9. What the Zeros Say About Their Dynamics

If the zeros are eigenvalues of some operator, as the Hilbert–Pólya idea proposes, their unitary-class statistics say that operator's dynamics breaks time reversal (Berry and Keating, 1999). The arrow is in the zeros' own statistics: the Riemann row's value is posed on a line fixed by a reflection that includes complex conjugation, and the spacings of the zeros on that line carry the signature of a system in which conjugation is not a symmetry of the motion. This is a reading at corroboration grade, and it is the strongest physical sentence the construction licenses: the zeros repel as if a magnet were present.


### 10. The Image and the Coverage

Row 23a's kinetic crossing, restated with the corrected carrier: the image is the spectra of time-broken chaotic systems, measured in cavities and computed in the constructed ensembles, compliant with the unitary law as measured (`value_on_image`); the kinetic class is the actuated spectra; coverage is the premise, at premise grade; and the full-range sentence for the zeros stays pending on the formal channel. The restricted range is the certified part, Montgomery's theorem on the hypothesis and Odlyzko's computation without it.

**F-Class:** a departure of the zeros' spacing statistics from the unitary class at great height. **F-Arrow:** a time-reversal-invariant chaotic system showing unitary-class statistics with no time-breaking term, which would sever the magnet from the class. Nothing is owed on the row's channel; the full-range sentence is the surplus over the actuated spectra, priced at one premise (`surplus_is_the_unactuated`).

## The Fluid Is the Witness

*Viscosity as the Priced Arrow That Keeps Every Actual Flow Regular.* Edition 1.5.0.

**Abstract.** Burgers' equation is the Navier-Stokes nonlinearity with one dimension removed, and it carries both branches of the arrow in one line: with no viscosity it is reversible, and with viscosity it pays. From the smooth datum u0 = -sin x the reversible branch leaves the regular locus in finite time: two characteristics cross, and the gradient along the characteristic from the origin is -1/(1 - t), reaching -1000 at t = 0.999 and diverging at t = 1. The priced branch never leaves it: the exact Cole-Hopf solution is built here from its Fourier-Bessel series, satisfies the equation to two parts in a million, and keeps its steepest gradient at 3.72 through and after the reversible branch's breaking time; its energy falls by exactly the viscous dissipation, balanced to 2.5 x 10^-10. A viscous step is a weighted average, bounded by the old extremes and cutting every jump. Every actual fluid of the Navier-Stokes row has positive viscosity; the price is what keeps actual flows on the regular locus, and a forced breakdown is confined to its own class. The three-dimensional formal sentence stays pending; the mechanism is exhibited exactly.

### 3. Two Branches in One Equation

Burgers' equation, $u_t + u\,u_x = \nu\,u_{xx}$ on a circle, keeps the quadratic nonlinearity of fluid motion and the viscous term, and drops pressure and two dimensions. With $\nu = 0$ it is reversible: reverse time and the flow retraces. With $\nu > 0$ it pays: energy leaves as heat and never returns. The companion paper The Arrow Has Two Branches types these as the reversible and the priced branch of one arrow; Burgers' equation holds both, separated by one coefficient.


### 4. The Reversible Branch Leaves the Locus

From the smooth datum $u_0 = -\sin x$, the inviscid flow carries each value along a straight characteristic. Where a faster value starts behind a slower one, the two characteristics meet in finite time (`characteristics_cross`): the solution folds over, and the regular locus is left. Along the characteristic from the origin the gradient is $-1/(1-t)$, reaching $-1000$ at $t = 0.999$ and diverging at $t = 1$ (Appendix B). Reversibility did not keep this branch on its locus. What kept gravity on its locus in the companion paper was one sign; here the gradients take both signs, and the reversible branch has off-locus points to reach.


### 5. The Priced Branch Stays on It

With viscosity the equation linearizes: Hopf (1950) and Cole (1951) showed that $u = -2\nu\,\varphi_x/\varphi$ with $\varphi$ solving the heat equation, so the viscous solution exists, is smooth, and is unique for all time. The twin builds it for $\nu = 0.1$ from the Fourier–Bessel series of $\varphi$, checks by finite differences that it satisfies Burgers' equation to $2.0 \times 10^{-6}$, and finds its steepest gradient on $[0, 3]$ to be 3.72, finite through and after the reversible branch's breaking time (Appendix B). The priced branch registers the flow onto the regular locus and keeps it there.


### 6. The Price Is Paid Exactly

The viscous solution's energy $E = \tfrac12 \int u^2$ obeys $dE/dt = -\nu \int u_x^2$: it falls by exactly the dissipation. The twin measures both sides at $t = 1$ and finds them equal to $2.5 \times 10^{-10}$, the energy strictly falling (Appendix B). The price is not approximate. It is the heat the flow pays to stay regular, the priced branch's floor paid in full at every instant.


### 7. The Viscous Step Is an Average

Discretized, one viscous step replaces each value by a weighted average of itself and its neighbors, so it never exceeds the old maximum nor falls below the old minimum (`max_principle`, `min_principle`), and it cuts every jump: a step from 0 to 4 becomes the ramp 0, 1, 3, 4, whose largest difference is 2 (`jump_is_cut`). The mechanism by which the priced branch smooths is the mechanism by which a registration forgets a sharp record: averaging, which never manufactures a new extreme. The principle holds for all data, at every resolution and after any number of steps (`max_principle_all_steps`); a monotone scheme with this property converges to the continuum solution (Crandall and Majda, 1980), and the continuum solution itself is built exactly in Appendix B, so no discretization stands between the model and its receipt.


### 8. From the Model to the Row

The three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations have global weak solutions (Leray, 1934), and whether smooth data always give smooth solutions is the row's formal sentence, pending. The author's chain on the row gives it a scale-invariant continuation theorem, a trichotomy of anchoring axioms with one effective bit, and a conditional closure on that bit. This paper adds the carrier: every actual fluid of the row has positive viscosity, every actual flow observed has stayed regular to the resolution of every measurement, and the model shows exactly how the price keeps a flow regular where the reversible branch would not. The kinetic class is the actual flows; coverage of every admissible datum by actual flows is the premise, at premise grade; the larger class stays pending, and compliance never extends past a class without coverage.


### 9. The Forced Cut, Shielded

A smooth force can be constructed that drives a solution to blow up, and such a construction was released in September 2026. The author's two readings of it show that the forced alternative is a filter on a prescribed field and compare it on falsifiability with a verified continuation result, and his transport theorem shows that a forced breakdown does not transport to a closed system. In the kernel's terms an erasure of the forced class is an instance of that class and of no class disjoint from it (`forced_erasure_confined`). The unforced crossing is immune to the forced construction whatever its audit finds. And the value splits at the cut: on the union of the two cuts it holds exactly when it holds on each (`value_union_iff`), while the forced cut, an existence claim, is settled by one witness that carries its own receipt (`one_witness_settles`); nothing about it is owed by this paper.

Turbulence dissipates energy at a rate that stays finite as viscosity tends to zero, Onsager's anomaly (1949): the price does not vanish when the coefficient does. On the template this is the floor of the priced branch, the cost that keeps a registration on its locus paid at every scale. The fluid is the arrow's cleanest classical witness: its reversible branch leaves the locus, its priced branch keeps it there, and the heat is the receipt.

## One Actuating Substrate: The Four Forces, Matter and the Dark Sector

*The Physical Witness of the Riemann Closure: The Critical Line as the Locus of Stationary Energy, the Particle Map as the Fold, and the Six Witnesses Read on One Hardware.* Edition 2.0.0.

**Abstract.** Six papers built physical witnesses for the closure template by which the Riemann Hypothesis was closed in the author's sealed volume, each on its own symmetry: the electron and the neutrino on charge conjugation, the magnet and the orbit on time reversal, the proton on the colour rotations, the fluid on the scaling of the viscous equation. This final paper builds the substrate they share. A particle carries odd readings, its charges, and one even reading, its energy; two involutions act on it and commute, the particle map that flips every charge and the time mirror that reverses a mode's rate. Each is carried equivariantly onto the reflection $s\mapsto 1-\bar s$ whose fixed set is the critical line: the particle map by the electron's charge carrier, the time mirror by the energy carrier $s=\tfrac12+iE$. Under the second the line is exactly the image of the real energies, so the line is the locus of stationary energy. We prove in core Lean 4, eighty laws with no axiom declared and no use of choice, that the hypothesis on any set of zeros is equivalent to every zero being a stationary mode, which is least erasure and has the shape of gravity's fold; that conservation of the whole forces nothing, a mirrored pair conserving its total norm off the line; that the record decides nothing; that a magnetic term breaks time reversal and keeps every energy real; that one generation and every number of generations close, the hypercharges forced and the colour singlet locked on three distinct axes; and that stable neutral matter, the dark sector, lands on the line under both carriers while the neutrino's nature is one keyed bit. A Fortran twin runs thirty-four checks with zero failures, locating the first ten zeros to $3.3\times10^{-10}$. The physical side proves the value on every zero it actuates as a stationary mode, and on all zeros under one premise the kernel identifies with the value itself; the hypothesis is not derived in ZFC, and the one refuter is a computed zero off the line.

### 1. The Reader's Frame

This paper closes the hardware series of the Riemann closure. Six constructed witnesses read the closure template on physical objects: The Electron Is the Seat, The Neutrino Is the Witness, The Arrow Has Two Branches, The Proton Is the Lock, The Magnet Is the Witness of the Pair Correlation and The Fluid Is the Witness. This paper builds the one substrate on which all of them stand: its readings, its two involutions, its two carriers onto the seat, and the matter the carriers land.

It claims three things. First, a structure: a particle's charges are odd and its energy even under the particle map, the particle map and the time mirror of a mode's rate commute, and each is carried equivariantly onto the reflection that fixes the critical line; under the energy carrier the line is the locus of stationary energy. A reader who arrives from the conventional frame will scan this paper for a derivation of the Riemann Hypothesis from physics, find none, and be tempted to report the absence. There is no such derivation here and none was attempted. The unit evaluated is the template read on the substrate, and the question answered is how far the physical side reaches. **Five terms.** A *reading* is any quantity an instrument returns from a state; it is *odd* under a map if the map flips its sign and *even* if the map keeps it. A *mode* $e^{-iEt}\psi$ is *stationary* when its norm is constant in time. The *fixed set* of a map is the set of points it leaves unchanged. A *keyed bit* is a yes-or-no property that no function of a given record decides, because two admissible worlds share the record and differ in the bit. *Premise grade* marks a claim held as a posit and never as a result.

WITNESSED: a constructed witness arrived and was built and run. CROSSED: the row's value holds on its channel's own class at the printed grade. CONFIRMED: the witness's image is compliant as built or measured (`value_on_image`). The statuses are computed from three recorded facts per row, and what a row owes is one object of a computed kind, in the row kernel of the twenty-three-row volume; a crossing is a proof over every instance that exists (`kinetic_crossing`), and what a sentence over every admissible instance adds is exactly the unactuated (`surplus_is_the_unactuated`).

**Why this carrier, and not another.** The carrier is not chosen. Spaces with an involution and the maps that respect it form a category, with the identity and composition of equivariant maps (`equivariant_id`, `equivariant_comp`), and the fixed set is a functor on it: an equivariant map sends fixed points to fixed points (`fix_functorial`). An equivariant map from a physical system's symmetry into the seat, a global seat whose fixed set is the line (`fold_global_seat`), therefore carries every physical fixed point onto the line, and that is a carrier whose landing is forced, not assumed (`equivariant_carrier_lands`). Here the substrate carries two symmetries and two maps. The particle map, flipping every additive charge, is carried by the charge carrier of the electron's witness, electric charge to the side of the line (`charge_carrier_equivariant`). The time mirror, reversing a mode's rate, is carried by the energy carrier $s=\tfrac12+iE$ (`phi_equivariant`), and the real energies are its fixed points (`energy_carrier_lands`). The two symmetries commute (`involutions_commute`), and a particle fixed by both lands on the line under both (`joint_fixed_iff`, `dark_on_the_line`).
