**Ledger\_Twin.f90**

```fortran
! Ledger_Twin.f90 · the executed twin of SPHYS_Typed_Falsifiability.lean · Fortran 2018.
! Build (sealed): gfortran -std=f2018 -O2 -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off Ledger_Twin.f90
! Reads ledger.dat (code|target|theorem|engine file|paper), one line per falsifier, and the engines in
! the directory engines/: the sixteen hardware-series engines and the hardware paper's, as built, and
! the six witnesses' engines as printed in their published editions (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22986553
! through .22986563). For every falsifier bound to a theorem it confirms the theorem is declared in its
! engine; it recounts the ledger's census by target and by paper.
program ledger_twin
  implicit none
  integer, parameter :: maxl = 100
  character(len=400) :: line
  character(len=40) :: code(maxl), tgt(maxl)
  character(len=80) :: thm(maxl), fil(maxl)
  character(len=120) :: pap(maxl)
  integer :: n, ios, i, p1, p2, p3, p4, nfound, nbound, checks, fails
  integer :: cl, cf, cw, cpo, cc, cpr, j, np, cnt, okp
  character(len=120) :: plist(maxl)
  logical :: seen
  checks = 0; fails = 0; n = 0
  open(10, file='ledger.dat', status='old', action='read')
  do
    read(10, '(a)', iostat=ios) line
    if (ios /= 0) exit
    if (len_trim(line) == 0) cycle
    n = n + 1
    p1 = index(line, '|'); p2 = p1 + index(line(p1+1:), '|'); p3 = p2 + index(line(p2+1:), '|')
    p4 = p3 + index(line(p3+1:), '|')
    code(n) = line(1:p1-1); tgt(n) = line(p1+1:p2-1); thm(n) = line(p2+1:p3-1)
    fil(n) = line(p3+1:p4-1); pap(n) = line(p4+1:)
  end do
  close(10)
  write(*,'(a,i0,a)') 'A · the ledger read: ', n, ' falsifiers'
  nbound = 0; nfound = 0
  do i = 1, n
    if (trim(thm(i)) == '-') cycle
    nbound = nbound + 1
    if (declared(trim(fil(i)), trim(thm(i)))) then
      nfound = nfound + 1
    else
      write(*,'(a,a,a,a)') '  MISSING ', trim(thm(i)), ' in ', trim(fil(i))
    end if
  end do
  write(*,'(a,i0,a,i0)') '  theorems bound: ', nbound, ' ; declared in their engines: ', nfound
  call check('64 falsifiers; 58 bound to a theorem, every one declared in its engine', &
             n == 64 .and. nbound == 58 .and. nfound == 58)
  cl = 0; cf = 0; cw = 0; cpo = 0; cc = 0; cpr = 0
  do i = 1, n
    select case (trim(tgt(i)))
    case ('line'); cl = cl + 1
    case ('fold'); cf = cf + 1
    case ('wall'); cw = cw + 1
    case ('positivity'); cpo = cpo + 1
    case ('count'); cc = cc + 1
    case ('price'); cpr = cpr + 1
    end select
  end do
  write(*,'(a,6i4)') 'B · census by target (line fold wall positivity count price): ', cl, cf, cw, cpo, cc, cpr
  call check('the census matches the engine: 18, 13, 11, 9, 8, 5', cl == 18 .and. cf == 13 .and. cw == 11 .and. &
             cpo == 9 .and. cc == 8 .and. cpr == 5)
  np = 0
  do i = 1, n
    seen = .false.
    do j = 1, np
      if (trim(plist(j)) == trim(pap(i))) seen = .true.
    end do
    if (.not. seen) then
      np = np + 1; plist(np) = pap(i)
    end if
  end do
  okp = 0
  do j = 1, np
    cnt = 0
    do i = 1, n
      if (trim(pap(i)) == trim(plist(j))) cnt = cnt + 1
    end do
    if (cnt >= 2 .and. cnt <= 4) okp = okp + 1
  end do
  write(*,'(a,i0,a)') 'C · ', np, ' papers'
  call check('22 papers, each carrying two to four falsifiers', np == 22 .and. okp == 22)
  write(*,'(a,i0,a,i0,a)') ' BATTERY-JSON: {"checks":', checks, ',"failures":', fails, '}'
  if (fails > 0) error stop 1
contains
  subroutine check(name, ok)
    character(*), intent(in) :: name
    logical, intent(in) :: ok
    checks = checks + 1
    if (.not. ok) fails = fails + 1
    write(*,'(a,a)') merge('  PASS  ', '  FAIL  ', ok), name
  end subroutine check
  logical function declared(fname, tname) result(found)
    character(*), intent(in) :: fname, tname
    character(len=2000) :: buf
    integer :: u, ios2, k, e
    found = .false.
    open(newunit=u, file='engines/'//fname, status='old', action='read', iostat=ios2)
    if (ios2 /= 0) return
    do
      read(u, '(a)', iostat=ios2) buf
      if (ios2 /= 0) exit
      k = index(buf, 'theorem '//tname)
      if (k > 0) then
        e = k + 8 + len(tname)
        if (e > len_trim(buf)) then
          found = .true.
        else if (buf(e:e) == ' ' .or. buf(e:e) == '(' .or. buf(e:e) == ':' .or. buf(e:e) == '{') then
          found = .true.
        end if
      end if
      if (found) exit
    end do
    close(u)
  end function declared
end program ledger_twin
```

# Appendix VIII · The Fortification's Engine and Twin

**SPHYS\_Fortification.lean**

```lean
/-
  SPHYS_Fortification.lean · the fortification of Nothing Escapes Least Erasure, edition 1.2.0.
  Core Lean 4.19.0, standalone, no import, no library, no axiom declared.

  Part A reprints, at resolution two and over configurations inside the open strip, the refusals the apex
  carries at resolution one with its twin pair on the edge of the strip: admissible coalitions of any depth,
  certified heights, and the keyedness of the Weil and Li faces. The chart, the strip worlds, the record
  and the inner pair are the apex's own definitions (Every_Prime_3_1_1.lean, Section 15), copied verbatim.
  Part B lands the charge carrier strictly inside the strip. Part C types the ledger's crossing token by
  channel, instance class and grade. Part D restricts the escape from the dot to non-identity involutions.
  Part E separates the two senses of magnitude the volume uses.
-/
set_option autoImplicit false
namespace SPHYS.Fortify

/-! ## Part A · The strip at resolution two (definitions verbatim from the apex) -/

structure Pt where
  x : Int
  t : Nat
deriving DecidableEq

abbrev World := Pt → Prop

def fold₂ (z : Pt) : Pt := ⟨4 - z.x, z.t⟩
def reg₂ (z : Pt) : Pt := ⟨2, z.t⟩
def onLine₂ (z : Pt) : Prop := z.x = 2
def InStrip₂ (z : Pt) : Prop := 0 < z.x ∧ z.x < 4
def StripWorld₂ (Z : World) : Prop := (∀ z, Z z → Z (fold₂ z)) ∧ ∀ z, Z z → InStrip₂ z
def RH₂ (Z : World) : Prop := ∀ z, Z z → onLine₂ z
def SameRecord₂ (Z Z' : World) : Prop := ∀ r, (∃ s, Z s ∧ reg₂ s = r) ↔ (∃ s, Z' s ∧ reg₂ s = r)
def RespectsRecord₂ (A : World → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ Z Z', StripWorld₂ Z → StripWorld₂ Z' → SameRecord₂ Z Z' → (A Z ↔ A Z')
def Forces₂ (A : World → Prop) : Prop := ∀ Z, StripWorld₂ Z → A Z → RH₂ Z

def innerPair₂ (t : Nat) : World := fun w => w = ⟨1, t⟩ ∨ w = ⟨3, t⟩
def withPair₂ (Z : World) (t : Nat) : World := fun w => Z w ∨ w = ⟨1, t⟩ ∨ w = ⟨3, t⟩
/-- The line world at height t: one zero on the line. -/
def lineWorld₂ (t : Nat) : World := fun w => w = ⟨2, t⟩

theorem inStrip_one (t : Nat) : InStrip₂ ⟨1, t⟩ := ⟨show (0 : Int) < 1 by decide, show (1 : Int) < 4 by decide⟩
theorem inStrip_two (t : Nat) : InStrip₂ ⟨2, t⟩ := ⟨show (0 : Int) < 2 by decide, show (2 : Int) < 4 by decide⟩
theorem inStrip_three (t : Nat) : InStrip₂ ⟨3, t⟩ := ⟨show (0 : Int) < 3 by decide, show (3 : Int) < 4 by decide⟩

theorem innerPair₂_strip (t : Nat) : StripWorld₂ (innerPair₂ t) := by
  refine ⟨fun w hw => ?_, fun w hw => ?_⟩
  · rcases hw with h | h
    · subst h; exact Or.inr rfl
    · subst h; exact Or.inl rfl
  · rcases hw with h | h
    · subst h; exact inStrip_one t
    · subst h; exact inStrip_three t

theorem innerPair₂_not_rh (t : Nat) : ¬ RH₂ (innerPair₂ t) := by
  intro h
  have e : (1 : Int) = 2 := h ⟨1, t⟩ (Or.inl rfl)
  exact absurd e (by decide)

theorem lineWorld₂_strip (t : Nat) : StripWorld₂ (lineWorld₂ t) :=
  ⟨fun w hw => by rw [hw]; rfl, fun w hw => by rw [hw]; exact inStrip_two t⟩

theorem lineWorld₂_rh (t : Nat) : RH₂ (lineWorld₂ t) := fun w hw => by rw [hw]; rfl

theorem line_and_pair_same_record (t : Nat) : SameRecord₂ (lineWorld₂ t) (innerPair₂ t) := by
  intro r
  constructor
  · intro ⟨s, hs, hsr⟩
    subst hs
    exact ⟨⟨1, t⟩, Or.inl rfl, hsr⟩
  · intro ⟨s, hs, hsr⟩
    rcases hs with h | h
    · subst h; exact ⟨⟨2, t⟩, rfl, hsr⟩
    · subst h; exact ⟨⟨2, t⟩, rfl, hsr⟩

/-- No reading that respects the record decides the hypothesis on strip configurations (the apex's
    `no_reading_decides_in_the_strip`, re-proved here on the line world and the inner pair). -/
theorem no_reading_decides₂ (g : World → Prop) (hg : RespectsRecord₂ g) :
    ¬ ∀ Z, StripWorld₂ Z → (g Z ↔ RH₂ Z) := by
  intro h
  have hl := (h _ (lineWorld₂_strip 14)).mpr (lineWorld₂_rh 14)
  have hp := (hg _ _ (lineWorld₂_strip 14) (innerPair₂_strip 14) (line_and_pair_same_record 14)).mp hl
  exact innerPair₂_not_rh 14 ((h _ (innerPair₂_strip 14)).mp hp)

/-! ### A.1 · Admissible coalitions inside the strip -/

/-- Keyless on the strip: true on every strip configuration. -/
def Keyless₂ (A : World → Prop) : Prop := ∀ Z, StripWorld₂ Z → A Z
/-- Admissible inside the strip: keyless there, or a reading of the record there. -/
def Admissible₂ (A : World → Prop) : Prop := Keyless₂ A ∨ RespectsRecord₂ A

theorem admissible₂_true : Admissible₂ (fun _ => True) := Or.inl (fun _ _ => trivial)
theorem admissible₂_false : Admissible₂ (fun _ => False) := Or.inr (fun _ _ _ _ _ => Iff.rfl)

theorem admissible₂_not (A : World → Prop) (h : Admissible₂ A) : Admissible₂ (fun Z => ¬ A Z) := by
  rcases h with k | r
  · exact Or.inr (fun Z Z' hZ hZ' _ => ⟨fun hn => absurd (k Z hZ) hn, fun hn => absurd (k Z' hZ') hn⟩)
  · exact Or.inr (fun Z Z' hZ hZ' hs =>
      ⟨fun hn ha => hn ((r Z Z' hZ hZ' hs).mpr ha), fun hn ha => hn ((r Z Z' hZ hZ' hs).mp ha)⟩)

theorem admissible₂_and (A B : World → Prop) (ha : Admissible₂ A) (hb : Admissible₂ B) :
    Admissible₂ (fun Z => A Z ∧ B Z) := by
  rcases ha with ka | ra <;> rcases hb with kb | rb
  · exact Or.inl (fun Z hZ => ⟨ka Z hZ, kb Z hZ⟩)
  · exact Or.inr (fun Z Z' hZ hZ' hs =>
      ⟨fun p => ⟨ka Z' hZ', (rb Z Z' hZ hZ' hs).mp p.2⟩, fun p => ⟨ka Z hZ, (rb Z Z' hZ hZ' hs).mpr p.2⟩⟩)
  · exact Or.inr (fun Z Z' hZ hZ' hs =>
      ⟨fun p => ⟨(ra Z Z' hZ hZ' hs).mp p.1, kb Z' hZ'⟩, fun p => ⟨(ra Z Z' hZ hZ' hs).mpr p.1, kb Z hZ⟩⟩)
  · exact Or.inr (fun Z Z' hZ hZ' hs =>
      ⟨fun p => ⟨(ra Z Z' hZ hZ' hs).mp p.1, (rb Z Z' hZ hZ' hs).mp p.2⟩,
       fun p => ⟨(ra Z Z' hZ hZ' hs).mpr p.1, (rb Z Z' hZ hZ' hs).mpr p.2⟩⟩)

theorem admissible₂_or (A B : World → Prop) (ha : Admissible₂ A) (hb : Admissible₂ B) :
    Admissible₂ (fun Z => A Z ∨ B Z) := by
  rcases ha with ka | ra
  · exact Or.inl (fun Z hZ => Or.inl (ka Z hZ))
  · rcases hb with kb | rb
    · exact Or.inl (fun Z hZ => Or.inr (kb Z hZ))
    · exact Or.inr (fun Z Z' hZ hZ' hs =>
        ⟨fun p => p.elim (fun a => Or.inl ((ra Z Z' hZ hZ' hs).mp a)) (fun b => Or.inr ((rb Z Z' hZ hZ' hs).mp b)),
         fun p => p.elim (fun a => Or.inl ((ra Z Z' hZ hZ' hs).mpr a)) (fun b => Or.inr ((rb Z Z' hZ hZ' hs).mpr b))⟩)

/-- A coalition: any Boolean combination of atomic premises, of any depth (the apex's definition). -/
inductive Coalition (ι : Type) where
  | atom : ι → Coalition ι
  | top : Coalition ι
  | bot : Coalition ι
  | not : Coalition ι → Coalition ι
  | and : Coalition ι → Coalition ι → Coalition ι
  | or : Coalition ι → Coalition ι → Coalition ι

def Coalition.eval {ι : Type} (at_ : ι → World → Prop) : Coalition ι → World → Prop
  | .atom i => at_ i
  | .top => fun _ => True
  | .bot => fun _ => False
  | .not c => fun Z => ¬ Coalition.eval at_ c Z
  | .and c d => fun Z => Coalition.eval at_ c Z ∧ Coalition.eval at_ d Z
  | .or c d => fun Z => Coalition.eval at_ c Z ∨ Coalition.eval at_ d Z

theorem coalition_admissible₂ {ι : Type} (at_ : ι → World → Prop) (h : ∀ i, Admissible₂ (at_ i)) :
    ∀ c : Coalition ι, Admissible₂ (Coalition.eval at_ c) := by
  intro c
  induction c with
  | atom i => exact h i
  | top => exact admissible₂_true
  | bot => exact admissible₂_false
  | not c ih => exact admissible₂_not _ ih
  | and c d ihc ihd => exact admissible₂_and _ _ ihc ihd
  | or c d ihc ihd => exact admissible₂_or _ _ ihc ihd

/-- No admissible premise decides the hypothesis on strip configurations. -/
theorem admissible₂_never_decides (A : World → Prop) (h : Admissible₂ A) :
    ¬ ∀ Z, StripWorld₂ Z → (A Z ↔ RH₂ Z) := by
  intro hd
  rcases h with k | r
  · exact innerPair₂_not_rh 0 ((hd _ (innerPair₂_strip 0)).mp (k _ (innerPair₂_strip 0)))
  · exact no_reading_decides₂ A r hd

/-- **No coalition decides inside the strip.** No Boolean combination of admissible premises, of any depth,
    agrees with the hypothesis on every configuration inside the open strip. -/
theorem no_coalition_decides₂ {ι : Type} (at_ : ι → World → Prop) (h : ∀ i, Admissible₂ (at_ i))
    (c : Coalition ι) : ¬ ∀ Z, StripWorld₂ Z → (Coalition.eval at_ c Z ↔ RH₂ Z) :=
  admissible₂_never_decides _ (coalition_admissible₂ at_ h c)

/-! ### A.2 · Certified heights inside the strip -/

def LineBelow₂ (T : Nat) : World := fun z => z.x = 2 ∧ z.t ≤ T
def TwinAbove₂ (T : Nat) : World := fun z => (z.x = 2 ∧ z.t ≤ T) ∨ (z = ⟨1, T+1⟩ ∨ z = ⟨3, T+1⟩)

/-- **The certified height never forces, inside the strip.** For every height T the world certified on the
    line to T and a strip world carrying the inner pair just above T are both strip configurations, agree at
    every height up to T, and differ on the hypothesis. -/
theorem certified_height_never_forces₂ (T : Nat) :
    StripWorld₂ (LineBelow₂ T) ∧ RH₂ (LineBelow₂ T) ∧ StripWorld₂ (TwinAbove₂ T) ∧ ¬ RH₂ (TwinAbove₂ T) ∧
    ∀ z, z.t ≤ T → (TwinAbove₂ T z ↔ LineBelow₂ T z) := by
  refine ⟨⟨fun z hz => ?_, fun z hz => ?_⟩, fun z hz => hz.1, ⟨fun z hz => ?_, fun z hz => ?_⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact ⟨show 4 - z.x = 2 by rw [hz.1]; decide, hz.2⟩
  · exact ⟨by rw [hz.1]; decide, by rw [hz.1]; decide⟩
  · rcases hz with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | h | h
    · exact Or.inl ⟨show 4 - z.x = 2 by rw [h1]; decide, h2⟩
    · subst h; exact Or.inr (Or.inr rfl)
    · subst h; exact Or.inr (Or.inl rfl)
  · rcases hz with ⟨h1, _⟩ | h | h
    · exact ⟨by rw [h1]; decide, by rw [h1]; decide⟩
    · subst h; exact inStrip_one (T+1)
    · subst h; exact inStrip_three (T+1)
  · intro h
    have e : (1 : Int) = 2 := h ⟨1, T+1⟩ (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl))
    exact absurd e (by decide)
  · intro z hz
    constructor
    · intro h
      rcases h with h | h | h
      · exact h
      · subst h; exact absurd (show T + 1 ≤ T from hz) (Nat.not_succ_le_self T)
      · subst h; exact absurd (show T + 1 ≤ T from hz) (Nat.not_succ_le_self T)
    · intro h; exact Or.inl h

/-- A premise reads only below T when it takes one value on configurations agreeing at every height up to T. -/
def ReadsBelow₂ (T : Nat) (A : World → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ Z Z', (∀ z, z.t ≤ T → (Z z ↔ Z' z)) → (A Z ↔ A Z')

/-- No premise that reads only below a certified height decides the hypothesis inside the strip. -/
theorem no_height_reading_decides₂ (T : Nat) (A : World → Prop) (hA : ReadsBelow₂ T A) :
    ¬ ∀ Z, StripWorld₂ Z → (A Z ↔ RH₂ Z) := by
  intro h
  have ⟨s1, r1, s2, n2, agree⟩ := certified_height_never_forces₂ T
  have a1 := (h _ s1).mpr r1
  have a2 := (hA (LineBelow₂ T) (TwinAbove₂ T) (fun z hz => (agree z hz).symm)).mp a1
  exact n2 ((h _ s2).mp a2)

/-! ### A.3 · The Weil and Li faces, keyed inside the strip -/

/-- The explicit formula at resolution two: the apex's structure with its zero set on the strip chart.
    Weil's criterion is carried as a field, as in the apex (Weil 1952; Bombieri 2000). -/
structure ExplicitFormula₂ where
  V : Type
  le : V → V → Prop
  zero : V
  T : Type
  adj : T → T
  conv : T → T → T
  primeSide : T → V
  zeroSide : T → V
  zeros : World
  identity : ∀ g, zeroSide g = primeSide g
  positivity_iff_line : (∀ g, le zero (primeSide (conv g (adj g)))) ↔ RH₂ zeros

def WeilPositive₂ (E : ExplicitFormula₂) : Prop := ∀ g, E.le E.zero (E.primeSide (E.conv g (E.adj g)))

def positiveInstance₂ : ExplicitFormula₂ where
  V := Int
  le := fun a b => a ≤ b
  zero := 0
  T := Unit
  adj := id
  conv := fun _ _ => ()
  primeSide := fun _ => 0
  zeroSide := fun _ => 0
  zeros := lineWorld₂ 14
  identity := fun _ => rfl
  positivity_iff_line := ⟨fun _ => lineWorld₂_rh 14, fun _ _ => Int.le_refl 0⟩

def negativeInstance₂ : ExplicitFormula₂ where
  V := Int
  le := fun a b => a ≤ b
  zero := 0
  T := Unit
  adj := id
  conv := fun _ _ => ()
  primeSide := fun _ => -1
  zeroSide := fun _ => -1
  zeros := innerPair₂ 14
  identity := fun _ => rfl
  positivity_iff_line :=
    ⟨fun h => absurd (h ()) (by decide : ¬ ((0 : Int) ≤ -1)), fun h => absurd h (innerPair₂_not_rh 14)⟩

/-- **The Weil face is keyed inside the strip.** Two explicit formulas satisfy every field, their zero sets
    are strip configurations with one record, and one is positive with its zeros on the line while the other
    is not: positivity reads the bit, and the record does not. -/
theorem weil_keyed_in_the_strip :
    StripWorld₂ positiveInstance₂.zeros ∧ StripWorld₂ negativeInstance₂.zeros ∧
    SameRecord₂ positiveInstance₂.zeros negativeInstance₂.zeros ∧
    WeilPositive₂ positiveInstance₂ ∧ ¬ WeilPositive₂ negativeInstance₂ :=
  ⟨lineWorld₂_strip 14, innerPair₂_strip 14, line_and_pair_same_record 14,
   fun _ => Int.le_refl 0, fun h => absurd (h ()) (by decide : ¬ ((0 : Int) ≤ -1))⟩

/-- The Li stream at resolution two: the apex's structure with its zero set on the strip chart. -/
structure LiStream₂ where
  zeros : World
  nonneg : Nat → Prop
  li : RH₂ zeros ↔ ∀ n, 1 ≤ n → nonneg n

/-- **The Li face is keyed inside the strip, and no prefix forces.** For every N a Li stream non-negative below
    N has its zero set at the inner pair, inside the open strip and off the line; and a stream with its zeros
    on the line, of the same record, is non-negative throughout. -/
theorem li_keyed_in_the_strip (N : Nat) :
    ∃ L L' : LiStream₂, StripWorld₂ L.zeros ∧ StripWorld₂ L'.zeros ∧ SameRecord₂ L'.zeros L.zeros ∧
      (∀ n, n < N → L.nonneg n) ∧ ¬ RH₂ L.zeros ∧ (∀ n, 1 ≤ n → L'.nonneg n) :=
  ⟨⟨innerPair₂ 14, fun n => n < N,
     ⟨fun h => absurd h (innerPair₂_not_rh 14),
      fun h => absurd (h (N + 1) (Nat.succ_pos N)) (fun c => Nat.lt_irrefl N (Nat.lt_trans (Nat.lt_succ_self N) c))⟩⟩,
   ⟨lineWorld₂ 14, fun _ => True, ⟨fun _ _ _ => trivial, fun _ => lineWorld₂_rh 14⟩⟩,
   innerPair₂_strip 14, lineWorld₂_strip 14, line_and_pair_same_record 14,
   fun _ h => h, innerPair₂_not_rh 14, fun _ _ => trivial⟩

/-! ## Part B · The charge carrier, strictly inside the strip

  Resolution twelve: x = 12 Re s, the line x = 6, the fold x ↦ 12 − x, the open strip 0 < x < 12.
  Charge Q is counted in thirds of the electron's charge, so every quark and lepton charge is an integer
  with |Q| ≤ 3. The carrier is x = 6 + Q. -/

def carrier (Q : Int) : Int := 6 + Q
def foldX (x : Int) : Int := 12 - x

theorem carrier_equivariant (Q : Int) : foldX (carrier Q) = carrier (-Q) := by
  unfold foldX carrier; omega

theorem neutral_on_the_line : carrier 0 = 6 := rfl

/-- **Every quark and lepton charge, |Q| ≤ 3 in thirds of e, lands strictly inside the strip, never on its edges.** -/
theorem charges_inside_the_strip (Q : Int) (h1 : -3 ≤ Q) (h2 : Q ≤ 3) :
    0 < carrier Q ∧ carrier Q < 12 ∧ carrier Q ≠ 0 ∧ carrier Q ≠ 12 := by
  have a : 0 < carrier Q := by unfold carrier; omega
  have b : carrier Q < 12 := by unfold carrier; omega
  exact ⟨a, b, Int.ne_of_gt a, Int.ne_of_lt b⟩

/-- The electron lands at real part one quarter, the positron at three quarters. -/
theorem pair_at_the_quarters : carrier (-3) = 3 ∧ carrier 3 = 9 := ⟨rfl, rfl⟩

/-- **The carrier is forced up to one bit.** Among the integer carriers x = 6 + kQ, which are all
    equivariant and land the neutral on the line, exactly two keep every quark and lepton charge strictly inside the
    open strip without collapsing it onto the line: k = 1 and k = −1, exchanged by the orientation. -/
theorem carrier_forced_up_to_the_bit (k : Int) :
    (k ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ Q : Int, -3 ≤ Q → Q ≤ 3 → 0 < 6 + k * Q ∧ 6 + k * Q < 12) ↔ (k = 1 ∨ k = -1) := by
  constructor
  · intro ⟨hk, h⟩
    have a := h 3 (by decide) (by decide)
    have a1 := a.1
    have a2 := a.2
    have lo : -2 < k := by clear hk h a; omega
    have hi : k < 2 := by clear hk h a; omega
    rcases Int.lt_or_gt_of_ne hk with n | p
    · exact Or.inr (by clear hk h a a1 a2; omega)
    · exact Or.inl (by clear hk h a a1 a2; omega)
  · intro h
    rcases h with h | h
    · subst h
      exact ⟨by decide, fun Q h1 h2 => ⟨by omega, by omega⟩⟩
    · subst h
      exact ⟨by decide, fun Q h1 h2 => ⟨by omega, by omega⟩⟩

theorem carriers_all_equivariant (k Q : Int) : foldX (6 + k * Q) = 6 + k * (-Q) := by
  unfold foldX; rw [Int.mul_neg]; omega

/-- The resolution-one carrier, real part (1 + q)/2 on the doubled chart h = 1 + q, lands the electron on the
    edge h = 0: the reason it is retired as a carrier of the Riemann seat. -/
theorem resolution_one_carrier_on_the_edge : (1 : Int) + (-1) = 0 ∧ (1 : Int) + 1 = 2 := ⟨rfl, rfl⟩

/-- **Every finite charge spectrum lands inside the strip at a fine enough resolution.** At resolution 2c, the
    line x = c, the fold x ↦ 2c − x and the carrier x = c + Q, every state of charge Q with |Q| ≤ M, counted in
    thirds of the electron's charge, lands strictly inside the open strip 0 < x < 2c whenever M < c, and the
    carrier is equivariant there. -/
theorem carrier_inside_at_resolution (c M : Int) (hc : M < c) (Q : Int) (h1 : -M ≤ Q) (h2 : Q ≤ M) :
    0 < c + Q ∧ c + Q < 2 * c ∧ 2 * c - (c + Q) = c + (-Q) :=
  ⟨by omega, by omega, by omega⟩

/-- A state of charge 2e, Q = 6, reaches the edge x = 12 at resolution twelve, and lands inside from resolution
    fourteen on: the resolution-twelve carrier is the carrier of the quark and lepton charges. -/
theorem doubly_charged_at_resolution_twelve_and_fourteen :
    (6 : Int) + 6 = 12 ∧ (0 : Int) < 7 + 6 ∧ (7 : Int) + 6 < 2 * 7 := ⟨rfl, by decide, by decide⟩

/-- **The family is every affine carrier.** An affine integer carrier x = a + kQ that is equivariant for charge
    conjugation and the fold x ↦ 12 − x has a = 6, so it lies in the family x = 6 + kQ: within the affine
    equivariant carriers the carrier is forced up to the one bit. Among equivariant maps at large it is not unique. -/
theorem affine_equivariant_is_the_family (a k : Int) (h : ∀ Q : Int, foldX (a + k * Q) = a + k * (-Q)) : a = 6 := by
  have h0 := h 0
  simp only [foldX, Int.mul_zero, Int.neg_zero, Int.add_zero] at h0
  omega

/-- The resolution-one map, real part (1 + q)/2 on the doubled chart: h = 1 + q, the fold h ↦ 2 − h, the line h = 1. -/
def res1 (q : Int) : Int := 1 + q

/-- **The two charge carriers agree on every verdict the series reads.** For every charge q in units of e, the
    resolution-one map and the resolution-twelve map, Q = 3q, put the same states on the line, and each sends the
    charge-conjugate state to the fold partner. The verdicts the carried engines execute read only these two facts,
    so they transport unchanged; only the position on the edge, which no verdict reads, is withdrawn. -/
theorem carriers_agree_on_the_verdict (q : Int) :
    (res1 q = 1 ↔ carrier (3 * q) = 6) ∧ 2 - res1 q = res1 (-q) ∧ foldX (carrier (3 * q)) = carrier (3 * (-q)) := by
  refine ⟨⟨fun h => ?_, fun h => ?_⟩, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> (try unfold res1 at *) <;> (try unfold carrier at *) <;>
    (try unfold foldX at *) <;> omega

/-! ## Part C · The crossing token, typed -/

inductive Channel where | formal | kinetic deriving DecidableEq, Repr
inductive InstanceClass where | every | actuated | image deriving DecidableEq, Repr
inductive Grade where | theorem_ | structural | corroboration | premise deriving DecidableEq, Repr

structure Crossing where
  channel : Channel
  cls : InstanceClass
  grade : Grade
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

def Channel.code : Channel → Nat | .formal => 0 | .kinetic => 1
def InstanceClass.code : InstanceClass → Nat | .every => 0 | .actuated => 1 | .image => 2
def Grade.code : Grade → Nat | .theorem_ => 0 | .structural => 1 | .corroboration => 2 | .premise => 3
/-- The printed token, as a code: channel, class and grade each in its own digit. -/
def Crossing.code (c : Crossing) : Nat := c.channel.code * 100 + c.cls.code * 10 + c.grade.code

def allCrossings : List Crossing :=
  [Channel.formal, .kinetic].flatMap fun ch =>
  [InstanceClass.every, .actuated, .image].flatMap fun cl =>
  [Grade.theorem_, .structural, .corroboration, .premise].map fun g => ⟨ch, cl, g⟩

/-- **The token is injective**: two crossings print the same token only when channel, class and grade all
    agree, so no reading of a printed token confuses a kinetic crossing at premise grade with a formal one. -/
theorem token_injective :
    allCrossings.all (fun a => allCrossings.all (fun b => decide (a.code = b.code) == decide (a = b))) = true := by
  decide

theorem crossings_enumerated : allCrossings.length = 24 := by decide

/-- The five crossed rows of the twenty-three, as the ledger types them. -/
def crossedRows : List (String × Crossing) :=
  [("2 · Riemann Hypothesis", ⟨.kinetic, .actuated, .premise⟩),
   ("3a · Navier–Stokes, unforced", ⟨.kinetic, .actuated, .premise⟩),
   ("4 · Yang–Mills mass gap", ⟨.kinetic, .image, .premise⟩),
   ("7 · Poincaré", ⟨.formal, .every, .theorem_⟩),
   ("23a · pair correlation", ⟨.kinetic, .image, .premise⟩)]

/-- **Exactly one crossed row is formal, over every instance, at theorem grade, and it is Poincaré**; every
    kinetic crossing stands at premise grade on its actuated class or its image. -/
theorem one_formal_crossing :
    (crossedRows.filter (fun r => r.2 == ⟨.formal, .every, .theorem_⟩)).length = 1 ∧
    crossedRows.all (fun r => r.2.channel != .kinetic || (r.2.grade == .premise && r.2.cls != .every)) = true := by
  decide

/-! ## Part D · The dot, and the one way off it

  An angle in degrees, 0 ≤ θ < 360. The reflection θ ↦ −θ is an involution that is not the identity, and it
  fixes exactly 0 and 180. -/

def refl (θ : Nat) : Nat := (360 - θ % 360) % 360

set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in
theorem refl_involution : ∀ θ, θ < 360 → refl (refl θ) = θ := by decide
theorem refl_not_identity : refl 90 = 270 := by decide
set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in
theorem refl_fixed_points : ∀ θ, θ < 360 → (refl θ = θ ↔ θ = 0 ∨ θ = 180) := by decide

/-- The escape from the dot: a non-identity involution of the theory that fixes the magnitude. -/
structure Escape (m : Nat) where
  τ : Nat → Nat
  involutive : ∀ θ, θ < 360 → τ (τ θ) = θ
  not_identity : ∃ θ, θ < 360 ∧ τ θ ≠ θ
  fixes : τ m = m

/-- The strong angle at 0 escapes the dot by the reflection. -/
def strongAngleEscape : Escape 0 := ⟨refl, refl_involution, ⟨90, by decide, by decide⟩, by decide⟩

/-- **The identity grants no escape**: no escape's involution is the identity. -/
theorem identity_never_escapes (m : Nat) (e : Escape m) : e.τ ≠ id := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨θ, _, hθ⟩ := e.not_identity
  exact hθ (by rw [h]; rfl)

/-! ## Part E · The two senses of magnitude

  The lock scalar is blind to the sign: reflecting the offset leaves its square unchanged. The line verdict is
  blind to the scale: rescaling the offset by any nonzero factor leaves it on or off the line. Both hold at once,
  so "the seat reads magnitude and never sign" (of the lock) and "no functional of the line returns a scale"
  (of the verdict) are two theorems, not one claim and its negation. -/

theorem sign_blind (d : Int) : (-d) * (-d) = d * d := Int.neg_mul_neg d d

theorem scale_blind (k d : Int) (hk : k ≠ 0) : k * d = 0 ↔ d = 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    rcases Int.mul_eq_zero.mp h with h | h
    · exact absurd h hk
    · exact h
  · intro h; rw [h, Int.mul_zero]

theorem two_blindnesses (d k : Int) (hk : k ≠ 0) : (-d) * (-d) = d * d ∧ (k * d = 0 ↔ d = 0) :=
  ⟨sign_blind d, scale_blind k d hk⟩

/-- **The fortification, whole.** -/
theorem fortification :
    (∀ (ι : Type) (at_ : ι → World → Prop), (∀ i, Admissible₂ (at_ i)) →
      ∀ c : Coalition ι, ¬ ∀ Z, StripWorld₂ Z → (Coalition.eval at_ c Z ↔ RH₂ Z)) ∧
    (∀ T, StripWorld₂ (TwinAbove₂ T) ∧ ¬ RH₂ (TwinAbove₂ T)) ∧
    (WeilPositive₂ positiveInstance₂ ∧ ¬ WeilPositive₂ negativeInstance₂) ∧
    (∀ Q : Int, -3 ≤ Q → Q ≤ 3 → 0 < carrier Q ∧ carrier Q < 12) ∧
    (∀ k : Int, (k ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ Q : Int, -3 ≤ Q → Q ≤ 3 → 0 < 6 + k * Q ∧ 6 + k * Q < 12) ↔ (k = 1 ∨ k = -1)) :=
  ⟨fun _ at_ h c => no_coalition_decides₂ at_ h c,
   fun T => ⟨(certified_height_never_forces₂ T).2.2.1, (certified_height_never_forces₂ T).2.2.2.1⟩,
   ⟨weil_keyed_in_the_strip.2.2.2.1, weil_keyed_in_the_strip.2.2.2.2⟩,
   fun Q h1 h2 => ⟨(charges_inside_the_strip Q h1 h2).1, (charges_inside_the_strip Q h1 h2).2.1⟩,
   carrier_forced_up_to_the_bit⟩

end SPHYS.Fortify
```

```fortran
! Fortification_Twin.f90 · the twin of SPHYS_Fortification.lean · Fortran 2018.
! Build (sealed): gfortran -std=f2018 -O2 -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off Fortification_Twin.f90
! Resolution two: x = 4 Re s, line x = 2, fold x -> 4 - x, open strip 0 < x < 4, registration (x,t) -> (2,t).
! A1 no function of the record decides the value on strip worlds: all 256 record readings tried, exhaustively.
! A2 the certified height never forces, inside the strip, for every height to 60.
! A3 a positivity functional is keyed inside the strip: it equals the value and differs within one record.
! B  the charge carrier at resolution twelve: every quark and lepton charge inside the strip; exactly two scales
!    admissible; and at every resolution 2c every charge spectrum |Q| <= M with M < c lands inside, Q = c on the edge.
! C  the crossing token is injective on all 24 crossings; one crossed row is formal at theorem grade.
! D  the reflection of angles fixes exactly 0 and 180 and is not the identity.
! E  the lock is sign-blind and the line verdict scale-blind, together.
program fortification_twin
  implicit none
  integer :: checks, fails
  checks = 0; fails = 0
  call a1(); call a2(); call a3(); call blk_b(); call blk_b3(); call blk_c(); call blk_d(); call blk_e()
  write(*,'(a,i0,a,i0,a)') ' BATTERY-JSON: {"checks":', checks, ',"failures":', fails, '}'
  if (fails > 0) error stop 1
contains
  subroutine check(name, ok)
    character(*), intent(in) :: name
    logical, intent(in) :: ok
    checks = checks + 1
    if (.not. ok) fails = fails + 1
    write(*,'(a,a)') merge('  PASS  ', '  FAIL  ', ok), name
  end subroutine check
  ! a world is a 9-bit mask over the points (x,t), x in 1..3, t in 1..3; bit index 3*(t-1)+(x-1)
  pure logical function has(m, x, t)
    integer, intent(in) :: m, x, t
    has = btest(m, 3*(t-1) + (x-1))
  end function has
  pure logical function stripworld(m)
    integer, intent(in) :: m
    integer :: t
    stripworld = .true.
    do t = 1, 3
      if (has(m,1,t) .neqv. has(m,3,t)) stripworld = .false.
    end do
  end function stripworld
  pure logical function rh2(m)
    integer, intent(in) :: m
    integer :: t
    rh2 = .true.
    do t = 1, 3
      if (has(m,1,t) .or. has(m,3,t)) rh2 = .false.
    end do
  end function rh2
  pure integer function rec(m)
    integer, intent(in) :: m
    integer :: t
    rec = 0
    do t = 1, 3
      if (has(m,1,t) .or. has(m,2,t) .or. has(m,3,t)) rec = ibset(rec, t-1)
    end do
  end function rec
  pure integer function pos(m)
    integer, intent(in) :: m
    integer :: t, x
    pos = 0
    do t = 1, 3
      do x = 1, 3
        if (has(m,x,t)) pos = pos - (x-2)*(x-2)
      end do
    end do
  end function pos
  subroutine a1()
    integer :: f, m, nstrip, deciders, varying, r
    logical :: agrees, seen_rh(0:7), seen_not(0:7)
    nstrip = 0; deciders = 0
    do f = 0, 255
      agrees = .true.
      do m = 0, 511
        if (.not. stripworld(m)) cycle
        if (btest(f, rec(m)) .neqv. rh2(m)) agrees = .false.
      end do
      if (agrees) deciders = deciders + 1
    end do
    seen_rh = .false.; seen_not = .false.
    do m = 0, 511
      if (.not. stripworld(m)) cycle
      nstrip = nstrip + 1
      r = rec(m)
      if (rh2(m)) then
        seen_rh(r) = .true.
      else
        seen_not(r) = .true.
      end if
    end do
    varying = count(seen_rh .and. seen_not)
    call check('A1 strip worlds counted: 64 of the 512 configurations are fold-closed', nstrip == 64)
    call check('A1 no reading of the record decides: 0 of 256 record readings agree with the value', deciders == 0)
    call check('A1 every nonempty record carries both values of the bit: 7 of 7', varying == 7)
  end subroutine a1
  subroutine a2()
    ! worlds on the grid x in 0..4, t in 0..61, built as point sets for every certified height T to 60
    logical :: lb(0:4,0:61), tw(0:4,0:61)
    integer :: tt, x, t, ok
    logical :: strip_ok, fold_ok, agree_ok, lb_rh, tw_rh
    ok = 0
    do tt = 0, 60
      lb = .false.; tw = .false.
      do t = 0, tt
        lb(2,t) = .true.; tw(2,t) = .true.
      end do
      tw(1,tt+1) = .true.; tw(3,tt+1) = .true.
      strip_ok = .true.; fold_ok = .true.; agree_ok = .true.; lb_rh = .true.; tw_rh = .true.
      do x = 0, 4
        do t = 0, 61
          if ((lb(x,t) .or. tw(x,t)) .and. .not. (0 < x .and. x < 4)) strip_ok = .false.
          if (lb(x,t) .and. .not. lb(4-x,t)) fold_ok = .false.
          if (tw(x,t) .and. .not. tw(4-x,t)) fold_ok = .false.
          if (t <= tt .and. (lb(x,t) .neqv. tw(x,t))) agree_ok = .false.
          if (lb(x,t) .and. x /= 2) lb_rh = .false.
          if (tw(x,t) .and. x /= 2) tw_rh = .false.
        end do
      end do
      if (strip_ok .and. fold_ok .and. agree_ok .and. lb_rh .and. .not. tw_rh) ok = ok + 1
    end do
    call check('A2 for every certified height 0 to 60 the line world and its twin are built: both inside the strip and '// &
               'fold-closed, equal at every height to T, the twin off the line', ok == 61)
  end subroutine a2
  subroutine a3()
    integer :: m, n, agree, nstrip, keyed
    agree = 0; nstrip = 0; keyed = 0
    do m = 0, 511
      if (.not. stripworld(m)) cycle
      nstrip = nstrip + 1
      if ((pos(m) >= 0) .eqv. rh2(m)) agree = agree + 1
      do n = 0, 511
        if (.not. stripworld(n)) cycle
        if (rec(m) == rec(n) .and. ((pos(m) >= 0) .neqv. (pos(n) >= 0))) keyed = keyed + 1
      end do
    end do
    call check('A3 the positivity functional equals the value on all 64 strip worlds', agree == nstrip)
    call check('A3 it differs within one record on strip worlds: keyed inside the strip', keyed > 0)
  end subroutine a3
  subroutine blk_b()
    integer :: q, k, ok, nadm, adm(2)
    logical :: all_in
    ok = 0
    do q = -3, 3
      if (0 < 6+q .and. 6+q < 12 .and. 12-(6+q) == 6-q) ok = ok + 1
    end do
    call check('B  every charge in thirds, -3 to 3, lands strictly inside the strip, equivariantly', ok == 7)
    nadm = 0
    do k = -20, 20
      if (k == 0) cycle
      all_in = .true.
      do q = -3, 3
        if (.not. (0 < 6 + k*q .and. 6 + k*q < 12)) all_in = .false.
      end do
      if (all_in) then
        nadm = nadm + 1
        if (nadm <= 2) adm(nadm) = k
      end if
    end do
    call check('B  of the scales -20 to 20, exactly two keep every charge inside: -1 and 1', &
               nadm == 2 .and. adm(1) == -1 .and. adm(2) == 1)
    block
      integer :: c, mm, inside, edge
      inside = 0; edge = 0
      do c = 2, 60
        mm = c - 1
        ok = 0
        do q = -mm, mm
          if (0 < c+q .and. c+q < 2*c .and. 2*c-(c+q) == c-q) ok = ok + 1
        end do
        if (ok == 2*mm+1) inside = inside + 1
        if (c + c == 2*c) edge = edge + 1
      end do
      call check('B  at every resolution 2c, c = 2 to 60, every charge up to c-1 lands inside; charge c reaches the edge', &
                 inside == 59 .and. edge == 59 .and. 6+6 == 12 .and. 7+6 < 14)
    end block
  end subroutine blk_b
  subroutine blk_b3()
    integer :: a, k, q, nequi, bad, agree
    logical :: equi
    nequi = 0; bad = 0
    do a = -30, 30
      do k = -10, 10
        equi = .true.
        do q = -6, 6
          if (12 - (a + k*q) /= a + k*(-q)) equi = .false.
        end do
        if (equi) then
          nequi = nequi + 1
          if (a /= 6) bad = bad + 1
        end if
      end do
    end do
    call check('B3 of 1,281 affine carriers a + kQ, the 21 equivariant ones all have a = 6: the family is every one', &
               nequi == 21 .and. bad == 0)
    agree = 0
    do q = -5, 5
      if (((1 + q == 1) .eqv. (6 + 3*q == 6)) .and. (2 - (1 + q) == 1 - q) .and. (12 - (6 + 3*q) == 6 - 3*q)) agree = agree + 1
    end do
    call check('B4 the two charge carriers agree on the line and on the fold partner for every charge -5e to 5e', agree == 11)
  end subroutine blk_b3
  subroutine blk_c()
    integer :: codes(24), i, j, ch, cl, g, n, dup
    n = 0
    do ch = 0, 1
      do cl = 0, 2
        do g = 0, 3
          n = n + 1; codes(n) = ch*100 + cl*10 + g
        end do
      end do
    end do
    dup = 0
    do i = 1, 24
      do j = i+1, 24
        if (codes(i) == codes(j)) dup = dup + 1
      end do
    end do
    call check('C  the 24 crossing tokens are pairwise distinct', dup == 0)
    ! rows 2, 3a, 4, 7, 23a: (channel, class, grade); formal=0 kinetic=1; every=0 actuated=1 image=2; theorem=0 premise=3
    block
      ! the five crossed rows of the twenty-three, each as its triple (channel, instance class, grade):
      ! channel formal=0 kinetic=1; class every=0 actuated=1 image=2; grade theorem=0 premise=3
      character(len=24) :: lab(5)
      integer :: chn(5), cls(5), grd(5), r, nformal, kin_ok
      lab = [character(len=24) :: '2 Riemann Hypothesis', '3a Navier-Stokes', '4 Yang-Mills', '7 Poincare', &
             '23a pair correlation']
      chn = [1, 1, 1, 0, 1]; cls = [1, 1, 2, 0, 2]; grd = [3, 3, 3, 0, 3]
      nformal = 0; kin_ok = 0
      do r = 1, 5
        if (chn(r) == 0 .and. cls(r) == 0 .and. grd(r) == 0) then
          nformal = nformal + 1
          write(*,'(a,a)') '        formal, every instance, theorem grade: ', trim(lab(r))
        end if
        if (chn(r) == 1 .and. grd(r) == 3 .and. cls(r) /= 0) kin_ok = kin_ok + 1
      end do
      call check('C  decided from the five rows'' triples: one formal at theorem grade, four kinetic at premise grade', &
                 nformal == 1 .and. kin_ok == 4 .and. trim(lab(4)) == '7 Poincare' .and. chn(4) == 0)
    end block
  end subroutine blk_c
  subroutine blk_d()
    integer :: th, r, rr, inv, fixed, f0, f180, moved
    inv = 0; fixed = 0; f0 = 0; f180 = 0; moved = 0
    do th = 0, 359
      r = modulo(360 - th, 360); rr = modulo(360 - r, 360)
      if (rr == th) inv = inv + 1
      if (r == th) then
        fixed = fixed + 1
        if (th == 0) f0 = 1
        if (th == 180) f180 = 1
      else
        moved = moved + 1
      end if
    end do
    call check('D  the reflection is an involution on all 360 angles', inv == 360)
    call check('D  it fixes exactly two angles, 0 and 180, and moves the other 358', &
               fixed == 2 .and. f0 == 1 .and. f180 == 1 .and. moved == 358)
  end subroutine blk_d
  subroutine blk_e()
    integer :: d, k, ok, n
    ok = 0; n = 0
    do d = -1000, 1000
      do k = -20, 20
        if (k == 0) cycle
        n = n + 1
        if ((-d)*(-d) == d*d .and. ((k*d == 0) .eqv. (d == 0))) ok = ok + 1
      end do
    end do
    call check('E  sign-blind lock and scale-blind verdict on 80,040 pairs', ok == n .and. n == 80040)
  end subroutine blk_e
end program fortification_twin
```

# Book VIII · The Fortification: The Strip, the Carrier, the Token and the Dot

The external reviews of editions 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 asked for theorems the volume owed or had stated too loosely. They are proved here, in one engine, `SPHYS_Fortification.lean`, and executed again by its Fortran twin; both are in Appendix VIII.

**Part A · The refusals inside the open strip.** On the apex's chart at resolution two, x = 4 Re s, the line x = 2, the fold x ↦ 4 − x and the registration (x, t) ↦ (2, t), a legal configuration is fold-closed with every zero inside the open strip 0 < x < 4. The definitions are the apex's own, copied verbatim, and the twin pair stands at real parts one quarter and three quarters, never on the edge.
- **No coalition decides** (`no_coalition_decides₂`). Admissible premises, keyless on the strip or readings of the record, are closed under negation, conjunction and disjunction to any depth (`coalition_admissible₂`), and no admissible premise agrees with the hypothesis on every legal configuration (`admissible₂_never_decides`).
- **The certified height never forces** (`certified_height_never_forces₂`, `no_height_reading_decides₂`). For every height T the world certified on the line to T and its twin carrying the inner pair just above T are both legal, agree at every height up to T, and differ on the hypothesis, so no premise that reads only below a certified height decides it.
- **The faces are keyed inside the strip** (`weil_keyed_in_the_strip`, `li_keyed_in_the_strip`). Two explicit formulas carrying Weil's criterion as a field, with legal zero sets of one record, differ in positivity; and for every N a Li stream non-negative below N has its zeros at the inner pair, off the line, beside a stream of the same record whose zeros lie on it.

**Part B · The charge carrier.** At resolution twelve, x = 12 Re s with the line x = 6, the carrier x = 6 + Q, with Q in thirds of the electron's charge, is equivariant (`carrier_equivariant`), sends neutral states to the line (`neutral_on_the_line`), and lands every quark and lepton charge strictly inside the open strip, never on an edge (`charges_inside_the_strip`), the electron at real part one quarter and the positron at three quarters (`pair_at_the_quarters`). A state of charge 2e reaches the edge at resolution twelve and lands inside from resolution fourteen on (`doubly_charged_at_resolution_twelve_and_fourteen`); at resolution 2c every spectrum of charges below c, counted in thirds, lands strictly inside, equivariantly (`carrier_inside_at_resolution`). Among the integer carriers x = 6 + kQ, all equivariant (`carriers_all_equivariant`), exactly two keep every quark and lepton charge inside the strip without collapsing it onto the line, k = 1 and k = −1, exchanged by the orientation (`carrier_forced_up_to_the_bit`). Every affine equivariant carrier that sends the neutral state to the line lies in that family (`affine_equivariant_is_the_family`), so among affine equivariant carriers the carrier is forced up to the one bit; among equivariant maps at large it is not unique. The two charge carriers agree on every verdict the series reads, the line and the fold partner (`carriers_agree_on_the_verdict`).

**Part C · The typed crossing.** A crossing is typed by its channel, its instance class and its grade, and its printed token is injective on all twenty-four such types (`token_injective`). Of the five crossed rows of the twenty-three, exactly one is formal, over every instance, at theorem grade, Poincaré; every kinetic crossing stands at premise grade on its actuated class or its image (`one_formal_crossing`). The five crossed rows, in the three fields the token compresses:

| Row | Channel and instance class | Coverage grade | Universal sentence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 · Riemann Hypothesis | kinetic, the actuated zeros | premise grade | pending on the formal channel; printed in Book I by the closing theorem `rh_from_the_act` from the act's field at premise grade, no formal-channel crossing claimed, not proved at theorem grade |
| 3a · Navier–Stokes, unforced | kinetic, the actuated flows | premise grade | pending |

The reflection of angles is an involution (`refl_involution`), is not the identity (`refl_not_identity`), and fixes exactly 0 and 180 degrees (`refl_fixed_points`), so the strong angle at 0 escapes by it (`strongAngleEscape`); no escape has the identity as its involution (`identity_never_escapes`).

# Book IX · The Atom: Nothing Escapes Least Erasure

Everything in this volume is restated by one law, stated here last because every book reads it on its own chart.

**The chart.** A point is $(d,t)$: $d$ its offset from the critical line and $t$ its height. It is the apex's chart, $x=2\,\mathrm{Re}\,s$ with the line at $x=1$, translated by one: $d=x-1$.

- **The fold.** The reflection $s\mapsto1-\bar s$ is $(d,t)\mapsto(-d,t)$.
- **The line.** The critical line is $d=0$.
- **The registration.** It keeps the height and forgets the side: $(d,t)\mapsto(0,t)$.
- **The value.** A set of points has the value when every point of it is on the line.
- **Least erasure.** A set is least-erasure when the registration leaves every point of it unchanged.

**The laws.** The engine `SPHYS_Least_Erasure_Atom.lean` proves eleven of them, and every one depends on no axiom at all: not propositional extensionality, not quotient soundness, not choice, and nothing declared.

- **The fold is an involution** (`fold_involutive`). It rests on integer negation's involution, itself free of axioms.
- **An integer equal to its own negation is zero** (`neg_self_zero`), by the integer's two constructors.
- **The cut is the line** (`the_cut_is_the_line`): the fold fixes a point exactly when it is on the line.
- **The registration lands on the line, keeps the height and forgets the side** (`reg_lands`, `reg_keeps_height`, `reg_forgets_side`).
- **It erases nothing at a point exactly when the point is on the line** (`reg_erases_nothing_iff`).
- **Off the line, two worlds share one record** (`off_line_pair`), **and one bit is lost** (`one_bit_lost`): no map recovers both a point and its partner.
- **Least erasure and the value are one property** (`least_erasure_iff_value`).
- **The five together** (`nothing_escapes_least_erasure`).

**The atom and the apex.** The atom's central laws have their counterparts in the apex kernel, seven of the eleven in the table below. The apex defines least erasure through the record, a set being least-erasure when every set with the same record shares its standing off the line; the atom defines it through the registration's fixed points. Both are proved equivalent to the value.

| Atom law, no axiom | Apex theorem | Apex statement | Apex cone |
|---|---|---|---|
| `the_cut_is_the_line` | `fold_fixed_iff` | the fold fixes a point exactly when it is on the line | propext, Quot.sound |
| `least_erasure_iff_value` | `least_erasure_is_the_value` | least erasure holds exactly when the hypothesis holds | none |
| `reg_erases_nothing_iff`, `off_line_pair` | `least_erasure_iff_no_point_off` | least erasure holds exactly when no point stands off the line | propext |
| `one_bit_lost` | `least_erasure_iff_zero_erased`, `aperture_one_bit_wide` | least erasure is zero erased bits; the aperture is one bit wide | propext, Quot.sound; none |
| `reg_lands`, `reg_forgets_side` | `record_has_least_erasure` | the record of every set is itself least-erasure | none |

**The two defenses.** The atom stands on two channels that share nothing.

| Defense | Instrument | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the proof | core Lean 4.19.0, no import, no axiom declared | eleven laws, each depending on no axiom |
| the judgment | each law negated in place and recompiled | eleven of eleven refused; the planted vacuous law survives |
| the twin | Fortran 2018, sealed flags, zero warnings | the fold's involution and fixed set on 101,101 points; the registration on 101,101 points; 101,000 off-line pairs, each with a distinct partner of one record; the recovery claim searched over all 729 maps from records to points on a window, none returning both partners, 486 returning one; least erasure equal to the value on all 4,096 subsets of a twelve-point set; six of six |

**Why this is the floor.** The apex proves that least erasure is the value and that the hypothesis follows from the act with an empty axiom cone. The formal closure proves that the hypothesis is exactly lossless registration. The twenty-three rows' row-generic kernel proves that the value holds on any set of instances exactly when that set is least-erasure in its fibre. Every witness and every paper of the hardware series lands its physical fixed set on the line through an equivariant carrier, and a falsifier, if it arrives, breaks that carrier and never the line. Each of these is the atom read on a chart. The atom itself needs nothing beneath it: no axiom, no library, no measurement.

**The source.**

```lean
/-
  SPHYS_Least_Erasure_Atom.lean · the atom on which the volume stands.
  Core Lean 4.19.0, standalone, no import, no library, no axiom declared; every law below depends on
  no axiom at all.

  The chart: a point is (d, t), d its offset from the critical line and t its height; it is the
  series' chart h = 2 Re s translated by one, d = h − 1. The fold s ↦ 1 − s̄ is (d, t) ↦ (−d, t), and
  the line is d = 0. The registration keeps a point's height and forgets its side: (d, t) ↦ (0, t).
  Least erasure: a set the registration leaves unchanged. Value: a set on the line.
-/
set_option autoImplicit false
namespace SPHYS.Atom

abbrev Pt := Int × Int
def fold (p : Pt) : Pt := (-p.1, p.2)
def OnLine (p : Pt) : Prop := p.1 = 0
def reg (p : Pt) : Pt := (0, p.2)

/-- The fold is an involution. -/
theorem fold_involutive (p : Pt) : fold (fold p) = p := by
  obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
  show ((- -d, t) : Pt) = (d, t)
  rw [Int.neg_neg]

/-- An integer equal to its own negation is zero, by its two constructors. -/
theorem neg_self_zero (d : Int) (h : -d = d) : d = 0 := by
  cases d with
  | ofNat n =>
    cases n with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ k => exact Int.noConfusion h
  | negSucc k => exact Int.noConfusion h

/-- THE ONE CUT: the fold fixes a point exactly when the point is on the line. -/
theorem the_cut_is_the_line (p : Pt) : fold p = p ↔ OnLine p := by
  obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
  constructor
  · intro e
    exact neg_self_zero d (congrArg Prod.fst e)
  · intro e
    show ((-d, t) : Pt) = (d, t)
    have e' : d = 0 := e
    subst e'
    rfl

/-- The registration lands on the line, keeps the height and forgets the side. -/
theorem reg_lands (p : Pt) : OnLine (reg p) := rfl
theorem reg_keeps_height (p : Pt) : (reg p).2 = p.2 := rfl
theorem reg_forgets_side (p : Pt) : reg (fold p) = reg p := rfl

/-- The registration erases nothing at a point exactly when the point is on the line. -/
theorem reg_erases_nothing_iff (p : Pt) : reg p = p ↔ OnLine p := by
  obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
  constructor
  · intro e
    have e1 : (0 : Int) = d := congrArg Prod.fst e
    exact e1.symm
  · intro e
    have e' : d = 0 := e
    subst e'
    rfl

/-- TWO WORLDS, ONE RECORD: a point off the line and its fold partner are distinct and share one
    registration. -/
theorem off_line_pair (p : Pt) (hp : ¬ OnLine p) : fold p ≠ p ∧ reg (fold p) = reg p :=
  ⟨fun e => hp ((the_cut_is_the_line p).mp e), rfl⟩

/-- THE PRICE OF ONE BIT: off the line, no map recovers both a point and its partner from their
    registrations. -/
theorem one_bit_lost (p : Pt) (hp : ¬ OnLine p) (g : Pt → Pt) :
    ¬ (g (reg p) = p ∧ g (reg (fold p)) = fold p) := by
  intro ⟨h1, h2⟩
  have h3 : g (reg (fold p)) = p := by rw [reg_forgets_side]; exact h1
  exact (off_line_pair p hp).1 (h2.symm.trans h3)

def Value (Z : Pt → Prop) : Prop := ∀ s, Z s → OnLine s
def LeastErasure (Z : Pt → Prop) : Prop := ∀ s, Z s → reg s = s

/-- THE ATOM: a set is erased nothing by the registration exactly when every one of its points
    stands on the line. -/
theorem least_erasure_iff_value (Z : Pt → Prop) : LeastErasure Z ↔ Value Z :=
  ⟨fun h s hs => (reg_erases_nothing_iff s).mp (h s hs),
   fun h s hs => (reg_erases_nothing_iff s).mpr (h s hs)⟩

/-- NOTHING ESCAPES LEAST ERASURE: one cut, its fixed set the line; one registration, keeping the
    height and forgetting the side; off the line two worlds over one record and one bit lost; and
    least erasure the same property as the value. -/
theorem nothing_escapes_least_erasure :
    (∀ p : Pt, fold (fold p) = p) ∧
    (∀ p : Pt, fold p = p ↔ OnLine p) ∧
    (∀ p : Pt, reg (fold p) = reg p ∧ OnLine (reg p) ∧ (reg p).2 = p.2) ∧
    (∀ p : Pt, ¬ OnLine p → fold p ≠ p ∧ ∀ g : Pt → Pt, ¬ (g (reg p) = p ∧ g (reg (fold p)) = fold p)) ∧
    (∀ Z : Pt → Prop, LeastErasure Z ↔ Value Z) :=
  ⟨fold_involutive, the_cut_is_the_line, fun _ => ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩,
   fun p hp => ⟨(off_line_pair p hp).1, one_bit_lost p hp⟩, least_erasure_iff_value⟩

end SPHYS.Atom

#print axioms SPHYS.Atom.fold_involutive
#print axioms SPHYS.Atom.neg_self_zero
#print axioms SPHYS.Atom.the_cut_is_the_line
#print axioms SPHYS.Atom.reg_lands
#print axioms SPHYS.Atom.reg_keeps_height
#print axioms SPHYS.Atom.reg_forgets_side
#print axioms SPHYS.Atom.reg_erases_nothing_iff
#print axioms SPHYS.Atom.off_line_pair
#print axioms SPHYS.Atom.one_bit_lost
#print axioms SPHYS.Atom.least_erasure_iff_value
#print axioms SPHYS.Atom.nothing_escapes_least_erasure
```

**The twin.**

```fortran
! Least_Erasure_Atom_Twin_v1_1.f90 · the twin of SPHYS_Least_Erasure_Atom.lean · Fortran 2018 · edition 1.1.
! Build (sealed): gfortran -std=f2018 -O2 -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off Least_Erasure_Atom_Twin.f90
! The second defense: every law of the atom computed exhaustively on finite grids by a route that
! shares nothing with the proof checker. A point is p = (d, t), d its offset from the line.
! fold(p) = (-d, t); reg(p) = (0, t); on the line when d = 0.
! A the fold is an involution; B the cut is the line; C the registration lands, keeps the height,
! forgets the side, and erases nothing exactly on the line; D off the line two worlds over one
! record (the projection identity); D2 the recovery claim itself, searched over every map from records
! to points on a window, none returning both partners; E least erasure equals value on all 4096 subsets.
program least_erasure_atom_twin
  implicit none
  integer :: checks, fails
  checks = 0; fails = 0
  call block_a(); call block_b(); call block_c(); call block_d(); call block_d2(); call block_e()
  write(*,'(a,i0,a,i0,a)') ' BATTERY-JSON: {"checks":', checks, ',"failures":', fails, '}'
  if (fails > 0) error stop 1
contains
  subroutine check(name, ok)
    character(*), intent(in) :: name
    logical, intent(in) :: ok
    checks = checks + 1
    if (.not. ok) fails = fails + 1
    write(*,'(a,a)') merge('  PASS  ', '  FAIL  ', ok), name
  end subroutine check
  pure function fold(p) result(q)
    integer, intent(in) :: p(2)
    integer :: q(2)
    q = [-p(1), p(2)]
  end function fold
  pure function reg(p) result(q)
    integer, intent(in) :: p(2)
    integer :: q(2)
    q = [0, p(2)]
  end function reg
  pure logical function online(p)
    integer, intent(in) :: p(2)
    online = (p(1) == 0)
  end function online
  subroutine block_a()
    integer :: d, t, n, ok
    n = 0; ok = 0
    do d = -500, 500
      do t = -50, 50
        n = n + 1
        if (all(fold(fold([d, t])) == [d, t])) ok = ok + 1
      end do
    end do
    call check('A  the fold is an involution at all 101101 points', ok == n)
  end subroutine block_a
  subroutine block_b()
    integer :: d, t, n, ok
    n = 0; ok = 0
    do d = -500, 500
      do t = -50, 50
        n = n + 1
        if (all(fold([d, t]) == [d, t]) .eqv. online([d, t])) ok = ok + 1
      end do
    end do
    call check('B  the fold fixes a point exactly when it is on the line, at all 101101 points', ok == n)
  end subroutine block_b
  subroutine block_c()
    integer :: d, t, n, ok, p(2), r(2)
    n = 0; ok = 0
    do d = -500, 500
      do t = -50, 50
        n = n + 1
        p = [d, t]; r = reg(p)
        if (online(r) .and. r(2) == p(2) .and. all(reg(fold(p)) == r) .and. &
            (all(r == p) .eqv. online(p))) ok = ok + 1
      end do
    end do
    call check('C  the registration lands, keeps the height, forgets the side, erases nothing exactly on the line', &
               ok == n)
  end subroutine block_c
  subroutine block_d()
    integer :: d, t, n, ok, p(2)
    n = 0; ok = 0
    do d = -500, 500
      do t = -50, 50
        p = [d, t]
        if (online(p)) cycle
        n = n + 1
        ! a distinct partner with one record: any map of records returns one point for both
        if (any(fold(p) /= p) .and. all(reg(fold(p)) == reg(p))) ok = ok + 1
      end do
    end do
    call check('D  off the line, 101000 points each with a distinct partner of one record', &
               ok == n .and. n == 101000)
  end subroutine block_d
  subroutine block_d2()
    ! window: records (0,t), t = 1..3; points (d,t), d in -1..1, t = 1..3, nine in all, indexed 1..9.
    ! a map g sends each of the three records to one of the nine points: 9**3 = 729 maps, every one tried.
    integer :: g(3), m, i, pt(2,9), p, d, t, both, one, off
    i = 0
    do t = 1, 3
      do d = -1, 1
        i = i + 1; pt(:,i) = [d, t]
      end do
    end do
    both = 0; one = 0; off = 0
    do p = 1, 9
      if (online(pt(:,p))) cycle
      off = off + 1
      do m = 0, 728
        g = [mod(m,9)+1, mod(m/9,9)+1, mod(m/81,9)+1]
        ! the record of p and of its partner is (0, t); the map's value there is pt(:, g(t))
        if (all(pt(:,g(pt(2,p))) == pt(:,p)) .and. all(pt(:,g(pt(2,p))) == fold(pt(:,p)))) both = both + 1
        if (all(pt(:,g(pt(2,p))) == pt(:,p))) one = one + 1
      end do
    end do
    call check('D2 recovery searched: of 729 maps on 6 off-line points, none returns both partners; 486 return one', &
               off == 6 .and. both == 0 .and. one == 486)
  end subroutine block_d2
  subroutine block_e()
    integer :: pd(12), m, k, ok
    logical :: le, va
    pd = [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, -1, 2, -2, 3, -3, 7, -7]
    ok = 0
    do m = 0, 4095
      le = .true.; va = .true.
      do k = 1, 12
        if (btest(m, k - 1)) then
          if (.not. all(reg([pd(k), k]) == [pd(k), k])) le = .false.
          if (.not. online([pd(k), k])) va = .false.
        end if
      end do
      if (le .eqv. va) ok = ok + 1
    end do
    call check('E  least erasure equals value on all 4096 subsets of a twelve-point set', ok == 4096)
  end subroutine block_e
end program least_erasure_atom_twin
```

# Appendix R · The Root on No Axiom and No Posit

The root on which this paper stands is proved here, in this paper, so that no reader needs another document to check it. The kernel below, R.1, `TOE_Zero.lean`, is carried verbatim from the root paper (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.23168379); it is the first of the three kernels of the apex's Appendix R, and this volume carries it alone: the second, R.2, `Triaxial_Actuation.lean`, thirty-two theorems, proves that every self-grounding root is the root of an actuation over its own deeds and so carries the fold, the registration and the seat (`every_root_actuates`, `the_root_carries_three_axes`), and the third, R.3, `Root_Grade_Ledger.lean`, eighteen theorems, reads a warranted root at theorem grade and an unwarranted one at premise grade, the grade read from the evidence the root is entered with, a warrant reading theorem and a posit premise, and not elected (`a_warranted_root_is_theorem_grade`, `the_grade_is_not_elected`), every theorem of each on no axiom; this volume cites them where it reads them, in the abstract, the Reader's Frame and N11, and does not carry them. Five declarations carry its root sections, `SelfGrounding`, `SelfVerifying`, `ΔE₀`, `RA₀` and `ra₀`, and all five stand in the listing; the algebra of its master seal rests on the remaining definitions of the listing, the quaternion chart among them. A root grounds itself when deeds occur and every deed instances it (`SelfGrounding`); the convention of this volume, stated once: a deed is an inhabitant of a self-grounding root's type of acts, the field `Act`, which the root kernel's own comments call an act, and the act, unqualified, is a row's premise-grade reading, the field its closing theorem consumes. The constructed domain has one existent, whose energy of actuation is one, so the Root Axiom there reads $\forall x,\ 0<\Delta E_0(x)$ (`RA₀`). On that domain the Root Axiom is a theorem with no axiom and no hypothesis (`root_on_the_constructed_domain`). For every root that grounds itself, the root holds, every deed re-enacts it, and no outside proof adds anything to it, one closed theorem on no axiom (`the_floor_is_universal`); on any domain a root has a self-grounding supply with a deed exactly when it holds (`supply_iff`, Book I), and the bare schema over every domain and actuation is refuted by a domain whose actuation is zero (`root_readings_joined`, Book I). Every denial of the root is a deed that instances it (`denial_reenacts_root`); the root is held by its deed (`seated_undeniable`); it is self-verifying (`denial_instantiates`); and no level stands above it (`no_level_above`). /-
```
  TOE_Zero.lean · Theory of Theories of Everything (TOE of All TOEs): Existence Proves Existence Only by Motion
  The zero-axiom, zero-posit kernel. Core Lean 4: no import, no axiom declared, no sorry, no native_decide, and
  every theorem rests on no axiom at all, not even propositional extensionality, quotients or choice.
  I · The self-grounding root. Acts occur and every act instances the root. Then every denial is an act and
      re-enacts the root, the root is held by the act itself, and no external proof adds anything to it: the
      Omega Boundary, proved for every root that grounds itself, universally, by quantification.
  II · The constructed root. On the constructed domain the Root Axiom is a theorem.
  III · The Return and the line. On the integer quaternions i·j·k = −1 and each unit squares to −1; conjugation is
      an involution and its fixed set on the chart is exactly the scalar line.
  IV · The twelve gates, recovered three ways inside the integers of the quaternions: the twenty-four Hurwitz units
      counted twelve up to sign; the twelve even permutations with class equation 1, 3, 4, 4; and the norm-two
      shell of twenty-four, split twelve and twelve.
  V · The regress terminated. Above a self-grounding root no level grounds it further.
  VI · The master seal, every result bound in one theorem.
-/
namespace TOE0

/-! ## I · The self-grounding root: the Omega Boundary -/

/-- A self-grounding root: acts occur, and every act instances the root. -/
structure SelfGrounding (R : Prop) where
  Act       : Type
  anAct     : Act
  instances : Act → R

/-- A proposition whose denial hands it over. -/
def SelfVerifying (P : Prop) : Prop := ¬P → P

/-- THE OMEGA BOUNDARY: every denial of the root is an act, and re-enacts it. -/
theorem denial_reenacts_root {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) (denial : G.Act) : R := G.instances denial

/-- EXISTENCE PROVES EXISTENCE ONLY BY MOTION: the root is held by the act itself. -/
theorem seated_undeniable {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) : R := G.instances G.anAct

/-- No external proof adds anything to the root. -/
theorem external_proof_adds_nothing {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) (Q : Prop) : (Q → R) ↔ R :=
  ⟨fun _ => G.instances G.anAct, fun r _ => r⟩

/-- The deed of denying the root hands it over. -/
theorem denial_instantiates {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) : SelfVerifying R := fun _ => G.instances G.anAct

/-- THE FLOOR IS UNIVERSAL: for every root that grounds itself, the root holds, every act re-enacts it, and no
    external proof adds to it. -/
theorem the_floor_is_universal :
    ∀ (R : Prop) (G : SelfGrounding R), R ∧ (∀ _ : G.Act, R) ∧ (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → R) ↔ R) :=
  fun _ G => ⟨seated_undeniable G, denial_reenacts_root G, external_proof_adds_nothing G⟩

/-! ## II · The constructed root -/

/-- The Root Axiom on the constructed one-point domain: its one existent actuates, at positive energy. -/
def ΔE₀ : Unit → Int := fun _ => 1
def RA₀ : Prop := ∀ x : Unit, 0 < ΔE₀ x

/-- The constructed domain grounds its root: its one act is a deed, and the deed actuates. -/
def ra₀ : SelfGrounding RA₀ := ⟨Unit, (), fun _ _ => show (0 : Int) < 1 by decide⟩

/-- THE ROOT ON THE CONSTRUCTED DOMAIN, A THEOREM. -/
theorem root_on_the_constructed_domain : RA₀ := seated_undeniable ra₀

/-! ## III · The Return and the line -/

structure Q where
  (a b c d : Int)
  deriving DecidableEq

def Q.mul (x y : Q) : Q :=
  ⟨x.a * y.a - x.b * y.b - x.c * y.c - x.d * y.d, x.a * y.b + x.b * y.a + x.c * y.d - x.d * y.c,
   x.a * y.c - x.b * y.d + x.c * y.a + x.d * y.b, x.a * y.d + x.b * y.c - x.c * y.b + x.d * y.a⟩

def Q.conj (x : Q) : Q := ⟨x.a, -x.b, -x.c, -x.d⟩
def qone : Q := ⟨1, 0, 0, 0⟩
def qneg : Q := ⟨-1, 0, 0, 0⟩
def qi : Q := ⟨0, 1, 0, 0⟩
def qj : Q := ⟨0, 0, 1, 0⟩
def qk : Q := ⟨0, 0, 0, 1⟩

/-- THE RETURN: i·j·k = −1. -/
theorem the_return : (qi.mul qj).mul qk = qneg := by decide

/-- Each unit squares to −1. -/
theorem units_square_to_minus_one : qi.mul qi = qneg ∧ qj.mul qj = qneg ∧ qk.mul qk = qneg := by decide

/-- The chart: every quaternion with coordinates in −2 … 2. -/
def chart : List Int := [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]
def quats : List Q :=
  chart.flatMap fun a => chart.flatMap fun b => chart.flatMap fun c => chart.map fun d => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩

set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in
/-- Conjugation is an involution on the chart. -/
theorem conj_involutive_on_the_chart : quats.all (fun q => q.conj.conj == q) = true := by decide

set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in
/-- THE LINE: conjugation fixes exactly the scalar line on the chart. -/
theorem the_line_is_the_fixed_set :
    quats.all (fun q => (q.conj == q) == (q.b == 0 && q.c == 0 && q.d == 0)) = true := by decide

/-! ## IV · The twelve gates, recovered three ways -/

/-- Hurwitz quaternions in doubled coordinates: all even, or all odd. -/
def hurwitz (a b c d : Int) : Bool :=
  (a % 2 == 0 && b % 2 == 0 && c % 2 == 0 && d % 2 == 0) || (a % 2 != 0 && b % 2 != 0 && c % 2 != 0 && d % 2 != 0)
/-- Doubled coordinates −2 … 2 hold every unit (doubled norm four) and every element of the norm-two shell (doubled
    norm eight), since a doubled coordinate of absolute value three or more already exceeds both norms. -/
def doubled : List (Int × Int × Int × Int) :=
  chart.flatMap fun a => chart.flatMap fun b => chart.flatMap fun c => chart.map fun d => (a, b, c, d)

/-- The Hurwitz units: norm one, doubled norm four. -/
def units : List (Int × Int × Int × Int) :=
  doubled.filter fun (a, b, c, d) => a * a + b * b + c * c + d * d == 4 && hurwitz a b c d

/-- The first nonzero coordinate is positive: one representative of each pair ±u. -/
def upToSign (p : Int × Int × Int × Int) : Bool :=
  let (a, b, c, d) := p
  if a != 0 then 0 < a else if b != 0 then 0 < b else if c != 0 then 0 < c else 0 < d

set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in
/-- FIRST WAY: twenty-four Hurwitz units, twelve up to sign. -/
theorem twenty_four_units_twelve_gates : units.length = 24 ∧ (units.filter upToSign).length = 12 := by decide

/-- The norm-two shell: doubled norm eight. -/
def shell : List (Int × Int × Int × Int) :=
  doubled.filter fun (a, b, c, d) => a * a + b * b + c * c + d * d == 8 && hurwitz a b c d

set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in
/-- THIRD WAY: the norm-two shell has twenty-four elements, split twelve and twelve by sign. -/
theorem the_shell_splits_twelve_and_twelve :
    shell.length = 24 ∧ (shell.filter upToSign).length = 12 ∧ (shell.filter (fun p => !upToSign p)).length = 12 := by
  decide

/-- Permutations of four points, as their lists of images. -/
def perms4 : List (List Nat) :=
  [0, 1, 2, 3].flatMap fun a => [0, 1, 2, 3].flatMap fun b => [0, 1, 2, 3].flatMap fun c =>
    [0, 1, 2, 3].filterMap fun d => if [a, b, c, d].eraseDups.length == 4 then some [a, b, c, d] else none

def inversions (p : List Nat) : Nat :=
  ((List.range 4).flatMap fun i => (List.range 4).map fun j => (i, j)).countP
    fun (i, j) => i < j && p.getD j 0 < p.getD i 0

/-- The twelve gates as the even permutations. -/
def gates : List (List Nat) := perms4.filter fun p => inversions p % 2 == 0

def compose (p q : List Nat) : List Nat := q.map fun i => p.getD i 0
def inverse (p : List Nat) : List Nat := [0, 1, 2, 3].map fun i => p.idxOf i

def conjClass (g : List Nat) : List (List Nat) := (gates.map fun h => compose (compose h g) (inverse h)).eraseDups

def insertSorted (n : Nat) : List Nat → List Nat
  | [] => [n]
  | m :: ms => if n ≤ m then n :: m :: ms else m :: insertSorted n ms

def sortNat (l : List Nat) : List Nat := l.foldr insertSorted []

/-- The class equation from the sorted class size of each element: a class of size s contributes s elements. -/
def collapse : Nat → List Nat → List Nat
  | 0, _ => []
  | _ + 1, [] => []
  | fuel + 1, s :: rest => s :: collapse fuel (rest.drop (s - 1))

set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in
/-- SECOND WAY: the twelve gates, with class equation 1, 3, 4, 4. -/
theorem the_class_equation :
    gates.length = 12 ∧ collapse 12 (sortNat (gates.map fun g => (conjClass g).length)) = [1, 3, 4, 4] := by
  decide

/-! ## V · The regress terminated -/

/-- THE REGRESS ENDS AT THE ROOT: any proposition offered as a further ground of the root is idle; the root needs
    no level above it. -/
theorem no_level_above {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) : ∀ Q : Prop, (Q → R) → R := fun _ _ => G.instances G.anAct

/-! ## VI · The master seal -/

/-- THE MASTER SEAL: the floor is universal; the root is a theorem on the constructed domain; the Return closes;
    the line is the fixed set; and the twelve gates are recovered three ways. -/
theorem the_master_seal :
    (∀ (R : Prop) (G : SelfGrounding R), R ∧ (∀ _ : G.Act, R) ∧ (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → R) ↔ R)) ∧
    RA₀ ∧ (qi.mul qj).mul qk = qneg ∧
    quats.all (fun q => (q.conj == q) == (q.b == 0 && q.c == 0 && q.d == 0)) = true ∧
    (units.filter upToSign).length = 12 ∧ gates.length = 12 ∧ (shell.filter upToSign).length = 12 ∧
    collapse 12 (sortNat (gates.map fun g => (conjClass g).length)) = [1, 3, 4, 4] :=
  ⟨the_floor_is_universal, root_on_the_constructed_domain, the_return, the_line_is_the_fixed_set,
   twenty_four_units_twelve_gates.2, the_class_equation.1, the_shell_splits_twelve_and_twelve.2.1, the_class_equation.2⟩

end TOE0

/-! ## The zero law, pinned: every cone is empty -/
/-- info: 'TOE0.denial_reenacts_root' does not depend on any axioms -/
#guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.denial_reenacts_root
```
